questions.stem: Sol Studio in St. John’s is hired by a clinic to "make something digital" to cut long waiting times. Which pre-production step should the team complete FIRST?
options: Draw a storyboard of the main screens
Define the problem, purpose and goal of the product
Build a Gantt chart for the production schedule
Test a clickable prototype with patients
questions.explain: Key: B. Problem definition comes first: until the team knows exactly what challenge it is solving and for whom, every later step is guesswork. The Gantt chart is tempting because planning feels like an early step, but you cannot schedule tasks for a product that has not yet been defined.

questions.stem: Malik is framing a shot of a cruise ship in Scarborough harbour for a Tobago cruise port promo. Which framing BEST applies the rule of thirds?
options: Place the ship on one of the four points where lines dividing the frame into thirds, horizontally and vertically, intersect
Zoom in until the ship fills the whole frame
Place the horizon along the very bottom edge of the frame
Place the ship exactly in the centre of the frame
questions.explain: Key: A. The rule of thirds divides the frame with two horizontal and two vertical lines and places the point of interest on a line or an intersection, which feels more dynamic than central framing. Centring the ship is tempting because it looks "balanced", but that is symmetrical composition, not the rule of thirds.

questions.stem: On the traditional red, yellow, blue (RYB) colour wheel, which pair of colours is COMPLEMENTARY?
questions.explain: Key: D. Complementary colours sit directly opposite each other on the colour wheel; blue is opposite orange. Blue and green is tempting because the colours look good together, but they sit next to each other, which makes them analogous, not complementary.

questions.stem: In the PayRite utility app, after a user taps "Pay bill", the button turns into a spinner and then shows a green tick with "Payment received". Which principle of interactive design is MOST clearly applied?
questions.explain: Key: D. Feedback means the system tells users what has happened as a result of their action, here the spinner and confirmation message. Consistency is tempting, but it is about using the same layouts, icons and behaviours across screens, not about responding to a specific action.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes a key motivation for producing indigenous Caribbean digital products such as local animations, games and apps?
options: To tell Caribbean stories in authentic local voices and preserve cultural identity in a media space dominated by imported content
To avoid having to follow copyright law
To guarantee lower production costs than imported content
To make content that only Caribbean audiences can access
questions.explain: Key: A. Indigenous products are motivated by representation, authenticity and cultural preservation, giving Caribbean people content that reflects their lives. Lower cost is tempting, but local production is often more expensive per viewer than buying imported content, so cost is not the defining motivation.

questions.stem: Island Pulse Media rents servers, storage and computing power from Amazon Web Services to host its clients' websites. Which type of digital platform is Amazon Web Services in this case?
questions.explain: Key: D. Infrastructure platforms provide the underlying computing resources (servers, storage, networking) that other services are built on. Marketplace is tempting because Amazon also runs a shopping site, but here the company is renting computing resources, not buying goods from sellers.

questions.stem: Maya needs a version of the Island Pulse logo with sharp edges and a fully transparent background to place over photos on a website. Which file format is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: C. PNG uses lossless compression and supports full alpha transparency, so edges stay crisp and the background can be see-through. GIF is tempting because it also supports transparency, but it is limited to 256 colours and only on or off transparency, which gives jagged edges over photos.

questions.stem: Keisha has recorded a podcast episode about Carnival and must keep a master copy for further editing with NO loss of quality. Which audio format should she save the master in?
questions.explain: Key: D. WAV is an uncompressed format, so it keeps every detail of the recording and is ideal as an editing master. MP3 is tempting because it is the usual format for podcasts, but it is lossy: each export discards data, so it is the right format for distribution, not for the master.

questions.stem: In three-point lighting, which light is placed BEHIND the subject to separate them from the background?
questions.explain: Key: A. The back light shines from behind the subject, creating a thin outline of light that lifts them off the background. The fill light is tempting because it is also a supporting light, but it sits in front, opposite the key light, to soften shadows on the face.

questions.stem: In Malik's 2D bouncing ball exercise, the ball flattens when it hits the ground and becomes longer and thinner as it falls fast. Which principle of animation is he applying?
questions.explain: Key: C. Squash and stretch changes an object's shape to show weight, impact and speed while keeping its volume. Anticipation is tempting because it is also a core principle, but it is a preparatory movement before an action (such as crouching before a jump), not the deformation on impact.

questions.stem: In a 3D polygon mesh created in Blender, what is a VERTEX?
options: A complete 3D object made of many polygons
A single point in 3D space where edges meet
A straight line joining two points
A flat surface enclosed by edges
questions.explain: Key: B. A vertex is the most basic element of a mesh: one point with X, Y and Z coordinates. The straight line option is tempting because vertices and edges are closely linked, but a line between two vertices is an edge, and a flat surface enclosed by edges is a face.

questions.stem: Maya and a freelance designer in Guyana are editing the same Figma file when an internet outage in Roseau stops Maya's work for three hours. Which DISADVANTAGE of digital collaboration does this illustrate?
questions.explain: Key: A. Cloud collaboration tools only work when every member has a stable connection, so outages halt progress. Lack of version control is tempting because work time was lost, but Figma keeps version history; the problem here is access, not tracking changes.

questions.stem: To launch a juice bar on Broad Street, Keisha paints chalk footprints along the pavement leading to the shop, ending at a QR code for a free sample. The cost is very low and the idea is unusual. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: C. Guerrilla marketing uses unconventional, low-cost, high-impact ideas in public spaces to surprise people. Cross-platform marketing is tempting because the QR code links to a digital channel, but cross-platform marketing means keeping one consistent message across several channels, which is not the focus here.

questions.stem: A design trend that uses frosted, semi-transparent panels with a blurred background showing through is known as
questions.explain: Key: C. Glassmorphism imitates frosted glass: translucent layers with background blur and subtle borders. Neumorphism is tempting because the names are similar, but it uses soft inner and outer shadows to make elements look pressed into or pushed out of the background, not see-through.

questions.stem: Lolo Run game team raises US$4,000 online from about 300 supporters, each giving a small amount in return for rewards such as early access. Which source of funding is this?
questions.explain: Key: B. Crowdfunding raises money from many people, each contributing a small amount, usually through a platform such as Kickstarter or GoFundMe. Sponsorship is tempting because supporters receive something back, but sponsorship normally involves one organisation paying in exchange for brand exposure.

questions.stem: Which e-book format is REFLOWABLE, meaning the text adjusts to fit the screen size and the reader's chosen font size?
questions.explain: Key: B. ePub (electronic publication) is the open standard for reflowable e-books, so text rewraps on phones, tablets and e-readers. PDF is tempting because it is widely used for digital documents, but it is a fixed-layout format: pages look the same everywhere, which makes small screens hard to read.

questions.stem: Which network, funded by the United States Department of Defense and first connected in 1969, is regarded as the forerunner of the internet?
questions.explain: Key: D. ARPANET linked research computers using packet switching and is the ancestor of today's internet. The World Wide Web is tempting, but it came about twenty years later (Tim Berners-Lee, 1989 to 1991) and is a system of linked pages that runs on top of the internet.

questions.stem: Keisha finds a photo of San Pedro Beach licensed CC BY-NC. In which situation may she use it?
options: Only after buying the full copyright from the photographer
In a paid hotel advertisement, with credit given to the photographer
In any project, without giving credit
In a school blog post, with credit given to the photographer
questions.explain: Key: D. BY means attribution is required and NC means non-commercial use only, so a credited school blog post is allowed. The paid hotel advert is tempting because credit is given, but advertising is commercial use, which the NC condition forbids.

questions.stem: At the start of a website project for a Portsmouth restaurant, what is the MAIN advantage of a low-fidelity paper prototype over a high-fidelity Figma prototype?
options: It can be clicked through like the real website
It is quick and cheap to change, so the team gets feedback on structure and layout before investing time in detail
It can be handed straight to a developer as finished code
It shows the final colours, fonts and images exactly
questions.explain: Key: B. Low-fidelity prototypes are rough by design: they let you test ideas and layout early, when changes cost almost nothing. Being clickable is tempting, but that is a feature of high-fidelity digital prototypes, not paper sketches.

questions.stem: Maya draws a diagram showing every page of the KIN Carnival Village website, with the home page at the top and branches to Events, Food, Tickets and Contact. This diagram is a
questions.explain: Key: C. A site map shows all the pages of a website and how they are organised and linked, usually as a hierarchy from the home page. A concept map is tempting because it also uses boxes and lines, but it links ideas with labelled relationships, not pages of a site.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for web-appropriate content?
options: Using long, detailed paragraphs with technical jargon to show expertise
questions.explain: Key: A. The syllabus asks for short paragraphs, direct address, no needless repetition, no jargon and scannable text, because online readers skim. Addressing users directly might seem informal, but it is an explicit criterion: "you" language keeps web readers engaged.

questions.stem: Apart from helping visually impaired users with screen readers, the alt text on an image ALSO supports
options: faster page loading, because alt text compresses the image
machine indexability, because search engines read alt text to understand the image
higher image resolution on large screens
questions.explain: Key: C. Search engines cannot "see" images, so they rely on alt text to index them, which improves SEO. Faster loading is tempting, but alt text does not change the image file at all; only resizing and compression reduce load time.

questions.stem: Jerome recorded a voice-over in a room with a humming air conditioner. In Audacity, what is the FIRST step of the Noise Reduction process?
options: Select a few seconds containing only the background hum and choose Get Noise Profile
Export the track as MP3 to remove the noise
Apply a fade-in to the start of the track
Select the whole track and apply Amplify
questions.explain: Key: A. Audacity must first learn what the noise sounds like from a section with no speech; only then do you select the whole track and apply the reduction. Amplify is tempting, but it makes the voice AND the hum louder, so the problem gets worse, not better.

questions.stem:
What does the attribute target="_blank" do in this HTML?
<a href="https://www.cxc.org" target="_blank">CXC</a>
options: It makes the link text bold
It opens the linked page in a new browser tab or window
It turns the link into an internal anchor link
It downloads the linked page as a file
questions.explain: Key: B. target="_blank" tells the browser to open the destination in a new tab, so the user keeps your page open. The anchor link option is tempting, but internal anchor links use href="#id" to jump within a page and have nothing to do with the target attribute.

questions.stem: In the CSS box model, which order correctly lists the layers from the INSIDE of an element outwards?
questions.explain: Key: B. Content sits in the centre, padding is the space inside the border, then the border, then the margin outside it that separates the element from its neighbours. Margin, border, padding, content is tempting because it is the correct order reversed, but the question asks from the inside outwards.

questions.stem:
Look at this CSS rule:
.special { color: teal; }
Which elements will it style?
options: Only the first element on the page
questions.explain: Key: A. A full stop before a name makes a class selector, which applies to every element carrying that class. The id option is tempting, but an id selector starts with a hash (#special) and targets one unique element.

questions.stem: A student checks whether a blog post about Hurricane Irma recovery was written by a qualified, identifiable author or organisation. Which evaluation criterion is she applying?
questions.explain: Key: A. Authority asks who created the content and whether they are qualified and credible. Accuracy is tempting because the two are linked, but accuracy is about whether the facts themselves are correct and can be verified, not who wrote them.

questions.stem: Sunset Tours company builds its entire audience on one social media platform. When the platform changes its algorithm, the reach of its posts falls by half overnight. Which LIMITATION of online platforms does this illustrate?
options: Platform dependency and lack of control over algorithms
questions.explain: Key: C. When a business relies on one platform, the platform's rules and algorithms decide who sees its content, and it can change them at any time. Weak analytics is tempting because the company notices the drop through its statistics, but the cause is the algorithm change, not poor data.

questions.stem: Port Pulse tourism board wants ONE content store to feed its website, its mobile app and the digital screens at NMIA arrivals. Which type of CMS is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. A headless CMS separates content (the "body") from presentation (the "head") and delivers it through an API to any channel. A mobile content CMS is tempting, but it is designed around mobile delivery only, while the board needs web, app and airport screens fed from one source.

questions.stem: A website that can be installed on a phone's home screen, sends notifications and works offline, without going through an app store, is called a
questions.explain: Key: D. A PWA is a website built with modern web technologies so it behaves like an app: installable, offline-capable and able to send notifications. Native app is tempting, but native apps are written for a specific OS and are normally installed through an app store.

questions.stem: In the mobile ecosystem, what is the MAIN role of carriers such as Digicel, Flow and Flow?
options: Providing the network infrastructure and data connectivity that link devices to content and services
Designing the operating systems that run on phones
Reviewing and approving apps for the app stores
Writing the apps that users download
questions.explain: Key: A. Carriers (telcos) build and run the mobile networks, selling voice and data services so that devices can reach content. Designing operating systems is tempting because carriers sell phones, but operating systems are made by platform companies such as Google (Android) and Apple (iOS).

questions.stem: Which statement BEST explains the INTERDEPENDENCE of players in the mobile ecosystem?
options: Developers need users and good connectivity for their apps to succeed, while carriers and device makers need useful apps to drive demand for data and devices
Only carriers matter, because without them no other player exists
Each player works independently, so a change in one part has no effect on the others
Users depend on developers, but developers do not depend on users
questions.explain: Key: A. Interdependence means each component relies on the others: content drives demand for devices and data, while infrastructure and users make content worthwhile. The carriers option is tempting because networks are essential, but devices, content and users are equally necessary; no single player stands alone.

questions.stem: Jerome must test the BusSXM Android app on many phone brands, screen sizes and OS versions. Which characteristic of Android causes this extra testing?
options: The fact that Android runs only on Google Pixel phones
Its closed ecosystem, controlled entirely by one company
The requirement to write all Android apps in Swift
Fragmentation, because many manufacturers ship different devices running different Android versions
questions.explain: Key: D. Because Android is open-source and used by many manufacturers, the market is fragmented across devices and versions, so apps must be tested widely. A closed ecosystem is tempting, but that describes iOS, where Apple controls a small range of hardware, which actually reduces testing.

questions.stem: Smart water meters in a Caribbean town automatically send readings to the utility company over the network, with no person reading them. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: D. IoT describes everyday physical objects with sensors and network connections that collect and exchange data automatically. Cross-platform development is tempting because the data may reach different systems, but that term refers to building one app that runs on several operating systems.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes the content consumption versus content production imbalance in the Caribbean mobile ecosystem?
options: Caribbean mobile users do not consume digital content
Caribbean users produce more content than they consume
Caribbean users consume far more mobile content made outside the region than they produce locally
Content produced in the Caribbean cannot be shared on global platforms
questions.explain: Key: C. The region is a heavy consumer of imported apps, streaming and social content, while local production is comparatively small, so most value and cultural influence flows from abroad. The final option is tempting because local creators face challenges, but global platforms are open to Caribbean creators; the gap is in volume, not access.

questions.stem: Why are submarine fibre-optic cables critical to small island states such as Barbados?
options: They carry most international internet traffic, so damage to them can cut or slow connectivity for the whole island
They supply electricity to mobile phone towers
They are used only for landline telephone calls
Satellites carry most traffic, so cables are only a backup
questions.explain: Key: A. Most international data travels on undersea cables, so islands depend on them for fast, affordable internet; redundancy (more than one cable) improves resilience. The satellite option is tempting because satellites are used in emergencies, but they carry only a small share of traffic and usually with higher latency.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an ECONOMIC benefit of developing mobile apps locally in the Caribbean?
options: Preserving local languages such as Papiamentu
Sharing local history with young people
Creating local jobs and keeping app revenue within the region
questions.explain: Key: D. Economic benefits include jobs, entrepreneurship, export potential and keeping income in local hands. Preserving Papiamentu is tempting because it is a real benefit, but it is a cultural benefit, not an economic one; the command word asks you to classify the benefit correctly.

questions.stem: The FarmLink app will be used by farmers in rural Dominica where mobile data is slow and expensive. Which design strategy BEST addresses this?
options: Compress images, cache content for offline use and keep the app lightweight
Require a constant internet connection for every feature
Autoplay high-definition tutorial videos on the home screen
Add a large animated splash screen to build the brand
questions.explain: Key: A. Designing for low bandwidth means reducing data use and allowing offline access, so the app works on weak signals and saves users money. The animated splash screen is tempting because branding matters, but it adds file size and loading time, which hurts users on slow connections.

questions.stem: Fishers in Grenada will use a weather app on open boats in bright sunlight, often with wet hands. Which design decision BEST responds to this physical environment?
options: Many small icons packed onto one screen
High-contrast colours, large text and large touch targets
Long text forms that require typing
A dark, low-contrast theme with thin fonts
questions.explain: Key: B. Bright light washes out low-contrast screens, and wet hands make small targets hard to hit, so strong contrast and big buttons improve usability. Dark mode is tempting because it can reduce glare at night, but low contrast and thin fonts are very hard to read in direct sunlight.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes a WIREFRAME in mobile app development?
options: A marketing video showing the app's main features
A fully interactive version of the app used to test user flows
The finished code of the app ready for the app store
A basic skeletal layout showing where interface elements will be placed, without final colours or images
questions.explain: Key: D. A wireframe is a blueprint of the screen layout: boxes and placeholders for buttons, text and images. The interactive version is tempting because wireframes can be linked later, but a clickable, interactive model is a prototype, which comes after wireframing.

questions.stem: To build a NATIVE iOS app, which official development environment and programming language are used?
options: MIT App Inventor and code blocks
questions.explain: Key: B. Apple's official IDE is Xcode, and Swift is Apple's modern language for iOS apps. Android Studio and Kotlin is tempting because it is also an official native pairing, but it is for Android, not iOS.

questions.stem: Before launch, Jerome gives a beta of the BusSLU app to 20 regular riders on the Castries to Gros Islet route to confirm it meets their real needs. This is
questions.explain: Key: D. UAT is carried out by real target users to confirm the app does what they need before release. Unit testing is tempting because it is also testing, but it is done by developers on small individual pieces of code, not by end users.

questions.stem: App Store Optimisation (ASO) is BEST described as
options: paying influencers to post about an app on TikTok
improving an app's title, keywords, description, screenshots and ratings so it ranks higher in app store searches
improving a website's ranking in Google search results
sending a press release to app review websites
questions.explain: Key: B. ASO focuses on the app store listing itself so the app is found and downloaded more. Improving Google rankings is tempting because ASO is often called "SEO for apps", but SEO targets websites in search engines, while ASO targets app store search.

questions.stem: Bim Eats app is free to download and lets everyone browse menus and reviews, but users pay to unlock premium features such as booking tables with no fees. Which revenue model is this?
questions.explain: Key: C. Freemium gives the core app away free and charges for premium features. Subscription is tempting because premium users may pay regularly, but the defining feature here is a free core with paid upgrades; a pure subscription model charges for access itself on a recurring basis.

questions.stem: An app that combines messaging, payments, ride-hailing and food delivery in one platform, such as WeChat or Grab, is known as a
questions.explain: Key: D. Super apps consolidate many digital services inside one app, so users rarely need to leave it. Cross-platform app is tempting, but that term describes an app built to run on more than one operating system, not one that bundles many services.

questions.stem: Zara must show a client when scripting, filming, editing and review will happen across six weeks, including which tasks overlap and the key milestones. Which planning tool is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. A Gantt chart uses horizontal bars on a timeline to show each task's start, duration, overlaps and milestones. A storyboard is tempting because it is a pre-production document, but it plans the visual sequence of shots, not the schedule.

questions.stem: Why should a team test a prototype with target users BEFORE full production of a digital media product?
options: To replace the need for a written project proposal
To find problems and confirm that the idea meets users' needs while changes are still cheap to make
To produce the final export files for distribution
To secure copyright protection for the idea
questions.explain: Key: B. Idea validation tests a concept with real users early, so weaknesses are fixed before money and time are spent on the finished product. Copyright protection is tempting because it also protects work, but copyright is automatic once work is fixed; testing has nothing to do with it.

questions.stem: Serenity Spa in Gros Islet wants a calm palette of blue, blue-green and green for its website. Which colour harmony is this?
questions.explain: Key: A. Analogous colours sit next to each other on the colour wheel, giving a calm, unified look. Split-complementary is tempting because it also uses three colours, but it pairs one base colour with the two colours on either side of its complement, which creates far more contrast.

questions.stem: A designer adds black to a pure red to create a deep maroon for a Carnival band costume graphic. The maroon is a
questions.explain: Key: D. A shade is a hue mixed with black, which darkens it. Tone is tempting because it also reduces brightness, but a tone is a hue mixed with grey, and a tint is a hue mixed with white.

questions.stem: Every screen of the Carnival Pass app places the back arrow in the top left corner and uses the same icon style and colours. Which principle of interactive design is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. Consistency means using the same layout, controls and visual language throughout, so users do not have to relearn the interface. Predictability is tempting because consistent design helps users predict, but predictability is about users correctly anticipating what an action will do, not about repeated placement and style.

questions.stem: Free tools such as Canva, GIMP and Blender allow a student in Belize to create professional-looking designs without buying expensive software licences. Which TWO driving factors are MOST clearly shown?
questions.explain: Key: D. The tools cost nothing (affordability) and give individuals the power to create and compete (empowerment). Pervasiveness and adoption is tempting because the tools are popular, but the scenario stresses cost and personal capability, not how widespread the technology is.

questions.stem: When critiquing the AUTHENTICITY of a Caribbean animated series, which question is MOST useful?
options: Do the characters, settings, music and dialogue reflect real Caribbean experiences, and were people from that culture involved in making it?
How many episodes were produced in the first season?
Is each episode longer than imported cartoons?
Was the most expensive animation software used?
questions.explain: Key: A. Authenticity is about genuine cultural representation and whether the culture is portrayed from the inside rather than as a stereotype. The software question is tempting because production quality affects impact, but expensive tools do not make content more culturally authentic.

questions.stem: Keisha wants a small looping animation of a waving Guyana flag to play inside an email newsletter, which cannot play video. Which format is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. GIF supports simple frame animation and loops automatically, and it displays in almost all email software. MP4 is tempting because it gives better quality and smaller files, but most email clients will not play embedded video, so the animation would not appear.

questions.stem: Malik saves the same JPEG photo of Fort George many times, and blocky artefacts start to appear. Why does this happen?
options: JPEG uses lossy compression, discarding some image data every time the file is re-saved
JPEG stores only 1-bit colour, so detail is lost
JPEG is a vector format that cannot store photographs
JPEG uses lossless compression, which adds extra pixels on each save
questions.explain: Key: A. Lossy compression throws away data the eye is less likely to notice, and each re-save compresses again, so the loss builds up over time. The lossless option is tempting because it sounds technical, but lossless formats such as PNG keep all data, which is exactly why they do not degrade.

questions.stem: Malik is filming an interview on windy Trellis Bay beach in Tortola, beside the airport, with planes passing overhead. Which choice will BEST capture a clear voice?
options: Turn the recording level to maximum
Record with no microphone and add subtitles later
Rely on the camera's built-in microphone from three metres away
Clip a lavalier microphone close to the speaker's mouth and fit a foam or furry windscreen
questions.explain: Key: D. A lavalier sits close to the mouth, so the voice is much louder than the background, and a windscreen blocks wind rumble. Turning the level to maximum is tempting, but it raises the wind and plane noise too and can cause clipping and distortion.

questions.stem: Before a cartoon character leaps over a puddle, she bends her knees and swings her arms back. Which principle of animation is this?
questions.explain: Key: A. Anticipation is a preparatory movement that signals to the audience that an action is about to happen. Follow through is tempting because it also deals with movement around an action, but it happens AFTER the main action, when parts such as hair or clothes keep moving.

questions.stem: In Adobe Animate, Malik sets the ball's position at frame 1 and frame 24, and the software automatically creates the frames in between. This process is called
questions.explain: Key: D. Tweening (from "in-betweening") is when software calculates the intermediate frames between two keyframes. Onion skinning is tempting because it is also used when animating between keys, but it only shows faded previous and next frames for reference; it does not generate frames.

questions.stem: Which action shows good NETIQUETTE when working on a shared Google Doc for a group SBA?
options: Deleting sections you disagree with before the group meets
Typing comments in all capital letters so they stand out
Sharing the document link publicly without asking the group
Using suggestion mode and comments to propose changes instead of deleting a teammate's work
questions.explain: Key: D. Netiquette means respectful, professional conduct online; suggestions and comments let teammates see and discuss changes. Capital letters is tempting because it seems to add emphasis, but online it reads as shouting and is considered rude.

questions.stem: Keisha runs an Instagram campaign for a cashew jam brand and wants to know whether it is ENGAGING the audience. Which metric is MOST suitable?
options: The cost of the camera used for the photos
Engagement rate (likes, comments, shares and saves relative to reach)
The number of followers Keisha has on her personal account
The number of posts the team published
questions.explain: Key: B. Engagement rate measures how people interact with the content compared with how many saw it, which is a key performance indicator for social campaigns. The number of posts is tempting because it is easy to count, but it measures effort, not audience response.

questions.stem: Which section of a project proposal gives a brief overview of the WHOLE project, so busy funders can quickly decide whether to read further?
questions.explain: Key: C. The executive summary comes first and condenses the problem, solution, costs and outcomes into a short overview. The problem statement is tempting because it also appears early, but it explains only the need the project addresses, not the whole plan.

questions.stem: An author publishes her novel set in San Pedro as an e-book on Kobo and Google Play Books, and also as a paperback. She learns that each format needs its own unique 13-digit identifier. This identifier is the
questions.explain: Key: B. The International Standard Book Number uniquely identifies each edition and format of a book, so e-book and paperback get different ISBNs. Metadata is tempting because it also describes the book, but metadata is a set of descriptive fields (title, author, keywords), not one unique number.

questions.stem: Which stage of the web is MOST associated with user-generated content, social networking and two-way interaction?
questions.explain: Key: C. Web 2.0 turned users from readers into contributors through blogs, wikis, social media and video sharing. Web 3.0 is tempting because it is the newest, but it is associated with decentralisation, blockchain and the semantic web rather than the rise of social media.

questions.stem: Writing a podcast script differs from writing a blog post MAINLY because
options: a podcast script must include headings and hyperlinks
listeners cannot scan back, so the script needs conversational language, short sentences, signposting and repetition of key points
a podcast script must always be longer than a blog post
a podcast script relies on alt text for accessibility
questions.explain: Key: B. Audio is linear: listeners hear each word once, so writers signpost ("first", "next") and repeat key ideas. Headings and hyperlinks is tempting because they help readers, but they are techniques for scannable text on a screen, not for the ear.

questions.stem: Which of these actions is PLAGIARISM?
options: Using an image released under a CC0 public domain dedication
Linking to an article so readers can read it on the original site
Copying paragraphs from a newspaper article into your blog and presenting them as your own words
Quoting a short passage from an article and naming the source
questions.explain: Key: C. Plagiarism is presenting someone else's work or ideas as your own without credit. Quoting a short passage is tempting because it uses another person's words, but attribution makes it legitimate quotation, not plagiarism.

questions.stem: Keisha draws a diagram with "Carnival" in the centre, linked by labelled phrases such as "includes" to J'ouvert, the Parade and the Village, and "features" to soca and calypso. This is a
questions.explain: Key: A. A concept map links ideas using labelled connecting phrases to show relationships. A hierarchy map is tempting because both use connected boxes, but a hierarchy map shows levels of pages or content from top to bottom, not labelled relationships between ideas.

questions.stem: Which document is used BEFORE writing begins to define the target group, the tone of voice and a checklist of content to include?
questions.explain: Key: D. A creative brief sets out the purpose, audience, tone and content requirements so everyone works to the same plan. A site map is tempting because it is also a planning document, but it maps the structure of pages, not the audience and voice of the content.

questions.stem: For a product photo of a nutmeg bottle, Malik wants the bottle sharp and the background softly blurred. Which camera setting BEST achieves this shallow depth of field?
options: A narrow aperture, such as f/16
A very fast shutter speed with no other change
A wide aperture, such as f/1.8
questions.explain: Key: D. A wide aperture (low f-number) produces a shallow depth of field, isolating the subject from the background. f/16 is tempting because a bigger number sounds stronger, but a narrow aperture keeps more of the scene in focus, which is the opposite of what Malik wants.

questions.stem: On a tours website, the line "Home > Tours > Pigeon Island" near the top of the page is an example of
questions.explain: Key: D. Breadcrumbs show where the user is in the site's hierarchy and let them jump back to higher levels. A hamburger menu is tempting because it is also a navigation feature, but it is a hidden menu opened from a three-line icon, not a location trail.

questions.stem:
What will this HTML display in a browser?
<ol><li>Rice</li><li>Peas</li></ol>
options: A numbered list with two items
A bulleted list with two items
questions.explain: Key: B. <ol> creates an ordered list, which browsers number by default, and each <li> is a list item. A bulleted list is tempting, but that is produced by <ul> (unordered list).

questions.stem:
Look at this CSS rule:
#menu { background-color: navy; }
Which element(s) will it style?
options: Every nav element on the page
questions.explain: Key: A. The hash symbol makes an id selector, which targets the single element carrying that id. The class option is tempting, but class selectors begin with a full stop (.menu) and can style many elements.

questions.stem: Why do web designers often set font sizes in rem rather than fixed px values?
options: rem is required to set image dpi
rem sizes scale relative to the root font size, so text respects users' browser settings and supports accessibility
rem is used only for printed pages
rem sizes look exactly the same on every device regardless of settings
questions.explain: Key: B. One rem equals the root (html) font size, so if a user enlarges their default text, the whole layout scales with it. The "exactly the same" option is tempting, but that describes fixed pixel sizing, which ignores user preferences.

questions.stem: A free quiz app about Caribbean history asks for access to users' contacts and location, although it does not need them. Which evaluation criterion is MOST relevant?
questions.explain: Key: C. Unnecessary permissions put users' personal data at risk, so this is a privacy and security concern. Accuracy is tempting because the app is about history, but the issue here is how the app treats user data, not whether its facts are correct.

questions.stem: When writing a Wikipedia article about Emancipation Day in Barbados, which standard must contributors follow?
options: Their personal opinions about the celebration
Original research that has not been published elsewhere
A neutral point of view, supported by reliable, verifiable sources
Promotional language encouraging people to attend events
questions.explain: Key: C. Wikipedia requires neutrality and citations to reliable published sources, because articles are written collaboratively for a global audience. Original research is tempting because it sounds valuable, but Wikipedia does not accept unpublished findings that readers cannot verify.

questions.stem: Which sequence shows a typical content WORKFLOW in a content management system?
questions.explain: Key: A. Content is drafted, checked by an editor, formally approved, published and eventually archived when out of date. Create, publish, approve, review is tempting because it starts correctly, but publishing before review and approval risks putting errors live.

questions.stem: The rise of subscription newsletters (for example on Substack) helps writers MAINLY by
options: giving them a direct relationship with readers and recurring income that does not depend on social media algorithms
providing free hosting for large video files
removing the need to write regularly
guaranteeing that every newsletter goes viral
questions.explain: Key: A. Newsletters land directly in readers' inboxes and paid subscriptions give predictable income, reducing reliance on platforms. Going viral is tempting because newsletters can be shared, but nothing guarantees viral reach; the strength of newsletters is loyal, direct audiences.

questions.stem: A national telecommunications regulator that sets policy, allocates spectrum and licenses carriers is part of which component of the mobile ecosystem?
questions.explain: Key: C. The enabling environment includes policy, regulation, regulators and developer support that shape how the ecosystem operates. Infrastructure is tempting because spectrum is used by networks, but the regulator does not build networks; it sets the rules that carriers follow.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes iOS compared with Android?
options: Apps can be published with no review process
It runs on Samsung and Huawei phones as well as iPhones
Its source code is open, so any manufacturer can install it on their phones
Apple controls the hardware, the operating system and App Store review, giving tight security and a consistent design, but less customisation
questions.explain: Key: D. iOS is a closed ecosystem: Apple makes the devices and the OS and reviews every app. The open source option is tempting, but it describes Android, whose open-source base allows many manufacturers to use it.

questions.stem: HarmonyOS is a mobile operating system alongside Android and iOS. It was developed by
questions.explain: Key: B. HarmonyOS is Huawei's operating system for phones, wearables and smart devices. Samsung is tempting because it is also a major device maker, but Samsung phones mainly run Android (with Samsung's One UI on top).

questions.stem: The start-up Island Bites has ONE small team and a tight deadline, but needs its app on both Android and iOS. Which approach is MOST suitable?
options: Publish the menu as a PDF instead of an app
Release on iOS only and ignore Android users
Use a cross-platform tool such as Flutter or React Native to build both versions from one codebase
Build two separate native apps in Xcode and Android Studio
questions.explain: Key: C. Cross-platform tools let one team write one codebase for both platforms, saving time and money. Two native apps is tempting because native apps can perform best, but it doubles the work, which a small team with a tight deadline cannot afford.

questions.stem: How does mobile technology MOST strengthen the connection between Caribbean islands and their diaspora?
options: It removes the need for international submarine cables
It makes international travel unnecessary for all business
Messaging, video calls, remittance apps and streaming of local radio let families abroad stay in touch and send money home
It stops people from migrating abroad
questions.explain: Key: C. Mobile tools keep diaspora communities emotionally, culturally and economically linked to home, including through remittances. Removing cables is tempting because connectivity matters, but mobile services actually depend on submarine cables to carry international traffic.

questions.stem: Which is a key reason why 5G rollout may be slower in small islands and rural Caribbean areas than in large cities abroad?
options: 5G phones cannot be sold in the Caribbean
5G technology is banned throughout the region
Caribbean users have no demand for mobile data
High infrastructure costs compared with small populations make the return on investment lower for carriers
questions.explain: Key: D. Building towers and fibre backhaul is expensive, and small markets mean fewer paying customers per tower, so carriers roll out more slowly. No demand is tempting as a simple explanation, but mobile data demand in the region is high; the barrier is economics, not interest.

questions.stem: An app that teaches Kwéyòl phrases and folk stories to young people in St. Lucia MAINLY provides which benefit?
questions.explain: Key: B. Apps about language, history and stories help preserve culture and connect generations. Export revenue is tempting because any app might earn money, but the main purpose here is cultural, not economic.

questions.stem: Why might a locally built bus app serve Trinidad and Tobago riders better than a global maps app?
options: Global apps are always more expensive to download
Global maps apps cannot run on smartphones in the Caribbean
Local developers can include informal stops, local landmarks and route knowledge that global datasets often miss
Local apps never need internet access
questions.explain: Key: C. Locally relevant apps reflect how services really work in the community, such as buses that stop at landmarks rather than fixed timetabled stops. The cost option is tempting, but major global maps apps are free; their weakness is missing local detail, not price.

questions.stem: Users complain that the TrackFit app drains their battery because it checks GPS location every second, even in the background. Which factor and fix BEST match?
options: Screen size: increase the font size
Device performance and battery life: reduce location update frequency and limit background tasks
User profile: translate the app into Dutch
questions.explain: Key: B. Constant GPS polling uses processing power and drains the battery, so updating less often and pausing background work fixes it. Compressing images is tempting because it improves performance in general, but it saves data, not GPS-related battery use.

questions.stem: MIT App Inventor allows beginners to build Android apps by
options: snapping together visual code blocks in a web browser
designing in Blender and exporting to the Play Store
typing commands into a terminal only
questions.explain: Key: B. MIT App Inventor is a no-code, low-code tool: logic is built from drag-and-drop blocks, and the interface is designed in the browser. Swift in Xcode is tempting because it is a real app development route, but it is professional coding for iOS, not block-based building.

questions.stem: Which sequence shows the correct order for developing a mobile app?
questions.explain: Key: C. You first define the purpose and users, sketch layouts, create a clickable model, then code and test. Wireframe, build, conceptualise is tempting because wireframing is early, but you cannot sketch screens before deciding what the app is for.

questions.stem: In the app user journey, a person reading star ratings and comments before deciding to install an app is at which stage?
questions.explain: Key: A. The journey runs discover, test, review, purchase, download and retain; reading others' ratings and comments is the review stage. Discover is tempting because the person is still deciding, but discovery is when they first become aware of the app.

questions.stem: A mobile game gives players three extra lives if they choose to watch a 30-second advert. Which revenue model is this?
questions.explain: Key: A. Rewarded video ads are optional and give users something in return for watching. Interstitial ads are tempting because they are also full-screen, but they appear automatically between screens, and the user gets no reward.

questions.stem: The ReadyBVI hurricane app is free, shows no adverts and is funded by a government grant and a local NGO. Which category of app is this?
options: A civic, social good app funded by grants and sponsorship
questions.explain: Key: B. Civic and charity apps serve the public good, such as disaster preparedness, and are funded by grants, sponsors or donations rather than users. Freemium is tempting because the app is free, but freemium relies on selling premium features, which ReadyBVI does not do.

questions.stem: An app made in Sint Maarten is used by residents of the French side, Saint-Martin, which is part of the European Union. Which regulation MOST affects how it collects and stores their personal data?
questions.explain: Key: A. GDPR governs how personal data of people in the EU is collected, stored and used, requiring clear consent and data protection. WCAG is tempting because it is also a standard that apps should follow, but it covers accessibility, not data privacy.

questions.stem: Zara asks the team to take an existing tourist map and ask: what can we Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate or Reverse? Which brainstorming technique is this?
questions.explain: Key: C. SCAMPER is a checklist of seven prompts used to generate new ideas from an existing product. Mind mapping is tempting because it is also a brainstorming technique, but it branches ideas out from a central topic rather than applying set prompts to a product.

questions.stem: For a Carnival campaign, Keisha collects photos, colour swatches, fabric textures and font samples on one board to set the overall visual feel. This is a
questions.explain: Key: C. A mood board is an inspirational collage that communicates the look and feel of a project early in planning. A style guide is tempting because it also deals with colours and fonts, but it sets fixed rules (exact colour codes, logo use, type sizes) once the design is decided.

questions.stem: A poster for the Island Rhythm festival uses orange, green and violet, three colours spaced evenly around the colour wheel. Which colour harmony is this?
questions.explain: Key: B. A triadic scheme uses three colours equally spaced (about 120 degrees apart) on the wheel. Tetradic is tempting because it is also an evenly spaced scheme, but it uses four colours, forming two complementary pairs.

questions.stem: A designer divides a poster of Fort Charlotte into a large square and a smaller rectangle, then repeats the division to form a spiral, placing the fort where the spiral tightens. Which rule of composition is she using?
options: The golden ratio (golden rectangle), approximately 1 to 1.618
Symmetrical balance around a central axis
The rule of thirds, dividing the frame into nine equal parts
questions.explain: Key: A. The golden rectangle has sides in the ratio of about 1 to 1.618; repeatedly cutting off squares produces the golden spiral, and the point of interest sits where it tightens. The rule of thirds is tempting because it also guides subject placement, but it uses a simple grid of equal thirds, not a ratio-based spiral.

questions.stem: Maya is choosing text and background colours for a long article on the Island Pulse website. Which combination will give the BEST legibility on screen?
options: Light grey text on a white background
Yellow text on a white background
Dark navy text on an off-white background
Red text on a green background
questions.explain: Key: C. Strong value contrast (dark against light) makes text easy to read for long periods and for users with low vision. Red on green is tempting because they are complementary colours with high hue contrast, but they have similar values, vibrate on screen and are hard to separate for people with colour blindness.

questions.stem: In the DOM Tours app, the "Book now" button is pale grey on a light grey background, and testers do not notice it. Which principle of interactive design has been ignored?
questions.explain: Key: A. Perceivability means users must be able to see, hear or otherwise notice interface elements; a low-contrast button fails this. Learnability is tempting because users struggle, but learnability is about how quickly users understand how to use something once they find it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of POLICY support for local Caribbean digital creators?
options: A government offering tax incentives or grants for local film and animation production
A viewer leaving a positive comment on a local game
A creator buying a new camera with personal savings
Fans sharing a local creator's video with friends
questions.explain: Key: A. Policy support comes from governments and institutions through laws, incentives, quotas or funding programmes. Fans sharing videos is tempting because it genuinely helps creators, but it is community support, not policy.

questions.stem: Maya wants a YouTube video of the Carnival parade to play inside the school website WITHOUT uploading the large video file to the website's server. What is the BEST method?
options: Take a screenshot of the video and post the image
Download the MP4 and email it to every visitor
Convert the video into a GIF and upload that instead
Paste YouTube's embed code (an iframe) into the web page
questions.explain: Key: D. Embedding displays content hosted elsewhere inside your page, so YouTube streams the video and your server stores nothing. Converting to GIF is tempting because GIFs move, but a long video as a GIF would be a huge file with no sound and poor quality.

questions.stem: Malik is exporting a short promo for Instagram Reels and TikTok, which display full-screen vertical video on phones. Which aspect ratio should he choose?
questions.explain: Key: B. 9:16 is vertical video that fills a phone screen held upright, which suits Reels and TikTok. 16:9 is tempting because it is the standard for YouTube and television, but it is horizontal, so it would appear small with large empty bars on a vertical feed.

questions.stem: In Blender's Graph Editor, the curve for a ball's movement is flat at the start and end and steep in the middle. What does this show?
options: Squash and stretch: the ball changes shape
Anticipation: the ball moves backwards first
Ease in and ease out (slow in and slow out): the ball starts slowly, speeds up, then slows down
Linear motion: the ball moves at the same speed throughout
questions.explain: Key: C. A flat section means little change in value per frame (slow), and a steep section means rapid change (fast), which is the principle of slow in and slow out. Linear motion is tempting, but a linear interpolation would be a straight diagonal line with no flattening at the ends.

questions.stem: An animator first draws the key poses of a dance move, then goes back to fill in the drawings between them. Which approach is this?
questions.explain: Key: A. Pose-to-pose plans the important key poses first and adds in-betweens afterwards, giving control over timing. Straight-ahead action is tempting because it is the other main method, but there the animator draws each frame in order from start to finish without planned key poses.

questions.stem: A group member accidentally deletes a section of the shared SBA report in Google Docs. Which feature of cloud collaboration tools will BEST let the group recover it?
questions.explain: Key: C. Version history stores earlier versions of a file, so the group can restore the deleted section. Real-time chat is tempting because it helps the team communicate about the problem, but it cannot bring back lost text.

questions.stem: Sol Studio campaign uses the same slogan, colours and hashtag on TikTok, Instagram, its email newsletter and posters at Douglas–Charles Airport. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: C. Cross-platform marketing keeps one consistent message and identity across many channels so the brand is recognised everywhere. Viral marketing is tempting because a hashtag can spread, but viral marketing is about designing content that people share widely on their own.

questions.stem: Zara wants to see which visual and interactive design styles leading designers are publishing this month. Which research tools are MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. Behance and Dribbble are showcases where designers publish current work, so they reveal emerging styles directly. Google Trends is tempting because it tracks trends, but it shows search interest over time, not examples of design work.

questions.stem: A wealthy Barbadian businessperson invests her own money in a student animation start-up in exchange for a share of ownership and offers mentoring. This source of funding is
questions.explain: Key: A. An angel investor is an individual who invests personal funds in an early-stage venture in return for equity, often adding advice. Sponsorship is tempting because money comes from one source, but sponsors pay for brand exposure, not a share of the company.

questions.stem: Why is a Massively Multiplayer Online Game (MMOG) considered a form of digital publishing?
options: It can only be played offline on one computer
It must be printed and sold in shops before it can be played
Its content, such as worlds, events and expansions, is distributed and updated online to very large audiences at the same time
It is always published as an ePub file
questions.explain: Key: C. Publishing means making content available to an audience; MMOGs publish and continually update shared online worlds for thousands of players. The ePub option is tempting because ePub is a digital publishing format, but it is for e-books, not games.

questions.stem: The title, author, description, keywords and categories an author enters on Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing so readers can find her book are called
questions.explain: Key: C. Metadata is data about data: descriptive information that helps stores and search engines classify and surface the book. ISBN is tempting because it is also entered during publishing, but it is a single unique identifying number, not the descriptive fields.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes the internet from the World Wide Web?
options: The internet is the global network of connected computers; the World Wide Web is a system of linked web pages accessed over it
They are two names for exactly the same thing
The World Wide Web is the cables and routers that carry data
The World Wide Web was created before the internet
questions.explain: Key: A. The internet is the infrastructure; the Web, created by Tim Berners-Lee around 1989 to 1991, is one service that runs on it, alongside email and others. "The same thing" is tempting because people use the words interchangeably, but in an exam you must distinguish them.

questions.stem: Under copyright law, which of the following is protected AUTOMATICALLY as soon as it is created and fixed in a form?
options: An original song recorded by a Trinidadian soca artist
An idea for a story that has not been written down
questions.explain: Key: B. Copyright protects original creative works once they are fixed (recorded, written, saved); no registration is needed. The story idea is tempting because it is original, but copyright protects the expression of ideas, not ideas themselves.

questions.stem: Which pair of content management systems are BOTH open-source?
questions.explain: Key: A. WordPress, Drupal and Joomla are open-source: their code is free to use, modify and self-host. Wix and Joomla is tempting because Joomla is open-source, but Wix is proprietary, owned and hosted by one company.

questions.stem: Maya's wireframe for a tours website makes the main heading largest, the "Book a tour" button bold and prominent, and the small print smallest. Which design principle guides the user's eye from most to least important?
questions.explain: Key: B. Visual hierarchy uses size, weight, colour and position to show the order of importance. Proximity is tempting because it is also a layout principle, but it is about grouping related items close together, not ranking their importance.

questions.stem: Optimising a restaurant's web content for VOICE SEARCH mainly means
options: removing all text and using only images
using natural, question-style phrases with short, clear answers, such as "Where can I buy johnny cakes in Kingston?"
repeating the same keyword as many times as possible
questions.explain: Key: B. People speak to voice assistants in full questions, so content that mirrors natural speech and gives concise answers ranks better. Keyword repetition is tempting because keywords matter for SEO, but "keyword stuffing" is penalised by search engines and sounds unnatural.

questions.stem: Which licence allows anyone to use, change and sell a photo with NO conditions at all, not even giving credit?
questions.explain: Key: D. CC0 waives all rights, placing the work as close to the public domain as possible. CC BY is tempting because it is very open, but it still requires attribution to the creator.

questions.stem: The hero image for the Coral Cove Marina website is 6000 by 4000 pixels and 12 MB. What is the BEST way to prepare it for the web?
options: Resize it to the display width (about 1920 pixels), compress it as a web JPEG or WebP, and add alt text
Convert it to an uncompressed BMP file
Save it as a full-size PNG to avoid any loss of quality
Upload the original file so it looks as sharp as possible
questions.explain: Key: A. Web images should match their display size and be compressed, so pages load quickly on mobile data; alt text adds accessibility and SEO. A full-size PNG is tempting because it is lossless, but for a large photograph it would produce an even bigger file and a slow page.

questions.stem: In a podcast about Belize food, Keisha wants background music to sit quietly under her voice. What is the BEST technique?
options: Speed up the music so it finishes sooner
Put the music on a separate track and lower its volume (gain) under the speech
Normalise the music to full volume
Mix the music and voice onto the same track before editing
questions.explain: Key: B. Working with multiple tracks lets you adjust each element independently; lowering music under speech (ducking) keeps the voice clear. Mixing everything onto one track is tempting because it seems simpler, but then you can no longer change the music level without affecting the voice.

questions.stem:
What happens if the image in this HTML fails to load?
<img src="san-pedro.jpg" alt="Plane landing over San Pedro beach">
options: The text "Plane landing over San Pedro beach" is shown in its place, and screen readers read it aloud
The page refuses to load at all
A link to San Pedro beach opens in a new tab
The browser downloads san-pedro.jpg from Google instead
questions.explain: Key: A. The alt attribute provides alternative text for when the image cannot be displayed and for screen reader users. The new tab option is tempting because the tag contains text, but <img> displays an image; only an <a> tag creates a link.

questions.stem:
What does this CSS rule do?
a:hover { color: orange; }
options: It makes every link orange at all times
It turns links orange only after they are clicked and released
It changes a link's text colour to orange while the mouse pointer is over it
It makes all visited links orange permanently
questions.explain: Key: C. :hover is a pseudo-class that applies a style only while the pointer rests on the element, giving visual feedback. The visited option is tempting because it is also a link state, but visited links are styled with a:visited.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a DOMAIN NAME from web HOSTING?
options: A domain name stores the website's images and videos
Hosting is the address users type; the domain is the server
They are the same service with two names
A domain name is the address users type to find a site; hosting is the server space that stores the site's files
questions.explain: Key: D. In website infrastructure, the domain (for example islandpulse.sx) points to the hosting server where files live. Swapping the two is tempting because they are usually bought together, but the domain is the address and the host is the storage.

questions.stem: During a tropical storm watch, a student compares a viral social media post about wind speeds with the official bulletin from the national meteorological service. Which evaluation criterion is she applying?
questions.explain: Key: B. Checking facts against a reliable, official source tests accuracy. Audience engagement is tempting because the post is viral, but high engagement says nothing about whether the information is correct.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN advantage of a self-hosted WordPress.org site over a free hosted blog on WordPress.com or Blogger?
options: It needs no maintenance or updates
Full control over themes, plugins, data, monetisation and your own domain
Security is handled entirely by the platform
It costs nothing at all to run
questions.explain: Key: B. Self-hosting gives you ownership and freedom to customise and earn as you choose. "Costs nothing" is tempting because WordPress software is free, but you must pay for hosting and a domain, and you also take on maintenance and security yourself.

questions.stem: In the mobile ecosystem, apps, music, news, videos and games are examples of which component?
questions.explain: Key: C. Content is what users consume and create through their devices, and it drives demand across the ecosystem. Infrastructure is tempting because content travels over networks, but infrastructure refers to towers, cables and data centres, not the material itself.

questions.stem: The StormWatch alert app fails to reach many elderly residents because their older phones cannot install it. Which relationship in the mobile ecosystem does this BEST illustrate?
options: Carriers decide which apps users are allowed to install
Content has no connection to the devices users own
Regulators design the apps that users download
Device capability limits which content users can access, so developers must design for the devices people actually own
questions.explain: Key: D. This shows interdependence: content is only useful if it runs on users' devices, so developers must consider older hardware and OS versions. The carriers option is tempting because carriers sell phones, but here the barrier is the phone's capability, not the network provider.

questions.stem: Jerome is designing a smartwatch app for runners on the Palisadoes road in Kingston. Which design consideration is MOST important for this wearable device?
options: Use the same detailed layout as the tablet version
Show short, glanceable information with minimal input because the screen is very small
Rely on a full on-screen keyboard for all controls
Include long forms for runners to type their notes
questions.explain: Key: B. Wearables have tiny screens and are used on the move, so information must be readable at a glance with very few taps. Reusing the tablet layout is tempting because it saves design time, but it would be unreadable and unusable on a watch face.

questions.stem: Using 5G networks with edge computing improves augmented reality apps MAINLY by
options: making every smartphone cheaper to buy
removing the need for any internet connection
processing data closer to the user, reducing latency so digital overlays respond almost instantly
questions.explain: Key: D. Edge computing moves processing from distant data centres to servers near the user, and with 5G this cuts delay, which AR needs to feel real. Removing the need for internet is tempting, but edge computing still depends on the network; it just shortens the distance data travels.

questions.stem: A student needs reliable statistics on mobile internet use across the Caribbean for her SBA report. Which source is MOST appropriate?
options: A star rating in the app store
A recent ITU or GSMA report
questions.explain: Key: B. The ITU (International Telecommunication Union) and GSMA publish researched, regularly updated data on mobile and internet use. The travel blog is tempting because it may mention phone use in the islands, but it is personal opinion, not authoritative statistics.

questions.stem: Why are SMS text alerts still valuable in disaster management, even where smartphones are common?
options: SMS messages can carry high-definition video
SMS works on basic phones and often gets through on weak or congested networks when mobile data fails
SMS alerts work even when the phone is switched off
SMS uses satellites and needs no carrier network
questions.explain: Key: B. During hurricanes such as Irma, data networks may be overloaded or damaged, but short SMS messages need very little bandwidth and reach any handset. The satellite option is tempting because it sounds resilient, but standard SMS runs on the carrier's mobile network.

questions.stem: A Trinidad and Tobago app for managing steelpan band bookings is later licensed to bands in Miami and London. Which benefit of local app development does this MOST clearly show?
options: Export potential, earning income from outside the region
Reduced data usage for local users
Cultural preservation within Trinidad and Tobago
questions.explain: Key: A. Selling or licensing a Caribbean-made product abroad is export: it brings foreign income and shows regional entrepreneurship. Cultural preservation is tempting because steelpan is a cultural art form, but the scenario focuses on selling the app overseas, which is an economic benefit.

questions.stem: The AgriHelp app is for older farmers in rural Guyana, many with limited literacy and digital skills. Which design approach BEST suits this user profile?
options: Clear icons, voice prompts, simple language and large buttons
Small buttons to fit more features on screen
Dense text menus with many options on each screen
questions.explain: Key: A. Designing for the user profile means matching the app to users' age, literacy, skills and language. Fitting more features on screen is tempting because it seems to add value, but crowded small buttons confuse users with limited digital skills.

questions.stem: Adding text labels to icons so that a screen reader can announce "Search" and "Menu" to a blind user is an example of designing for
questions.explain: Key: D. Accessibility ensures people with disabilities can use the app, and screen readers need text labels on icons to work. Portability is tempting because phones are used on the go, but portability is about using the device while moving, not about disability access.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN purpose of a clickable Figma prototype in mobile app development?
options: To improve the app's ranking in app store searches
To test user flows and navigation with real users before investing time in coding
To serve as the final app submitted to the app store
To automatically generate Kotlin code for the app
questions.explain: Key: B. Clickable prototypes simulate the app's screens and links so problems in the user flow are found early. Submitting it to the app store is tempting because it looks realistic, but a prototype has no working code or data behind it.

questions.stem: Which is the official integrated development environment (IDE) for building native Android apps, and which language does Google recommend?
questions.explain: Key: D. Android Studio is Google's official IDE, and Kotlin is its preferred language (Java is still supported). Thunkable is tempting because it can build Android apps, but it is a no-code, low-code builder, not the official native IDE.

questions.stem: Jerome's app crashes with an error message he does not understand. Which resources are MOST appropriate for solving it?
options: Stack Overflow and the official Android developer documentation
questions.explain: Key: A. Online developer communities and official documentation explain errors and show tested solutions. Google Trends and Sensor Tower are tempting because they are research tools, but they track search and app market trends, not coding problems.

questions.stem: A hospital in Barbados wants an internal app for its staff only, NOT available to the public. Which distribution model is MOST suitable?
options: Direct download from a public website
questions.explain: Key: C. Enterprise distribution delivers apps privately to an organisation's own devices and staff. Direct download is tempting because it avoids the app store, but a public website download could be accessed by anyone, which the hospital does not want.

questions.stem: The developer Kezia builds one food ordering app and sells customised versions, each with its own name and branding, to restaurants in Barbados, St. Kitts and Antigua. Which revenue model is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. A white-label app is built once and licensed to clients who rebrand it as their own. Subscription is tempting because restaurants may pay yearly, but the defining feature is reselling one rebrandable product to many businesses.

questions.stem: Open-source and non-profit services such as the Signal messaging app and Wikipedia are funded MAINLY through
questions.explain: Key: C. Community-supported models rely on voluntary donations, grants and sponsorship, which lets them stay free and avoid ads. Banner adverts are tempting because many free apps use them, but Signal and Wikipedia deliberately avoid ads to protect user privacy and independence.

questions.stem: King Street Fabrics asks Island Pulse Media for a promotional video. Which pre-production activity should Zara's team complete FIRST?
options: Drawing the storyboard for each scene
Booking the camera, tripod and lighting kit
Choosing transitions and text overlays in WeVideo
Defining the problem, purpose and goal of the video
questions.explain: Problem definition comes first because every later decision (audience, message, shots, budget) depends on knowing what the product must achieve. The storyboard is tempting because it is an early planning tool, but you cannot plan scenes until you know the purpose and target audience.

questions.stem: Which planning tool shows each production task as a bar against a time scale, with milestones such as 'storyboard approved'?
questions.explain: A Gantt chart plots tasks against time, showing durations, overlaps and milestones, so a team can manage a production schedule. The storyboard is tempting because it is also a sequence, but it shows the order of shots in the product, not the timing of the work.

questions.stem: A document that fixes the logo placement, fonts, hex colour codes and spacing rules so every designer on a Carnival campaign produces consistent work is a
questions.explain: A style guide sets fixed rules that keep every item in a project consistent. A mood board is tempting because it also deals with colours and fonts, but it is a loose collection of inspiration that sets a feeling; it does not give exact rules.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the elements of visual design?
questions.explain: The elements are line, shape, form, space, texture, value and colour. Proximity is a principle of composition (how elements are arranged), not a basic element. Value is tempting because it sounds abstract, but it is the lightness or darkness of a colour and is a core element.

questions.stem: The logo of the Frigate Bay Grill uses orange and blue, which sit directly opposite each other on the colour wheel. This colour scheme is
questions.explain: Complementary colours are directly opposite each other on the wheel and create strong contrast. Split-complementary is tempting because it is based on the complement, but it uses a base colour with the two colours either side of its complement, so it has three colours, not two.

questions.stem: A photographer frames the Castries courthouse so that its cupola sits where two lines of a three-by-three grid cross. This applies
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the frame into a three-by-three grid and places the subject on a line or intersection. The golden ratio is tempting because it is also a composition rule, but it uses a proportion of about 1 to 1.618 and a spiral, not equal thirds.

questions.stem: On the ANU Ferry booking app, the 'Pay' button turns green and a message reads 'Booking confirmed' as soon as it is tapped. Which principle of interactive design is shown?
questions.explain: Feedback means the system responds visibly to every user action, confirming that it worked. Predictability is tempting, but it is about users being able to expect what will happen BEFORE they act, not the response afterwards.

questions.stem: Malik is designing a villain for a Caribbean animated short and wants colour alone to signal danger and menace. Which palette is MOST suitable?
options: Black, deep red and dark purple shades
Pastel pink and baby blue tints
questions.explain: Dark shades of red and purple with black are widely read as threatening, powerful and dangerous, which suits a villain. Bright yellow and sky blue is tempting because it is high contrast, but those colours suggest cheerfulness and energy, which fit a hero or a comic character better.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes an indigenous digital product?
options: A foreign film dubbed into a Caribbean language
Any game that is sold in a Caribbean store
Any app that can be downloaded in the Caribbean
Digital content created by local creators that reflects their own culture, identity and stories
questions.explain: Indigenous products are made by people from the culture and express that culture from the inside. A dubbed foreign film is tempting because it is adapted for local audiences, but it is still imported content: the stories and creative decisions come from elsewhere.

questions.stem: A Trinidadian studio produces an animated series featuring folklore characters such as Papa Bois and the soucouyant. What is the MAIN cultural motivation for this product?
options: To copy the style of imported cartoons exactly
To avoid paying any production costs
To avoid copyright law because folklore is old
To preserve and share Caribbean heritage with local and global audiences
questions.explain: Using local folklore keeps stories alive, builds cultural pride and introduces Caribbean heritage to the world. Avoiding copyright is tempting because folklore is traditional, but the studio's own scripts, characters and animation are still protected, and avoiding the law is not a cultural motivation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of POLICY support for local digital creators?
options: An imported game renaming characters with Caribbean names
A viewer streaming a Hollywood film
A creator buying followers on Instagram
A government film fund offering grants to Caribbean filmmakers
questions.explain: A government fund is a policy decision that directly finances local creative work. The renamed imported game is tempting because it looks local, but it is surface localisation of foreign content and does not support local creators.

questions.stem: Wikipedia is BEST classified as which type of digital media platform?
questions.explain: A knowledge platform exists to collect and share information, which is exactly Wikipedia's purpose. Infrastructure platform is tempting because Wikipedia is large and widely used, but infrastructure platforms provide underlying services (such as cloud hosting) for other products to be built on.

questions.stem: Maya needs the Island Pulse Media logo on a website with a transparent background, sharp edges and no compression artefacts. Which format is BEST?
questions.explain: PNG is lossless and supports full transparency, so edges stay crisp. GIF is tempting because it also supports transparency, but it is limited to 256 colours and only on-or-off transparency, so smooth edges and gradients look rough.
