questions.stem: Maya places a YouTube video of the Dominica Carnival parade inside a web page so that it plays there, without copying the video file to her own server. This is called
questions.explain: Embedding displays content hosted elsewhere inside your page using code such as an iframe. Importing is tempting, but importing brings a copy of the file into your own software or project.

questions.stem: Malik needs a full-quality master of a voice-over to edit in Audacity before the final export. Which format should he record and save in?
questions.explain: WAV is uncompressed, so no quality is lost while editing; you export to MP3 or OGG only at the end. OGG is tempting because it is an open format, but like MP3 it is lossy, and repeated saves in a lossy format degrade the audio.

questions.stem: In three-point lighting, which light is placed behind the subject to separate it from the background?
questions.explain: The back light (rim or hair light) shines from behind to outline the subject. The fill light is tempting because it is also a supporting light, but it sits on the opposite side of the key light to soften shadows on the face.

questions.stem: Keisha is recording an interview on a windy beach at Montego Bay. Which action BEST reduces unwanted noise?
options: Use the camera's built-in microphone from five metres away
Turn the input gain up as high as possible
Use a lavalier microphone with a furry windscreen and shield it from the wind
Add loud background music to cover the wind
questions.explain: A close lavalier with a windscreen captures the voice strongly while blocking wind. Turning the gain up is tempting because it makes the voice louder, but it also amplifies the wind noise and can cause clipping.

questions.stem: Which export setting is MOST suitable for a 30-second reel to be posted on Instagram?
questions.explain: Instagram Reels expect vertical 9:16 video, and MP4 with H.264 gives good quality at a small file size. GIF is tempting because it can animate, but it has no sound, poor colour and a very large file size for video-length content.

questions.stem: When a bouncing ball flattens as it hits the ground and lengthens as it rises, the animator is applying
questions.explain: Squash and stretch deforms the object to show weight, impact and speed while keeping its volume. Anticipation is tempting because it also involves a change of shape, but it is a preparatory movement before an action, such as crouching before a jump.

questions.stem: In Adobe Animate, Malik sets the ball's position on frame 1 and frame 24, and the software creates all the frames in between. This process is called
questions.explain: Interpolation, or tweening, is the automatic generation of in-between frames between keyframes. Onion skinning is tempting because it is also used when animating, but it only shows faint previous and next frames as a guide; it does not create frames.

questions.stem: In Blender, the flat surface enclosed by three or more edges of a mesh is called a
questions.explain: A face is the flat surface bounded by edges; faces together form the visible surface of the model. A vertex is tempting because it is also part of a mesh, but it is a single point where edges meet.

questions.stem: In a basic walk cycle, which key pose shows the legs furthest apart with both feet touching the ground?
questions.explain: The contact pose has the front heel and back toe both on the ground with the legs at full stride. The passing pose is tempting because it is also a key pose, but it shows one leg passing the other under the body, with the legs close together.

questions.stem: Why is version history in Google Docs an ADVANTAGE for a group writing an SBA proposal?
options: It closes the digital divide between group members
The group can see who changed what and restore an earlier version if needed
It removes the need for an internet connection
It stops group members from editing the same document
questions.explain: Version control records every change and lets the team roll back mistakes, which protects shared work. Working without internet is tempting, but Google Docs offline mode is limited and needs syncing; version history itself has nothing to do with connectivity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE of digital collaboration for a design team with members in Dominica and Guyana?
options: Unreliable connectivity during storms and power cuts
Access to a wider pool of talent
questions.explain: Connectivity problems and the digital divide can stop members from joining calls or uploading work. Access to a wider pool of talent is tempting because it involves distance, but it is an advantage (global reach), not a disadvantage.

questions.stem: Spice Lane food court paints giant footprints along the St. George’s boardwalk leading from the cruise pier to its stalls. This is an example of
questions.explain: Guerrilla marketing uses unconventional, low-cost, surprising tactics in public spaces. Cross-platform marketing is tempting because the idea could be shared online too, but cross-platform means keeping one consistent message across several channels, not one physical stunt.

questions.stem: Which KPI BEST shows whether a Mailchimp email campaign persuaded readers to visit a tour booking page?
questions.explain: Click-through rate measures the percentage of readers who clicked the link to the booking page, which is the action the campaign wanted. Open rate is tempting, but it only shows that people opened the email, not that they acted on it.

questions.stem: Smartphones, smart TVs and connected screens are now found in almost every home, school and workplace in Barbados, so designers must plan for them. Which driving factor does this BEST illustrate?
questions.explain: Pervasiveness means technology is present everywhere in daily life. Commoditisation is tempting because cheap devices help spread technology, but commoditisation describes technology becoming standardised and cheap, not how widespread it is.

questions.stem: A user interface uses frosted, semi-transparent panels floating over a blurred, colourful background. This trend is known as
questions.explain: Glassmorphism imitates frosted glass with transparency and background blur. Neumorphism is tempting because it is also a recent soft UI trend, but it uses solid, same-colour surfaces with soft shadows so elements look pushed out of or into the background.

questions.stem: A St. Lucian youth group raises money for an animated film by collecting small donations from hundreds of supporters on an online platform. This source of funding is
questions.explain: Crowdfunding raises many small contributions from the public online. Sponsorship is tempting because supporters give money, but sponsorship comes from one business or organisation in return for publicity, not from many individuals.

questions.stem: Which cost belongs under 'personnel' in an itemised budget for a 30-second ad?
options: A monthly Adobe Creative Cloud subscription
The fee for a freelance voice actor
questions.explain: Personnel costs are payments to people for their time and skills. The Adobe subscription is tempting because it is a recurring cost, but it belongs under software, and the tripod belongs under equipment.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes the ePub format?
options: A content management system for blogs
A video format for online courses
A fixed image of printed pages that cannot change size
An open e-book format with reflowable text that adapts to the reader's screen
questions.explain: ePub is an open standard whose text reflows to fit phones, tablets and e-readers. A fixed image of printed pages is tempting because some e-books look like print, but that describes a PDF or a fixed-layout scan, not reflowable ePub.

questions.stem: A Jamaican author publishes the same novel as a paperback and as an ePub e-book. What is the main purpose of giving each format its own ISBN?
options: To uniquely identify each edition and format for sellers, libraries and distributors
To improve the book's search engine ranking
To protect the novel automatically under copyright law
questions.explain: An ISBN is an identifier that lets the book trade track one specific edition and format. Copyright protection is tempting because both relate to books, but copyright exists automatically when the work is created; an ISBN gives no legal protection.

questions.stem: The network funded by the US Department of Defense in the late 1960s, which became the forerunner of the Internet, was
questions.explain: ARPANET linked research computers from 1969 and introduced packet switching that the Internet still uses. The World Wide Web is tempting, but it came about twenty years later (Tim Berners-Lee, around 1989 to 1991) and runs on top of the Internet.

questions.stem: An online game in which thousands of players from Barbados, Guyana and around the world share one persistent virtual world at the same time is a
questions.explain: MMOG means massively multiplayer online game: a very large, shared, persistent world. A PWA is tempting because games can run in browsers, but a PWA is simply a web app that installs like a native app; it says nothing about large numbers of shared players.

questions.stem: A Barbadian photographer licenses her photos under Creative Commons BY-NC. A hotel wants to use one in a paid advertisement. What should the hotel do?
options: Edit the photo so that it becomes a new work
Use it freely as long as it credits the photographer
Use it without credit because it is free online
Ask the photographer for permission, because NC does not allow commercial use
questions.explain: NC (non-commercial) forbids commercial use without separate permission, and an advert is commercial. Crediting the photographer is tempting because BY does require attribution, but attribution alone does not cancel the non-commercial condition.

questions.stem: A student copies three paragraphs from a national newspaper article into her blog post and publishes it under her own name with no credit. This is
questions.explain: Presenting another writer's words as your own is plagiarism, and it may also infringe copyright. Fair use is tempting because the passage is short, but fair use requires a limited, transformative purpose such as criticism; copying without credit and claiming authorship is never fair use.

questions.stem: Which writing technique is MOST suitable for a podcast script about the history of Anguilla's salt ponds?
options: Conversational language, short sentences and spoken signposts such as 'next, we will hear'
Long paragraphs with footnotes and references
Tables and bullet points for each date
questions.explain: Podcast scripts are written for the ear, so they must sound natural and guide the listener. Tables and bullet points are tempting because they organise facts clearly, but listeners cannot see them; they suit web pages, not audio.

questions.stem: Maya sketches the layout of a tour company's home page on paper and asks five users where they would tap to book. This is a
questions.explain: Paper sketches are low-fidelity prototypes: fast, cheap and ideal for early testing of layout and flow. A high-fidelity prototype is tempting because it is also tested with users, but it is a detailed digital model, often clickable, that looks close to the finished product.

questions.stem: A diagram that lists every page of the Tamarind Heritage website and shows how the pages link together is a
questions.explain: A site map shows the full set of pages and their links, planning site structure. A concept map is tempting because it also shows relationships, but it links ideas and topics, not the actual pages of a website.

questions.stem: Which of the following goes AGAINST the criteria for web-friendly content?
options: Long, dense paragraphs filled with technical jargon
Plain language and clear calls to action
questions.explain: Web-friendly content uses short paragraphs and direct address, and avoids jargon and needless repetition. Addressing the reader as 'you' is tempting because it feels informal, but direct address is specifically recommended for web writing.

questions.stem: Keisha adds a descriptive title tag, a meta description and relevant keywords to each page of a Grenada spice tour website. This MAINLY improves
options: the security of the booking form
the site's search engine optimisation and machine indexability
questions.explain: Titles, meta descriptions and keywords help search engines understand and rank the page. Loading speed is tempting because it also affects SEO, but metadata does not make images load faster; compressing and resizing images does.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN purpose of adding alt text to images on a web page?
options: To describe the image for screen reader users and search engines
To stop people from copying the image
To make the image file smaller
To add a caption below the image for all visitors
questions.explain: Alt text is read aloud by screen readers and indexed by search engines, supporting accessibility and SEO. A visible caption is tempting, but alt text is normally hidden and only shown if the image fails to load; captions are separate elements.

questions.stem: A photographer shooting johnny cakes for a café website wants the food sharp and the background softly blurred. Which technique should she use?
options: The rule of thirds with a fisheye lens
A deep depth of field with a small aperture
A shallow depth of field with a wide aperture
questions.explain: A shallow depth of field (wide aperture such as f/1.8, or portrait mode on a phone) keeps the subject sharp and blurs the background. Deep depth of field is tempting because it keeps things sharp, but it keeps the background sharp too, which makes it distracting.

questions.stem: A podcast recorded in a Castries classroom has a constant air-conditioner hum. In Audacity, the BEST way to remove it is to
options: add a fade-in to the start of the recording
increase the volume of the whole track
select a few seconds of hum only, capture the noise profile, then apply Noise Reduction to the whole track
questions.explain: Noise Reduction learns the hum from a sample (the noise profile) and removes it across the track. Converting to MP3 is tempting because it changes the file, but MP3 compression does not remove noise and actually loses some audio quality.

questions.stem: On a tour website, the line 'Home > Tours > Booby Island' at the top of a page is an example of
questions.explain: Breadcrumbs show users their location in the site hierarchy and let them step back up a level. An anchor link is tempting because it also helps navigation, but it jumps to a section within the same page.

questions.stem: Which HTML code opens an external booking site in a new browser tab?
questions.explain: The a element uses href for the address, and target="_blank" opens a new tab (rel="noopener" improves security). The link element is tempting because of its name, but it belongs in the head to connect files such as stylesheets; it does not create clickable links.

questions.stem: In the CSS box model, what is the correct order of layers from the inside of an element outwards?
questions.explain: Content sits inside padding, which is surrounded by the border, with margin outside the border separating the box from others. Content, border, padding, margin is tempting because it starts correctly, but padding is always inside the border.

questions.stem: Which elements does the CSS rule .price { color: #b00020; } style?
questions.explain: A full stop before a name is a class selector, which can apply to many elements. The id option is tempting, but id selectors use a hash (#price) and should match only one element.

questions.stem: A Grenada tourism page uses light grey text (#bbbbbb) on a white background. Which design principle does this MOST clearly break?
options: Accessibility, because the colour contrast is too low (WCAG)
questions.explain: WCAG requires sufficient contrast between text and background; pale grey on white is hard to read, especially outdoors or for users with low vision. Responsive layout is tempting because it is also a UI principle, but it concerns adapting to screen sizes, not colour.

questions.stem: A student researching hurricane preparedness checks who wrote a blog post and whether the writer works for a national disaster management office. Which evaluation criterion is she applying?
questions.explain: Authority asks who created the content and whether they are qualified and credible. Usability is tempting because it is a common evaluation criterion, but it measures how easy the content is to use and navigate, not who wrote it.

questions.stem: A Dominican heritage group wants commuters to learn Caribbean history in 20-minute episodes while driving. Which form of digital publishing is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Podcasts are audio and can be enjoyed safely while driving. An interactive e-book is tempting because it can include audio, but it is designed to be read and tapped, which is unsafe and impractical for drivers.

questions.stem: A Grenadian bakery built its whole audience on one social platform. After an algorithm change, its posts now reach far fewer followers. This illustrates which limitation of online platforms?
questions.explain: Platform dependency means you do not control the rules or algorithms of the platform your audience lives on. Analytics tools are tempting because the bakery would notice the drop through analytics, but analytics are a benefit, not the cause of the problem.

questions.stem: Which editorial standard is REQUIRED when writing a Wikipedia article about the Battle of Fort George?
options: A neutral point of view supported by reliable, verifiable sources
A persuasive tone that promotes Belize tourism
The author's name and photograph at the top
Original research from the writer's own interviews
questions.explain: Wikipedia requires neutrality and verifiability from published reliable sources. Original research is tempting because interviews sound rigorous, but Wikipedia does not allow unpublished original research; it must cite existing sources.

questions.stem: Compared with free hosted WordPress.com, a self-hosted WordPress site gives Frigate Bay Surf School
options: full control over plugins, design and data, but responsibility for hosting, backups and security
automatic security updates handled by the platform
no need to pay for hosting or a domain
questions.explain: Self-hosting gives maximum control and ownership but the owner must pay for hosting and maintain security and backups. Automatic updates are tempting because many hosts offer them, but on a self-hosted site keeping the system updated is ultimately the owner's responsibility.

questions.stem: A news organisation stores articles once and sends them through an API to its website, mobile app and smartwatch alerts, each with its own design. This is a
questions.explain: A headless CMS separates content (the 'body') from presentation (the 'head'), delivering content to many channels. A document CMS is tempting because it stores documents, but it manages files such as PDFs and contracts inside an organisation, not multi-channel publishing.

questions.stem: In a content workflow, which stage comes immediately after an editor reviews a draft blog post?
questions.explain: The workflow runs creation, review, approval, publishing, archiving. Publishing is tempting because it seems the natural next step, but content must be approved by someone with authority before it goes live.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a proprietary, cloud-hosted CMS?
questions.explain: Wix is owned by a company and runs on its own servers. WordPress.org software is tempting because WordPress is very well known, but the WordPress.org software is open source and can be self-hosted.

questions.stem: Which factor influencing trends in web publishing covers government regulation, censorship and data laws?
questions.explain: Politics covers government regulation, censorship and data laws, and sits alongside commoditisation, pervasiveness, affordability, accessibility, adoption and empowerment. Accessibility is tempting because it is very topical, but it is about whether people can reach and use content, not about government action.

questions.stem: More people now ask smart speakers questions such as 'Where can I buy sorrel drink in Port of Spain?'. How should web publishers respond to this trend?
options: Remove all text and use only images
Use longer pages full of repeated keywords
Write clear, conversational question-and-answer content with local details
questions.explain: Voice search favours natural-language questions and direct answers, such as FAQ sections with local information. Repeating keywords is tempting because it once helped SEO, but keyword stuffing is now penalised and does not match how people speak.

questions.stem: Which BEST describes a progressive web app (PWA)?
options: A social media page for a business
A printed brochure converted to PDF
An app that is only available on the Apple App Store
A website that can be installed on the home screen and can work offline like an app
questions.explain: A PWA is a website with app-like features such as installation, offline access and notifications. An App Store app is tempting because PWAs feel like apps, but PWAs are delivered through the web and do not need an app store.

questions.stem: Which of the following is part of the INFRASTRUCTURE component of the mobile ecosystem?
options: A news app from a national newspaper
Cell towers and submarine fibre-optic cables
A teenager streaming music in Port of Spain
questions.explain: Infrastructure is the physical and technical backbone that carries data, such as towers, spectrum and cables. A smartwatch is tempting because it is hardware, but it is a device, a separate component of the ecosystem.

questions.stem: A national regulator sets rules for spectrum licences and personal data protection that all mobile operators and app developers must follow. In the mobile ecosystem, the regulator is part of the
questions.explain: The enabling environment includes policy frameworks, regulators and laws that shape how the ecosystem works. The content layer is tempting because data protection affects apps, but content refers to the apps, media and services themselves, not the rules governing them.

questions.stem: After a hurricane damages towers across Grenada, residents cannot use a mobile banking app even though the bank's servers are working. This BEST illustrates
questions.explain: Each part of the ecosystem relies on the others: without carrier infrastructure, content and devices cannot connect. Fragmentation is tempting because it is a mobile problem, but it describes the variety of Android devices and versions, not network failure.

questions.stem: Which feature BEST describes the Android operating system?
options: Open source, used by many manufacturers, with a wide range of devices and versions
Closed source and available only on Apple devices
Unable to run apps from Google Play
questions.explain: Android is open source and licensed to many manufacturers, which brings variety but also fragmentation. Closed source on Apple devices describes iOS, which is the most tempting confusion between the two platforms.

questions.stem: Jerome wants to build a native iPhone app. Which development environment and language should he use?
questions.explain: Apple's Xcode with the Swift language and the iOS SDK is the official route to native iOS apps. Android Studio and Kotlin is tempting because it is also an official native toolset, but it builds Android apps, not iOS apps.

questions.stem: A farmer in St. Kitts places soil-moisture sensors in a field that send readings over the network to an app on her phone. This is an example of
questions.explain: The Internet of Things connects everyday objects with sensors so they can collect and share data. A progressive web app is tempting because the farmer views data on her phone, but a PWA is a type of web app; the sensors connected to the network are what make this IoT.

questions.stem: A start-up in Jamaica has a small budget and wants to reach as many local users as possible quickly. Most of its target users have mid-range Android phones. Which platform decision is MOST sensible?
options: Build for iOS first because Apple users spend more
Build separate native apps for Android, iOS and HarmonyOS at once
Build for Android first, or use a cross-platform tool such as Flutter
questions.explain: Matching the platform to the target audience, budget and time-to-market points to Android first, or one cross-platform code base. iOS first is tempting because iOS users often spend more on apps, but it ignores where this start-up's actual users are and adds cost.

questions.stem: Many Caribbean users spend hours on international streaming and social apps, but relatively few locally made apps and channels exist. This is described as
options: the imbalance between content consumption and content production
questions.explain: The syllabus highlights that the Caribbean consumes far more digital content than it produces. The digital divide is tempting because it is also an inequality, but it refers to unequal ACCESS to technology, not the gap between consuming and creating content.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN role of submarine fibre-optic cables in the Caribbean mobile ecosystem?
options: They provide GPS signals to phones
They carry international Internet traffic between islands and the rest of the world
They replace the need for local cell towers
questions.explain: Most international data travels through undersea cables that link island networks to the global Internet. Replacing cell towers is tempting because cables carry data, but towers are still needed to connect phones wirelessly to the network on land.

questions.stem: A Guyanese family living in Toronto sends money home and video-calls relatives every week using mobile apps. This BEST illustrates
options: the diaspora connection supported by mobile technology
questions.explain: Mobile apps bridge Caribbean communities across the world, supporting remittances and family ties. E-government is tempting because money transfers can be official, but e-government means government services delivered online, not personal family communication.

questions.stem: Which is the STRONGEST economic benefit of developing apps locally in Barbados rather than importing them?
options: Local apps cannot be used by tourists
Local development creates jobs and builds skills, and successful apps can be exported to other islands
questions.explain: Local app development keeps money and skills in the economy and can grow into regional exports. 'Local apps never need updating' is tempting because local developers are close by, but every app needs ongoing updates for OS changes and security.

questions.stem: KIN Heritage Trail app guides visitors to historic sites such as Fort Charles with audio stories told by local elders. Which benefit of local apps does this MOST directly demonstrate?
questions.explain: Recording elders' stories preserves heritage and connects visitors and residents to local culture. Reduced data usage is tempting because good apps optimise data, but it is a UX factor, not a benefit of the app being local.

questions.stem: An app for Dominica's disaster preparedness lets residents find shelters, receive alerts and mark themselves safe. This is BEST classified as a
questions.explain: Disaster preparedness apps serve public safety and community well-being, which makes them social impact or civic apps. A subscription app is tempting because alerts are ongoing, but charging people for life-saving alerts would conflict with the app's public purpose.

questions.stem: Older users of a health clinic app in Antigua keep tapping the wrong buttons. Which change MOST directly addresses this UX problem?
options: Add more features to the home screen
Use smaller text so more fits on screen
Increase touch target sizes and spacing between buttons
questions.explain: Larger touch targets (about 44 to 48 points) with space between them reduce mistaken taps, especially for older users. Adding more features is tempting because it seems helpful, but it crowds the screen and makes mis-taps more likely.

questions.stem: Many users of a Guyanese farming app live in rural areas with weak, expensive mobile data. Which design strategy is MOST appropriate?
options: Require users to stay online at all times
Use high-resolution autoplay videos on every screen
Add a large animated splash screen
Compress images, cache data and provide an offline mode
questions.explain: Optimising for low bandwidth means small files, caching and offline features so the app still works with poor coverage. Autoplay video is tempting because it is engaging, but it consumes large amounts of data and fails on weak connections.

questions.stem: A delivery app is used by drivers outdoors in bright Caribbean sunlight. Which factor of the mobile user experience is MOST relevant?
questions.explain: The environment (lighting, noise, movement) affects readability, so designers use high contrast, large text and possibly a high-visibility mode. Processing power is tempting because drivers need fast apps, but it does not explain the difficulty of reading a screen in sunlight.

questions.stem: Which feature MOST improves accessibility for blind users of a mobile app?
options: Labels on every button and image that screen readers such as TalkBack and VoiceOver can read
questions.explain: Screen readers depend on proper labels to describe buttons and images aloud. Gesture-only navigation is tempting because it removes visual clutter, but hidden gestures are hard to discover and are often unusable with a screen reader.

questions.stem: What is the main DIFFERENCE between a wireframe and a clickable prototype?
options: A wireframe shows static screen layouts; a clickable prototype links screens so users can test the flow
A wireframe is the finished app; a prototype is a sketch
A wireframe is written in Kotlin; a prototype is written in Swift
questions.explain: Wireframes plan layout and structure; prototypes add interactivity so user flows can be tested before coding. The first option is tempting because both are stages, but it reverses them: the wireframe comes first and the finished app comes last.

questions.stem: A group of CAPE students with no coding experience wants a working Android prototype of a school canteen ordering app within two weeks. Which tool is MOST suitable?
options: A text editor and Java only
questions.explain: No-code and low-code builders let beginners create working apps quickly with visual blocks. Xcode is tempting because it is a professional app tool, but it builds iOS apps and requires Swift coding, which does not fit beginners targeting Android.

questions.stem: Before launch, Jerome gives the BusLink GND app to twenty commuters, who check whether it actually meets their needs. This is
questions.explain: UAT is performed by real target users to confirm the app meets their requirements. Unit testing is tempting because it is also testing, but developers do it on small pieces of code, not real users on the whole app.

questions.stem: A Barbados bank releases an internal app only to its own staff, without listing it on Google Play or the App Store. This distribution model is
options: a beta release on a public store
questions.explain: Enterprise distribution delivers apps privately to an organisation's employees. Direct download is tempting because the app avoids public stores, but direct download usually offers the file to the general public from a website.

questions.stem: Keisha rewrites an app's store title, adds the keywords 'St. Lucia bus' and 'Castries', uploads clear screenshots and encourages happy users to leave ratings. This is
questions.explain: ASO improves the title, keywords, description, screenshots and ratings so the app ranks higher in store searches. Influencer marketing is tempting because ratings involve other people, but influencer marketing pays or partners with content creators to promote the app outside the store.

questions.stem: Which sequence shows the user journey for a mobile app in the correct order?
options: Discover, test, review, purchase, download, retain
Retain, review, test, discover, download, purchase
Purchase, download, discover, test, review, retain
Download, discover, review, retain, test, purchase
questions.explain: Users first discover the app, try or test it, read reviews, purchase (if paid), download and finally are retained. Starting with purchase is tempting because buying feels like the key step, but users rarely buy before they have discovered and judged the app.

questions.stem: A Trinidad language-learning app is free to download with basic lessons, but users pay to unlock advanced courses and offline downloads. This revenue model is
questions.explain: Freemium offers a free core product with paid premium features. Paid upfront is tempting because users do pay, but paid upfront means paying before downloading at all.

questions.stem: In a free mobile game, players can choose to watch a 30-second advert to earn extra lives. This is
questions.explain: Rewarded video gives users a reward for choosing to watch an advert. An interstitial is tempting because it is also full screen, but interstitials appear automatically at breaks; the user does not choose to watch them for a reward.

questions.stem: A St. Lucian developer builds one restaurant ordering app and licenses it to ten restaurants, each of which adds its own logo and colours. This revenue model is
questions.explain: White-label apps are built once and licensed to other businesses to rebrand as their own. Freemium is tempting because the developer may offer a basic version, but freemium earns from end users upgrading, not from businesses licensing the app.

questions.stem: Which revenue approach is MOST appropriate for a hurricane-alert app run by a Caribbean charity?
options: Grants, sponsorship and donations, with the app free to all users
questions.explain: Civic and social good apps are usually funded by grants, sponsors and donations so that everyone can access safety information. A subscription is tempting because it gives steady income, but it would exclude people who cannot pay from life-saving alerts, which is unethical for this purpose.

questions.stem: One app that combines messaging, taxi booking, food delivery and payments, as WeChat and Grab do, is known as a
questions.explain: Super apps consolidate many services into one platform. White-label app is tempting because it is also a business model term, but it describes one app rebranded for many businesses, not many services in one app.

questions.stem: A Caribbean health app developer must explain what personal data is collected, obtain consent and allow users to delete their data. These requirements are MOST influenced by
options: data protection regulation such as the GDPR and regional data protection laws
questions.explain: Privacy laws such as the GDPR and Caribbean data protection acts require transparency, consent and the right to deletion. 5G is tempting because it is a major trend, but it concerns network speed, not how personal data must be handled.

questions.stem: Which tool is designed MAINLY for tracking app downloads, rankings and market trends?
questions.explain: Sensor Tower (like data.ai, formerly App Annie, and Statista) tracks app market data and trends. Balsamiq is tempting because it is used in app development, but it is a wireframing tool, not a research tool.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: Maya at the Island Pulse Media is designing a booking website for the English Harbour Kayak Tours. After analysis and definition she develops three different homepage ideas at the same time, brings them together to select one, and after implementation the evaluation sends her back to re-analyse. Which creative process model is she using?

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Keisha at the Island Pulse Media is filling in the pre-production checklist for a Sugar Mas promo video in Basseterre. Sort each task under its core element.

Which core element does this task belong to?

Set a budget of US$1,500 for crew, gear hire and editing.
questions.explain: Money (budget) is a resource: it decides scale, equipment, crew and quality.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which core element does this task belong to?

Book an editor and a sound engineer for two days.
questions.explain: Personnel are a resource.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which core element does this task belong to?

Get a permit to film in a public area during the parade.
questions.explain: Permits for public or regulated spaces are clearances.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which core element does this task belong to?

Collect signed consent forms from the troupe members filmed.
questions.explain: Releases (consent forms) from talent and interviewees are clearances.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which core element does this task belong to?

License the calypso track used as background music.
questions.explain: Properly licensing third-party music protects against copyright infringement.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which core element does this task belong to?

Check that every photo in the end titles is original or cleared.
questions.explain: All material used must be legal and cleared: copyright and IP.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which core element does this task belong to?

Make sure the sponsor's claims in the advert are truthful.
questions.explain: Truthful advertising is legal and ethical compliance under codes of practice.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which core element does this task belong to?

Do a risk assessment for filming on a moving float at night.
questions.explain: Risk assessments for filming conditions are health and safety.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: Grande Riviere Turtle Watch group in Trinidad is worried that beachgoers disturb nesting turtles. Which is the STRONGEST problem statement for a digital media product?
options: We need to make a TikTok video about turtles.

Beachgoers at Grande Riviere and Matura Beach need a quick way to learn how to behave near turtle nests because many disturb nests without realising it; goal: reduce reported disturbances by half during the next nesting season.
The group wants a beautiful website with lots of turtle photos.
Turtles are important to the Caribbean.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Keisha is building a persona for Fish Fry Hop food-tour app in Providenciales. Sort each research finding.

What kind of audience information is this?

Most users are aged 25 to 44.
questions.explain: Age is a measurable fact about people, so it is demographic.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
What kind of audience information is this?

Users value authentic local food over chain restaurants.
questions.explain: Values and attitudes are psychographic.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
What kind of audience information is this?

Users book tours on their phones in the evening.
questions.explain: This describes what people actually do, so it is a behaviour.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
What kind of audience information is this?

Many visitors come from the United States and Canada.
questions.explain: Location or country of origin is demographic.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
What kind of audience information is this?

Users see themselves as adventurous foodies.
questions.explain: Self-image and lifestyle are psychographic.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
What kind of audience information is this?

Users read reviews on TripAdvisor before choosing.
questions.explain: Reading reviews before deciding is a behaviour.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
What kind of audience information is this?

Most users have a household income above the regional average.
questions.explain: Income is a measurable demographic factor.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
What kind of audience information is this?

Users share food photos on Instagram during the meal.
questions.explain: Sharing photos is an action they take, so it is a behaviour.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Maya at the Island Pulse Media is planning a website for the Punda Market Collective in Willemstad. Sort each planning item.

Which planning document does this belong in?

A quick pencil drawing showing the menu bar at the top and three product boxes below.
questions.explain: A loose layout drawing that explores structure is a rough sketch.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which planning document does this belong in?

Photos of spice stalls, woven baskets and sunset colours pinned together.
questions.explain: A collage of inspiring images that captures a feeling is a mood board.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which planning document does this belong in?

Heading font: Montserrat Bold, 32 px; body: Open Sans, 16 px.
questions.explain: Exact typography rules belong in the style guide.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which planning document does this belong in?

Primary colour: #E07A1F; never place the logo on a busy photo.
questions.explain: Exact colour values and logo rules are style guide content.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which planning document does this belong in?

Words like "fresh", "bilingual" and "market morning" beside fabric textures.
questions.explain: Mood words and textures set the direction, so this is a mood board.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which planning document does this belong in?

Eight tiny thumbnail layouts drawn in eight minutes.
questions.explain: Thumbnails are small rough sketches for exploring many layouts.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which planning document does this belong in?

All buttons have rounded corners and 12 px padding.
questions.explain: Rules for UI components keep the site consistent, so they belong in the style guide.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Which planning document does this belong in?

A loose drawing of the homepage hero area with notes saying "photo here".
questions.explain: An annotated, unfinished layout is a rough sketch.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
Jerome, Malik and Keisha at the Island Pulse Media are planning a promotional video for the English Harbour Reef Dive Centre. Answer each question about their planning.

On their Gantt chart, "Client approves storyboard" is shown as a diamond with no length. This is a...
questions.explain: A milestone is a key checkpoint with no duration, often drawn as a diamond.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: Editing cannot begin until underwater filming is complete. This relationship is called a...
questions.explain: When one task must wait for another, the tasks are dependent.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: The document that lists each task, who is responsible and the deadline is the...
questions.explain: A work plan assigns tasks, people, resources and deadlines.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: Filming is booked for 7 a.m. Saturday at the reef, with a back-up date the next weekend. Where is this recorded?
questions.explain: The production schedule gives the detailed when, where and who of production.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: The divers who appear in the video must sign a form allowing their image to be used. This is a...
questions.explain: A model release form gives legal permission to use a person's image, a key legal consideration in pre-production.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: Two extra days are added before the deadline in case of rough seas. This is...
questions.explain: Buffer time protects the deadline from delays such as bad weather.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem:
You are a junior designer at Island Pulse Media. Carnival Village Committee wants a digital product to help people enjoy Trinidad and Tobago Carnival. Zara asks you to lead pre-production. Make the best decisions.

The committee chair says: "Just build us an app with everything on it, fast." What do you do first?
options: Hold a short meeting to agree the brief: the problem, the users, the goal, the budget and the deadline.
Open Android Studio and start coding an app straight away.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: You survey 60 residents and visitors. Most want to know when and where bands and jump-ups pass, and many have limited data. Which problem statement do you write?
options: "The committee needs a beautiful app with a 3D Carnival City."
"Carnival-goers need a quick, low-data way to know where and when events happen because they miss events and waste data searching social media."

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: In ideation your team suggests a full app, a WhatsApp alert channel, a printable QR map and a live TikTok feed. You select a low-data web map with WhatsApp alerts. What next?
options: Create rough sketches, a mood board and a style guide, a storyboard for the 30-second promo, and a Gantt chart with milestones and buffer time.
Skip planning: Carnival is only six weeks away.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: Maya has a clickable Figma prototype of the map. Before full development, what do you do?
options: Ask the team if they like it, then launch.
Test it with eight real Carnival-goers on their own phones, observe them, collect feedback and fix problems.

questions.topic: Pre-production principles: creating a digital media product
questions.stem: The Bridgetown Fit Club in Barbados has a paper prototype of a workout app. The owner wants to skip testing and go straight to full development. Which is the BEST justification for validating the prototype first?
options: Testing makes the app look more professional.
Testing with real members reveals usability problems and confirms demand while changes are still cheap, reducing the risk of building an app nobody uses.
Testing is required by app stores before any app is published.
Testing means the team will not need a Gantt chart.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
Students at the Sol Studio in Georgetown are mixing paint for a mural of Kaieteur Falls. Answer each question using the traditional RYB colour wheel.

Mixing yellow and blue in equal amounts gives...
questions.explain: Yellow + blue = green, a secondary colour.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: Which of these is a tertiary colour?
questions.explain: Blue-green is a primary (blue) mixed with a neighbouring secondary (green).

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: How many tertiary colours are on a standard 12-part wheel?
questions.explain: There are six tertiaries, one between each primary and secondary.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: Which group contains only warm colours?
questions.explain: Reds, oranges and yellows are warm; they feel energetic and seem to advance.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: A vivid turquoise is made duller and greyer. Which property has changed?
questions.explain: Saturation is intensity. The hue stays turquoise, but it becomes less pure.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: Red, yellow and blue are primary on the RYB wheel because...
options: they cannot be made by mixing other colours
they are always used in logos
questions.explain: Primary colours are the starting colours that cannot be mixed from others in that model.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
Jerome at the Island Pulse Media is building a colour palette for the Sorrel Express delivery app, starting from one rich sorrel red. Sort each variation.

How was this variation of the base red created?

A soft pink used for the app's background cards.
questions.explain: Pink is red lightened with white, so it is a tint.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
How was this variation of the base red created?

A deep wine colour for the header bar.
questions.explain: Darkening red with black gives a shade such as wine or maroon.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
How was this variation of the base red created?

A dusty, muted rose for disabled buttons.
questions.explain: Muted and greyish means grey was added, so it is a tone.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
How was this variation of the base red created?

A very pale blush for the splash-screen glow.
questions.explain: Very light versions of a hue are tints.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
How was this variation of the base red created?

Near-black maroon for text that must be dark but still warm.
questions.explain: Lots of black added to red produces a deep shade.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
How was this variation of the base red created?

A greyish red that feels calm and sophisticated.
questions.explain: Grey reduces saturation without just lightening or darkening, which creates a tone.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
How was this variation of the base red created?

Strawberry milk pink for a "special offer" sticker.
questions.explain: Red plus white makes a light pink tint.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
How was this variation of the base red created?

A dark burgundy shadow beneath the logo.
questions.explain: Burgundy is a dark shade of red.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: Regent Street Bookshop in Georgetown has a logo with the hex colour #00A86B. The owner wants the logo printed on 500 paper bags and also shown on the shop's Instagram page. Which statement is MOST accurate?
options: The same hex code works perfectly on screens and paper because colours are universal.
The printer will use red, yellow and blue ink to match the hex code exactly.
The hex code is an RGB screen value, so it is right for Instagram, but the logo should be converted to a CMYK value and proof-checked before printing because ink mixes subtractively.
The logo should be designed in CMYK for Instagram because CMYK has more colours.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
The Island Pulse Media has five new clients across the Caribbean. Choose the most suitable main colour for each brief.

Calm Waters counselling app for teenagers in Barbados wants users to feel safe and relaxed.
questions.explain: Soft cool colours are associated with calm and trust; red and neon would feel urgent.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: Flash Sale Friday campaign for a Spanish Town electronics shop needs urgency.
questions.explain: Red signals urgency and energy, and yellow grabs attention.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: The Nature Isle Treks company in Dominica promotes rainforest hikes.
questions.explain: Greens and earth tones connect directly with nature and the rainforest.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: Velvet Nights luxury spa in Rodney Bay, St. Lucia, wants a premium, elegant feel.
questions.explain: Purple, black and gold suggest luxury and sophistication; primary triads feel playful.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: A designer assumes white will mean "pure" to every visitor of a global wedding site. What is the risk?
options: white is linked to mourning in some cultures
white cannot be shown on screens
none: colours mean the same everywhere
questions.explain: Colour meanings vary by culture, so a global audience needs testing.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem:
The Island Pulse Media is making a mobile game, Guardians of the Salt Pond, set in Bonaire. Zara asks you to choose the colours for the hero, a young pelican named Pip, and the villain, a pollution monster called Smog. Make the best decisions.

First, Pip the hero. Players are aged 9 to 14 and should trust and cheer for Pip instantly. Which palette do you choose?
options: Warm golden-yellow and soft sea blue with white highlights; light values and rounded shapes.
Dark grey and black with red eyes to look cool.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: Now Smog the villain. Smog must look threatening and must stand out clearly from Pip in every scene. Which palette?
options: Deep purple and charcoal shades with a sickly yellow-green glow, sharp jagged shapes.
The same golden-yellow and sea blue as Pip, but slightly darker.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: The game background is a bright blue sky and turquoise salt pond. Malik worries Pip's blue may blend in. What do you do?
options: Run a greyscale and contrast check, then give Pip a darker outline and more yellow so Pip stands out from the background.
Ignore it; players will find Pip eventually.

questions.topic: Elements of visual design and colour theory
questions.stem: Keisha notes that some players may have red-green colour vision deficiency. Smog's attacks are shown only by turning red. What do you change?
options: Add a shape change and an icon to each attack, so it does not rely on colour alone, and record all hex codes in the style guide.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Malik at the Island Pulse Media is framing shots for a tourism reel about English Harbour in Antigua. Answer each question.

Malik places the yacht exactly where the top-right grid lines cross in a 3 by 3 grid. He is using...
questions.explain: The intersections of a 3 by 3 grid are the power points of the rule of thirds.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem: The golden ratio is approximately...
questions.explain: Phi is about 1.618. 1.333 is the 4:3 aspect ratio and 1.777 is 16:9, which are traps.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem: A point about 61.8% along a line, dividing it in the golden ratio, is called the...
questions.explain: The golden section is a point (or line) that divides a length in the golden ratio.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem: He wants the sea horizon to emphasise a dramatic sunset sky. Where should the horizon go?
questions.explain: A low horizon gives about two thirds of the frame to the sky, which is the part he wants to emphasise.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem: A rectangle that leaves another rectangle of the same proportions when a square is removed is a...
questions.explain: That self-repeating property defines the golden rectangle and produces the golden spiral.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem: A jet-ski rider is moving left to right. Where should Malik leave the most space?
options: behind the rider, on the left
in front of the rider, on the right
questions.explain: Lead room in front of a moving or looking subject gives it somewhere to go and feels natural.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem: On a 24 in tall poster, where does the golden section put the headline, measured from the top?
questions.explain: 24 divided by 1.618 is about 14.8 in; 24 minus 14.8 leaves about 9.2 in from the top. 8 in is the thirds line and 12 in is the dead centre.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Maya at the Island Pulse Media is redesigning the website of a Grand Anse dive shop. Sort each change by the principle it mainly applies.

Which principle does this change mainly apply?

Every page uses the same coral-orange buttons and the same heading font.
questions.explain: Reusing colours and fonts across pages is repetition, which builds unity and brand identity.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Which principle does this change mainly apply?

The price, duration and depth of each dive are grouped tightly under its photo.
questions.explain: Placing related information close together is proximity.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Which principle does this change mainly apply?

All text blocks and images now line up on the same left margin.
questions.explain: Lining elements up on a common edge is alignment.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Which principle does this change mainly apply?

The headline "Dive the Wrecks of Gros Islet" is now three times larger than the body text.
questions.explain: Using size to show what matters most is hierarchy.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Which principle does this change mainly apply?

The "Book a dive" button is bold, bright and placed above the details.
questions.explain: Weight, colour and position signal importance, so this is hierarchy.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Which principle does this change mainly apply?

Each section uses the same wave-shaped divider.
questions.explain: A repeated visual motif is repetition.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Which principle does this change mainly apply?

The contact phone, email and address are moved together into one box.
questions.explain: Grouping related contact details is proximity.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Which principle does this change mainly apply?

Captions now start at the exact left edge of their photos.
questions.explain: Matching edges is alignment.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem: The Montserrat Heritage Circle wants a formal invitation for an Emancipation Day ceremony. The design must feel dignified, calm and orderly, with the foundation's crest at the top centre and the text mirrored around a central axis. Which type of balance BEST meets this brief?

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Keisha at the Island Pulse Media is reviewing a Carnival events app. Sort each note: is it about composition (what users see) or interaction (what users do)?

Is this note mainly about composition or interaction?

The J'ouvert headline is the largest element on the home screen.
questions.explain: Size and hierarchy decide what the eye sees first: composition.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this note mainly about composition or interaction?

The band photo is placed on a power point with a blurred crowd behind.
questions.explain: Placement and depth of field are composition tools.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this note mainly about composition or interaction?

The Buy button turns into a spinner, then a green tick, after it is tapped.
questions.explain: A response to the user's action is feedback: interaction.

questions.topic: Composition and principles of interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this note mainly about composition or interaction?

The Back arrow is in the same top-left corner on every screen.
questions.explain: Controls that work the same way everywhere are about consistency of interaction.

questions.explain: MP4 is the form the video takes. It needs a platform such as YouTube or Instagram to reach viewers.

questions.explain: PNG is an image format. The logo could appear on many platforms.

A Bahamian student finds a website claiming the island has no hurricane season. What is the best advice about search engines?
options: Trust it if it is the first result

Search engines only return verified facts

questions.stem: On a social platform, who mainly keeps the conversation moving?
options: The users who comment, react and share
questions.explain: The platform provides the space; its users keep the conversation moving through post, respond, share.

questions.stem: A seller in Antigua lists a used laptop on a classified-listing site. How is payment usually arranged?
options: Buyer and seller usually arrange payment between themselves
Payment is made through an app store
The site always processes the payment
questions.explain: Classified-listing platforms such as Craigslist often leave payment to buyers and sellers. Transaction-based marketplaces manage it through the site.

questions.stem: Which is an example of an app store beyond mobile devices?
options: A browser's catalogue of extensions and add-ons
questions.explain: Browsers such as Chrome and Firefox offer stores or catalogues for extensions and add-ons.

questions.explain: Crowdsourcing coordinates contributions from many people; infrastructure supplies servers, storage and networking.

questions.stem:
Malik at the Island Pulse Media is preparing files for a Spicemas promotion in Grenada. Answer each question.

Malik saves a poster as JPEG, opens it, edits it and saves again five times. The text edges look blotchy. Why?
options: JPEG converts the image to 256 colours
JPEG is lossy, so each re-save discards more data
JPEG reduces the resolution each time
questions.explain: This is generation loss. JPEG re-compresses and discards data on every save. Keep a lossless master (XCF, PSD or PNG) and export a JPEG once at the end.

questions.stem: An image uses 8 bits per pixel. How many colours can each pixel show?
questions.explain: 2 to the power of 8 is 256. That is why GIF and PNG-8 images are limited to 256 colours.

questions.stem: Which change would REDUCE file size the most for a web banner photo?
options: Scaling it from 4000 px wide to 1600 px wide and exporting as JPEG
Saving it as an uncompressed TIFF
questions.explain: Fewer pixels plus lossy compression gives a much smaller file. Adding an alpha channel or saving uncompressed makes files bigger.

questions.stem: A talking-head interview and a fast Carnival parade clip, both 1080p and one minute long, are exported at the same quality. Which is likely to be larger?
options: They will be exactly the same size
questions.explain: Inter-frame compression stores only the changes between frames. Fast movement means many changes, so more data is needed to keep the same quality.

questions.stem: Roughly how big is a raw 1920 by 1080 image at 24-bit colour?
questions.explain: 1920 x 1080 = 2,073,600 pixels; x 3 bytes = about 6.2 MB before compression.

questions.stem: Which pair are BOTH lossless?
questions.explain: PNG and ZIP rebuild the original data exactly. JPEG, MP3 and most MP4 video are lossy.

questions.stem:

A photo of sunset at Seven Mile Beach in Negril for a hotel's website gallery

questions.stem:
Which format suits this job best?

The Bayside Water Sports logo to place over a coloured website header

questions.stem:
Which format suits this job best?

A three-frame waving flag loop to embed in an Emancipation Day email newsletter
questions.explain: Most email programs do not play video, but they do play GIF animation. Three simple frames suit the 256-colour palette.

questions.stem:
Which format suits this job best?

A restaurant menu in Oranjestad that must print on A4 exactly as designed
questions.explain: PDF fixes the layout and embeds fonts, so it prints the same on any computer.

A screenshot of an app interface with small text, for a tutorial

questions.stem:
Which format suits this job best?

A product photo of a bottle of local pepper sauce for an Instagram post

questions.stem:
Which format suits this job best?

A 10-page SBA proposal with images and headings, to be submitted to the teacher
questions.explain: A PDF keeps headings, fonts and images in place whatever device the teacher uses to open it.

questions.stem:

questions.stem:
Keisha is recording a 30-second radio-style ad for Johnny Cake Corner in Portsmouth. Help her solve each problem.

Her waveform is flattened at the top and the meter flashes red. What has happened?
options: Clipping: the input was too loud
questions.explain: Clipping happens when the signal is louder than the maximum. The flattened peaks are distortion that cannot be repaired, so she must lower the input level and record again.

questions.stem: There is a constant air-conditioner hum behind her voice. What should she do first?
options: Select a few seconds of hum only, Get Noise Profile, then apply Noise Reduction
questions.explain: Noise Reduction learns the noise from a profile of room tone and removes it from the whole track. Normalising first would make the hum louder.

questions.stem: She wants the soca music to dip automatically whenever she speaks.
questions.explain: Auto Duck lowers one track (the music) when another track (the voice) has sound. The Envelope tool does the same thing by hand.

questions.stem: Her voice is clean but quiet. Which effect brings the loudest peak up to -1 dB?
questions.explain: Normalize raises (or lowers) the whole track so the loudest peak reaches the target, without clipping.

questions.stem: How should the music end so it does not stop abruptly?
options: Select the last 2 seconds and apply Fade Out
questions.explain: A fade out reduces the volume smoothly to silence, which sounds professional.

questions.stem: She needs to edit again next week. What should she save?
options: The .aup3 project file as the master, plus the exported MP3
questions.explain: The .aup3 project keeps the separate tracks and edits. An MP3 is a mixed, lossy file that is hard to re-edit.

questions.stem:

The master voice-over for the SBA ad, to be imported into the video editor

A weekly podcast episode about Barbados history for listeners on mobile data

Sound effects for Jerome's Android game built in Godot

questions.stem:
Keisha is learning manual camera settings before a shoot for the Bay Breeze Boutique on Young Street. Choose the best setting for each situation.

She wants the shop owner sharp and the busy street behind her softly blurred.
options: A wide aperture such as f/1.8
A narrow aperture such as f/11
questions.explain: A wide aperture gives a shallow depth of field, so the background blurs. This is perfect for interviews.

questions.stem: She is filming at 24 fps. Which shutter speed follows the 180-degree rule?
questions.explain: The 180-degree rule doubles the frame rate: 1/48 is the ideal, so 1/50 is the nearest standard setting. It gives natural-looking motion blur.

questions.stem: Her footage inside a dim Gros Islet restaurant is grainy. What is the best fix?
options: Add light, such as an LED panel, and lower the ISO
questions.explain: Grain comes from high ISO. Use the lowest ISO that works and add light rather than cranking ISO.

questions.stem: Under warm tungsten bulbs, faces look orange on camera.
options: Set the white balance manually to tungsten
questions.explain: White balance makes colours accurate for the light source. Matching it to tungsten removes the orange cast.

questions.stem: She wants slow-motion shots of a jet landing at Lynden Pindling International Airport.
options: Record at 120 fps and play back at 24 or 30 fps
questions.explain: High frame rates played back at a normal rate stretch time, giving smooth slow motion.

questions.stem: For a wide shot of Montego Bay from Fort Charles, everything from the rocks to the cruise ships must be sharp.
questions.explain: A narrow aperture gives a deep depth of field, which is ideal for landscapes.

questions.stem: The client may want a vertical crop of a landscape shot later in the edit.
options: Shoot in 4K so there is room to reframe
questions.explain: 4K allows reframing in post-production without losing too much detail.

Shoot her facing straight into the midday sun so her face is bright.

questions.stem:
Zara, creative director at Island Pulse Media, is reviewing animations for a Bahamas tourism campaign. Which principle is each animator using?

A cartoon pelican pulls its head back before diving into Nassau harbour.
questions.explain: The small backward move prepares the viewer for the dive. That is anticipation.

questions.stem: After the steel pan player stops, the long ribbons on his sleeves keep swinging, then settle.
questions.explain: Loose parts continuing to move after the body stops is follow through.

questions.stem: A ferry starts slowly, speeds up in the middle of the crossing, then slows before docking.
questions.explain: Gradual acceleration and deceleration is slow in and slow out (easing).

questions.stem: A swinging arm is checked frame by frame to make sure the hand follows a curved path.
questions.explain: Natural movements follow curves. Checking the path of the hand is checking arcs.

questions.stem: A character's jaw drops to the floor when she sees the price of a cruise ticket.
questions.explain: Pushing an expression beyond reality for clarity and humour is exaggeration.

questions.stem: The camera is placed side-on with a plain sky behind the character so the jump is easy to read.
questions.explain: Choosing angle and background so one idea reads clearly is staging.

questions.stem: While a fisherman hauls in his net (main action), he whistles and taps his foot.
questions.explain: Small supporting actions that add personality are secondary action, as long as they do not steal focus.

questions.stem: The Grenada Spice Studios must deliver a 10-second animated advert in which a mascot nutmeg waves, points to a logo and smiles, timed exactly to a voice-over. Which approach is MOST suitable, and why?
options: Straight-ahead, because the computer generates all the inbetweens.
Straight-ahead, because it always produces the smoothest motion.
Neither: a 10-second advert does not need any planning of poses.
Pose-to-pose, because key poses can be planned to match the voice-over and fit the fixed 10-second length.

questions.stem:
The Island Pulse Media has a list of jobs. Decide whether each is best done by hand, frame by frame, or with software tweening.

Which technique suits this job best?

A telecom company's logo sliding in and scaling up smoothly for a 5-second bumper.
questions.explain: Simple changes in position and scale between two keys are perfect for a motion or classic tween.

questions.stem:
Which technique suits this job best?

A crashing wave at Bathsheba with spray and foam changing shape every frame.
questions.explain: Chaotic, organic shapes need straight-ahead frame-by-frame drawing.

questions.stem:
Which technique suits this job best?

A circle morphing into a sun shape in a vector tool.
questions.explain: A shape tween in Animate (or Synfig) interpolates one vector shape into another.

questions.stem:
Which technique suits this job best?

A hand-drawn character crying, with tears and quivering lips.
questions.explain: Expressive acting with changing drawings is classic frame-by-frame work.

questions.stem:
Which technique suits this job best?

An infographic bar chart growing to show tourist arrivals at the airport.
questions.explain: Bars growing from one value to another are easily tweened with easing.

questions.stem:
Which technique suits this job best?

A cut-out puppet of a mocko jumbie whose limbs rotate at joints in Synfig.
questions.explain: Cut-out animation with bones relies on interpolation between waypoints.

questions.stem:
Which technique suits this job best?

Flames on a coal pot flickering under a pot of soup.
questions.explain: Fire changes shape unpredictably, so it is usually drawn straight ahead, frame by frame.

questions.stem:
Which technique suits this job best?

A rough pencil sketch animation made in Pencil2D with onion skin.
questions.explain: Pencil2D is built mainly for drawing each frame by hand.

questions.stem:
Answer these questions from the Island Pulse Media animation team.

A wind turbine on a hill in Curaçao must spin at a perfectly steady speed. Which interpolation?
questions.explain: Linear gives a constant rate of change, so the speed never eases in or out.

questions.stem: On an F-curve, the steepest section shows where the object is...
questions.explain: A steep slope means a large change in value per frame, which is high speed.

questions.stem: Malik wants to check his key poses with no inbetweens first. He sets interpolation to...
questions.explain: Stepped keys show only the poses, which is how animators block pose-to-pose.

questions.stem: In a walk cycle, the pose where the body is at its LOWEST point is the...
questions.explain: Just after contact the front leg bends to take the weight: the down pose.

questions.stem: In a walk cycle, both feet are on the ground and the legs are at their widest in the...
questions.explain: The contact pose has the heel striking and the back toe on the ground.

questions.stem: To make a 24-frame walk loop forever without adding more keys, he uses...
questions.explain: Cyclic extrapolation repeats the curve indefinitely.

questions.stem:
You are an intern at the Island Pulse Media. Zara needs a 15-second animated sting for an Emancipation Day community event post, due at 9 a.m. tomorrow. Make the best decisions.

The sting has a 3D conch shell that bounces onto the screen and reveals the event title. How do you begin?
options: Plan key poses and timing on paper or in a quick storyboard, then block them in Blender with stepped keys.
Start animating straight ahead from frame 1 and see where it ends up.

questions.stem: Your blocked keys look good. When you switch to Bezier, the shell floats and drifts into the floor between bounces. What do you do?
options: Add more and more keyframes on every frame until it looks right.
Open the Graph Editor, set the contact keys to Vector handles and add squash on the contact frames.
Switch everything to Linear so it moves evenly.

questions.stem: It is 10 p.m. A full Cycles render would take about 8 hours on the office computer. How do you render?
options: Render straight to an animated GIF in Cycles at full quality.
Render in Eevee at 1080 by 1920 (it will be posted as a vertical story), 30 fps, as a PNG sequence, then convert to MP4 H.264.

questions.stem: The render is done. How do you hand it over?
options: Name it IPM_EmancipationSting_v1_1080x1920.mp4, upload it with the .blend file to the shared Drive folder and message Zara with the settings used.
Email only the MP4 called final.mp4 and delete the project files to save space.

One member in a rural village cannot join video calls because her data plan is too expensive.

questions.stem: Week 4: one member, Devon, has not completed his storyboard task and is not replying in the group chat. How do you respond?
options: Send Devon a polite private message asking if he is okay, and offer to agree a new deadline or adjust tasks; inform the teacher if it continues.

Post in the group chat: "DEVON IS LAZY. Do your work!!!"

questions.stem: Devon explains his home Internet was cut off after a power problem. He can use the school library Wi-Fi only at lunch. How do you adapt?

Insist that all work happens in live evening video calls only.

questions.stem: Two weeks before submission, how do you show evidence of collaboration?
options: Write one sentence: "We all worked together well."
Include dated Trello screenshots, version history, comment threads and meeting minutes, with captions and private details removed.

questions.stem: The Antigua Youth Film Collective has members on three islands, several of whom use only mid-range phones with prepaid data. They need to share storyboards and feedback over a month. Which choice is BEST justified?

A Padlet board, because it is browser-based, works on phones, lets members post images and comments at any time, and needs little data compared with live video calls.
Emailing large image attachments to everyone, because email is universal.
Daily two-hour live video calls, because face-to-face discussion is always best.

A Trinidad snack brand leaves giant foam "doubles" on park benches in Port of Spain with a QR code on each one.
