questions.stem:
Keisha is preparing a report for the Antigua Sailing Week Fan Zone campaign. Use the formulas to answer.

A post reached 5,000 people and received 400 engagements. What is the engagement rate (by reach)?
questions.explain: 400 ÷ 5,000 × 100 = 8%. Engagement rate compares interactions with the people reached.

questions.stem: An ad had 20,000 impressions and 300 clicks. What is the CTR?
questions.explain: 300 ÷ 20,000 × 100 = 1.5%. CTR divides clicks by impressions.

questions.stem: 300 people clicked through and 45 bought tickets. What is the conversion rate?
questions.explain: 45 ÷ 300 × 100 = 15%. Conversion rate divides goal actions by clicks.

questions.stem: One person saw the same Story three times. How does this affect reach and impressions?
questions.explain: Reach counts unique people (1); impressions count every display (3).

questions.stem: The objective is "sell 500 fan zone passes by 20 April". Which is the most important KPI?
questions.explain: The KPI must match the objective. Likes and followers are vanity metrics here; sales are the conversion that matters.

questions.stem: Keisha wants to know which of three influencers produced the most sales. The best tracking method is...
options: give each influencer a unique discount code or UTM link
questions.explain: Unique codes or tagged links tie each sale to the source that produced it.

questions.stem: An influencer offers to post about the app without labelling it as paid, "so it looks natural". How does Keisha respond?
options: Insist on clear disclosure (#ad or the paid partnership label) in the written agreement.
Accept, because unlabelled posts get more engagement.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: Before redesigning, the team interviews tour guides and visitors about what frustrates them.
questions.explain: User research and testing to understand needs and preferences is user-centric design.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: The tour company uses empathise, define, ideate, prototype and test to improve its whole booking process, not just the app.
questions.explain: The handout notes that design thinking is now applied to business processes to foster innovation.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: The owner asks why accessibility matters. Which reason is correct?
options: It removes the need for testing
It makes the app cheaper to host
It is often required by law, for example WCAG standards
questions.explain: The three reasons are: more people can use it, it is inclusive and fair, and it is often required by law (WCAG).

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Zara at the Island Pulse Media keeps a notebook of changes she sees in design across the Caribbean. Sort each note by the factor it best illustrates.

Which factor is the main driver?

Hundreds of near-identical restaurant menus in Barbados use the same free template.
questions.explain: Standardised, interchangeable design products are a sign of commoditisation.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Which factor is the main driver?

The same airline booking flow must work on a phone, a tablet, a laptop and an airport kiosk.
questions.explain: Technology on every kind of screen drives responsive, multi-device design.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Which factor is the main driver?

A Belize student makes a professional animation with Blender, which costs nothing.
questions.explain: Free software lowers cost, so more people can create.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Which factor is the main driver?

A government website adds captions, alt text and a high-contrast mode for visually impaired users.
questions.explain: Designing for people with disabilities is accessibility.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Which factor is the main driver?

Basic website themes now sell for a few dollars and buyers choose mainly on price.
questions.explain: When buyers see little difference and choose on price, the product has been commoditised.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Which factor is the main driver?

Smartwatches, smart TVs and car dashboards all need interfaces readable at a glance.
questions.explain: Screens everywhere in daily life illustrate pervasiveness.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Which factor is the main driver?

Cheaper mid-range phones with good cameras lead to more vertical, phone-shot ads.
questions.explain: Lower device cost (affordability) changed the style of video content.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Which factor is the main driver?

Free public Wi-Fi in a town square lets more residents use an online heritage guide.
questions.explain: Improving access to technology widens who can use digital content, which a strong answer adds to the accessibility definition.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Jerome is reviewing app designs for Caribbean Beats music app. Identify the trend or evaluate it.

A now-playing panel is semi-transparent with the album art blurred behind it and a thin white border.
questions.explain: Translucency, background blur and a light border are the signs of glassmorphism.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: Buttons look softly raised from a pale grey background, with a light shadow top-left and a dark shadow bottom-right.
questions.explain: Two soft shadows on a same-colour background create the extruded look of neumorphism.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: Users can switch to light text on a dark grey background for late-night listening.
questions.explain: Light content on a dark background, chosen by the user, is dark mode.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: Testers with low vision cannot tell whether a neumorphic play button is pressed. What is the main problem?
questions.explain: Neumorphism relies on subtle shadows, so contrast is low and state changes are hard to see.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: Which is the BEST practice for a dark mode palette?
options: dark grey background with softened colours and good contrast
pure black with fully saturated neon text
questions.explain: Dark grey reduces harsh contrast and smearing, while softened colours stay readable and pass contrast checks.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: The Dominica Waitukubuli Trail app needs to confirm instantly when a hiker taps "Save trail for offline use", so that users know the download has started without opening a new screen. Which design trend is the BEST fit?
options: Dark mode: switch the whole app to a dark theme.
Immersive UI: a full-screen 3D fly-through of the whole trail.
Neumorphism: make the save button look softly raised.
A micro-interaction: the save icon fills with a small progress animation and the phone gives a short vibration.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: An AI mood-board image shows festival-goers in clichéd, inaccurate "tropical" costume that does not reflect Haitian culture. What next?
options: Reject it, and use your own photographs from local events, with permission, as the visual reference.
Keep it; tourists expect that look.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem: The client asks how AI was used. How do you respond?
options: Say no AI was used at all.
Disclose honestly: AI helped with early mood boards; all final artwork and photography is original.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Jerome at the Island Pulse Media has received eight project ideas. Sort each one.

Is this augmented reality or virtual reality?

Point a phone at Brimstone Hill Fortress and see the original walls rebuilt on screen.
questions.explain: Digital content is layered over the real ruins, so it is AR.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this augmented reality or virtual reality?

Wear a headset and explore a fully virtual coral reef without leaving the classroom.
questions.explain: The real world is replaced by a virtual one: VR.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this augmented reality or virtual reality?

An Instagram filter that adds Carnival feathers to your selfie.
questions.explain: Face filters add graphics on top of the live camera view: AR.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this augmented reality or virtual reality?

A fully simulated cockpit for training pilots at a flight school in Trinidad.
questions.explain: An immersive simulated environment is VR.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this augmented reality or virtual reality?

See how a new sofa would look in your living room through the phone camera.
questions.explain: A virtual object is placed in the real room: AR.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this augmented reality or virtual reality?

A 360-degree headset tour of a Barbados hotel suite before booking.
questions.explain: The viewer is immersed in a recorded or virtual space, not their real surroundings: VR.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this augmented reality or virtual reality?

Arrows appear on the live street view to guide you to the Basseterre ferry.
questions.explain: Directions overlaid on the real street are AR.

questions.topic: Trends and developments in visual and interactive design
questions.stem:
Is this augmented reality or virtual reality?

A virtual concert hall where fans with headsets watch a soca artist perform as avatars.
questions.explain: Users are inside a fully virtual environment: VR.

questions.stem:
Jerome is reviewing a CAPE group's proposal for a St. Kitts bus-times app. Answer each question.

"Most of our users use Android phones on prepaid data plans." This is an example of...
questions.explain: Devices and data plans describe technology use, which is technographics.

questions.stem: "Our users value saving time and dislike waiting in the sun without information." This is...
questions.explain: Values, attitudes and frustrations are psychographics and pain points.

questions.stem: The group lists two existing bus apps from other islands and notes what each lacks. This is...
questions.explain: Studying existing products and their weaknesses is competitor analysis, which reveals the gap.

questions.stem: "Heavy rain and hurricanes could stop buses and make the app's data wrong." In SWOT this is a...
questions.explain: It is external and harmful, so it is a threat. Weaknesses are internal to the team or product.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST data capture instrument for this proposal?
options: asking two friends what they think
a Google Forms survey of bus users at the Basseterre bus terminal, with 10 clear questions
copying statistics from an unrelated country
questions.explain: A designed survey of real users gives relevant evidence and earns the SBA research marks.

questions.stem:
This is the "Funding a Digital Media Project" activity. Each card is a statement about one of seven funding categories: crowdfunding, grants, angel investors, loans, venture capital, sponsorships and partnerships, and bootstrapping. Is it a benefit or a disadvantage for the creator?

Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Crowdfunding: it can build a loyal audience early and prove demand before launch.
questions.explain: Backers are your first fans, and their pledges are evidence that people want the product: a benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Crowdfunding: it needs heavy promotion and frequent updates, and campaigns can fail to reach the goal.
questions.explain: A campaign is a lot of marketing work with no guarantee of success: a disadvantage.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Grants: they provide money without giving up ownership or taking on debt.
questions.explain: Non-repayable money that costs you no shares is a major benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Grants: they are competitive and demand detailed proposals, timelines and reporting.
questions.explain: Many applicants, long forms and strict reports take time and may still end in rejection: a disadvantage.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Angel investors: they often add mentoring and industry connections along with the money.
questions.explain: Advice and contacts from an experienced investor can be worth as much as the cash: a benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Loans: you keep full ownership and creative control of the project.
questions.explain: A lender wants repayment, not shares or a say in your content: a benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Loans: repayments add financial pressure and are due even if income is delayed.
questions.explain: The bank still expects its monthly payment if the series launches late: a disadvantage.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Venture capital: it typically requires significant equity and board or decision-making power.
questions.explain: Giving away a large share and control of direction is the main drawback of VC.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Sponsorships and partnerships: creative choices may need to follow sponsor guidelines.
questions.explain: A sponsor protects its brand, which can limit what you say or show: a disadvantage.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a disadvantage?

Bootstrapping: it preserves complete ownership and creative freedom.
questions.explain: Using your own money means nobody else owns or directs the project: a benefit.

questions.stem:
Keisha at the Island Pulse Media is explaining funding offers to a new client, the Salt Pond Animation Studio in Sandy Ground, Anguilla. Sort each offer.

Is this debt or equity?

A local bank lends XCD 20,000 for animation computers, repaid monthly over three years at an agreed interest rate.
questions.explain: Borrowed money repaid with interest is debt. The bank owns no part of the studio.

questions.stem:
Is this debt or equity?

A credit union lends to the studio, secured against its camera and lighting equipment.
questions.explain: A secured loan uses assets as collateral, but it is still borrowing: debt.

questions.stem:
Is this debt or equity?

An angel investor puts in USD 30,000 in return for 10% of the studio's shares.
questions.explain: Money in exchange for a share of ownership is equity.

questions.stem:
Is this debt or equity?

A venture capital firm invests a large sum, takes 30% ownership and a seat on the board.
questions.explain: VC is equity funding: a big stake plus influence over direction.

questions.stem:
Is this debt or equity?

300 people each lend a small amount through an online platform and are repaid with interest.
questions.explain: This is debt crowdfunding (peer-to-peer lending): many small loans, still debt.

questions.stem:
Is this debt or equity?

Fans invest through an equity crowdfunding platform and each receive a small share of the company.
questions.explain: Equity crowdfunding gives backers shares, so it is equity.

questions.stem:
Is this debt or equity?

The owner's uncle lends XCD 5,000 under a written agreement to be repaid within a year.
questions.explain: FFF money can be either type. This one must be repaid, so it is debt.

questions.stem:
Is this debt or equity?

The owner's aunt gives XCD 5,000 in exchange for a 5% share of the studio.
questions.explain: FFF money in exchange for ownership is equity.

questions.stem:
Is this debt or equity?

A short-term bridge loan pays the voice actors until a grant arrives, then is paid back.
questions.explain: Bridge funding is temporary borrowing that is repaid: debt.

questions.stem:
Keisha at the Island Pulse Media is advising clients on how to fund their projects. Sort each description.

Which source of funding is described?

A ministry awards XCD 15,000 for a youth culture documentary; it does not need to be repaid but receipts must be submitted.
questions.explain: Public money for a project that meets public goals, with reporting rules: a government grant.

questions.stem:
Which source of funding is described?

420 people each pledge between USD 5 and USD 100 on Kickstarter to fund a Caribbean folklore animation.
questions.explain: Many small online pledges from the public is crowdfunding.

questions.stem:
Which source of funding is described?

A beverage company pays for the stage screens at a festival in return for its logo on every video.
questions.explain: Money in return for visibility is sponsorship.

questions.stem:
Which source of funding is described?

A retired businesswoman invests USD 50,000 in a student's app start-up for 15% of the company.
questions.explain: Personal money for a share of ownership (equity) is angel investment.

questions.stem:
Which source of funding is described?

Supporters receive rewards such as stickers, a credit in the film or an early download, depending on how much they pledge.
questions.explain: Reward tiers are a typical feature of crowdfunding campaigns.

questions.stem:
Which source of funding is described?

A mobile network provides free data for viewers of a learning app, and its name appears on the splash screen.
questions.explain: In-kind support in exchange for brand visibility is sponsorship.

questions.stem:
Which source of funding is described?

The applicant must complete a formal application form and meet a fixed deadline set by a public department.
questions.explain: Formal applications to a public department are the typical route to a government grant.

questions.stem:
Which source of funding is described?

The investor also mentors the team and joins its board of directors.
questions.explain: Angel investors often bring advice and contacts, and may want a say in decisions.

questions.stem:
Zara and Malik at the Island Pulse Media want to make a six-episode animated web series, Salt Pond Tales, retelling Caribbean folk stories for children. The budget is XCD 45,000. You are advising them on funding.

Zara asks for your first funding step. What do you recommend?
options: Apply to a CARICOM-region arts council or cultural grant programme with the full proposal, budget and timeline, and ask a local business to sponsor the launch.
Borrow the full XCD 45,000 as an unsecured, high-interest loan, even though no income is expected until the series is finished.
Plan an IPO on a regional stock exchange to raise the whole amount.

questions.stem: The grant panel awards XCD 25,000, restricted to animation and voice talent. Bay Street Bakehouse sponsors XCD 5,000 for its logo at the end of each episode. XCD 15,000 is still needed. Keisha suggests crowdfunding. Which campaign do you plan?
options: A rewards-based Kickstarter campaign with a realistic XCD 15,000 target, a 60-second trailer, reward tiers (name in the credits, sticker pack, early access) and weekly updates.
A Kickstarter campaign with an XCD 60,000 target "to be safe", promoted with one post.

questions.stem: The campaign succeeds, but the grant payment is delayed by two months and the voice actors must be paid now. What do you do?
options: Arrange short-term bridge funding, such as a small credit union loan, repay it when the grant arrives and add the interest to the budget.
Accept an angel investor's offer of XCD 10,000 for 40% of the rights to the series.

questions.stem: The grant arrives. Malik suggests using some of it to pay the office rent and boost social media posts. How do you respond?
options: No: the grant is restricted to animation and voice talent. Pay rent and promotion from unrestricted money, such as the sponsor fee, and keep receipts for the grant report.
Yes: the funder will probably not check.

questions.stem: A group is pitching the Tobago Reef Watch app to a panel of local sponsors. They have 10 minutes. Which slide design is MOST effective for presenting their survey results?
options: Five different charts on one slide, each in different colours and fonts, to show how much work was done.
A slide with the full questionnaire and every response pasted in 12-point text.
One slide with a bold headline ("82% of divers want live reef updates"), one clear bar chart in brand colours, and the source of the data in small text.
A slide with a dramatic stock photo of the sea and no data at all.

questions.stem:
Your CAPE group is pitching an app, Market Day KY, that lists local vendors at the George Town farmers' market, to a panel that includes a possible sponsor and an angel investor. Make the decisions.

You have 8 minutes. How do you open?
options: By reading your full proposal document aloud from the first page.
With a hook: a 15-second phone video of a vendor saying sales dropped because tourists cannot find her stall, plus one survey statistic.

questions.stem: The sponsor asks, "Why should we believe vendors and visitors will use this?" How do you answer?
options: Show your market analysis: survey of 60 visitors and 25 vendors, competitor gaps, and the persona slide.

questions.stem: The angel investor asks about money. Which budget slide do you show?
options: A clear itemised summary by category (production, equipment, software, personnel, hosting, marketing) with a 10% contingency, total in KYD and USD, and your exact ask.
A single line: "Total cost: about KYD 10,000, give or take."

questions.stem: The investor offers money in return for 40% of the app. You only wanted sponsorship. What do you say?
options: Thank them, explain the difference between equity and sponsorship, and ask for time to consider and compare options.
Accept on the spot to secure the money.

questions.stem:
Keisha at the Island Pulse Media is explaining digital publishing platforms to a client. Name the key feature, from the list of eight, that each situation shows.

A Grenada author sees a dashboard showing how many readers finished chapter 3 and where they live.
questions.explain: Tracking engagement and audience data is analytics. Creators use it to improve content and marketing.

questions.stem: A Jamaican cookbook writer sets a price of US$4.99 and earns a royalty on every download.
questions.explain: Earning money from content through sales, subscriptions or ads is monetisation.

questions.stem: A Dominican student publishes her novel without being accepted by any publishing house.
questions.explain: Publishing independently, without a traditional publishing house, is self-publishing.

questions.stem: The same e-book opens on a Kindle, an Android phone, an iPad and a laptop.
questions.explain: Reading on many kinds of devices is the accessibility feature.

questions.stem: A Barbados history e-book includes embedded video of Crop Over and links to museum archives.
questions.explain: Multimedia and hyperlinks that go beyond print are interactivity.

questions.stem: A Belize travel guide is bought by readers in Japan, Germany and Canada on its first day, with no shipping.
questions.explain: Reaching a worldwide audience without physical distribution channels is global reach.

questions.stem: A platform offers templates to lay out text, add images and build a quiz at the end of each chapter.
questions.explain: Tools for creating and formatting content are the content creation feature.

questions.stem:
Clients are calling the Island Pulse Media. Choose the best option for each.

An Ocho Rios restaurant owner with no coding skills wants a beautiful menu site, hosting included, set up this week.
questions.explain: Hosted drag-and-drop builders suit beginners who need speed and included hosting. Joomla needs technical skill, and IngramSpark is for books.

questions.stem: A Guyanese historian wants her e-book in Apple Books, Kobo and Barnes & Noble without uploading three times.
questions.explain: Draft2Digital is an aggregator: one upload, many stores. KDP reaches only Amazon.

questions.stem: A Jamaican news start-up needs a flexible, open-source site with plugins and several editors with different roles.
questions.explain: Self-hosted WordPress is open-source, has a huge plugin library and supports user roles such as editor and author.

questions.stem: A Barbadian poet wants her printed collection listed in bookshop and library catalogues.
questions.explain: IngramSpark distributes print-on-demand books through the network that supplies bookshops and libraries.

questions.stem: A Trinidad author wants the biggest single e-book store and does not want to buy an ISBN for the Kindle edition.
questions.explain: KDP is the largest e-book store and assigns its own ASIN, so a Kindle e-book does not need a purchased ISBN.

questions.stem: A Curaçao community group wants a multilingual site (Papiamentu, Dutch, English) and has a volunteer developer.
questions.explain: Joomla has strong multilingual features and suits a team with some technical skill.

questions.stem:
Maya at the Island Pulse Media is converting a stack of client projects into e-books. Decide the best layout for each.

Should this be published as reflowable or fixed layout?

A 300-page novel about a family in San Fernando.
questions.explain: Text-heavy novels should reflow so readers can resize text on any screen.

questions.stem:
Should this be published as reflowable or fixed layout?

A children's picture book where the text sits inside the illustrations.
questions.explain: Text placed on artwork must stay in position, so fixed layout is needed.

questions.stem:
Should this be published as reflowable or fixed layout?

A comic about a Carnival superhero, panel by panel.
questions.explain: Comic panels depend on exact placement: fixed layout.

questions.stem:
Should this be published as reflowable or fixed layout?

A collection of short essays on Caribbean identity.
questions.explain: Plain text suits reflowable layout and screen readers.

questions.stem:
Should this be published as reflowable or fixed layout?

A recipe book for johnny cakes and coconut tarts with photos beside each step.
questions.explain: Designed spreads with photos beside steps keep their meaning only in fixed layout.

questions.stem:
Should this be published as reflowable or fixed layout?

A poetry collection where readers with low vision need very large text.
questions.explain: Reflowable text can be enlarged without breaking the page, which supports accessibility.

questions.stem:
Should this be published as reflowable or fixed layout?

A replica of a printed tourism magazine with full-page adverts.
questions.explain: A magazine replica must look like the print design, so it is fixed layout (or a PDF).

questions.stem:
Should this be published as reflowable or fixed layout?

A guide to CAPE study skills that students read on phones.
questions.explain: Small phone screens need text that reflows.

questions.stem:
Jerome at the Island Pulse Media is building a slide for a school library talk. Sort each statement about e-books.

Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

One e-reader can hold thousands of books for a long trip to Guyana.
questions.explain: Portability (one device, many books) is a key advantage.

questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

The device battery dies during a power cut after a storm.
questions.explain: E-books require a power source, a real problem during outages.

questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

A history e-book embeds video of the 1848 Emancipation commemoration and audio interviews.
questions.explain: Digital convergence of text, video and audio is an advantage print cannot offer.

questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

Reading on a bright screen for hours gives a student tired eyes.
questions.explain: Eye strain is one of the listed disadvantages.

questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

A reader loses her whole library when she loses access to her account.
questions.explain: Some e-books are device or account specific, so access can be lost.

questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

The author fixes an error and every reader gets the updated edition.
questions.explain: E-books can be easily updated without reprinting costs.

questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

A student with low vision makes the text larger and it reflows.
questions.explain: Rearranging the flow of text supports accessibility.

questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

A reader's account is hacked and her purchases are stolen.
questions.explain: E-books and accounts can be hacked, a security disadvantage.

questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of e-books?

Some readers who love hard copies lose motivation to read on a screen.
questions.explain: E-books are not suited to all types of readers.

questions.stem:
Keisha is preparing a social media explainer for the Island Pulse Media. Sort each example into the correct stage of the Web.

Which stage of the Web does this example best represent?

A 1998 hotel website with one static page of text and a phone number.
questions.explain: Static, read-only pages with no user interaction are Web 1.0.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the Web does this example best represent?

Visitors post TikTok reviews of a Negril beach bar.
questions.explain: User-generated content and sharing are the heart of Web 2.0.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the Web does this example best represent?

A digital wallet lets a Belize artist sell and prove ownership of digital art on a blockchain.
questions.explain: Decentralised ownership on a blockchain is the Web3 idea of Web 3.0.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the Web does this example best represent?

Students edit a Wikipedia article about Emancipation Day.
questions.explain: Collaborative, read-write editing is Web 2.0.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the Web does this example best represent?

An early web directory where an editor lists links by hand.
questions.explain: Hand-built lists for reading only belong to Web 1.0.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the Web does this example best represent?

A search engine understands "cheap ferry to Anguilla tomorrow" and shows times and prices from tagged data.
questions.explain: Machines understanding meaning from structured data is the Semantic Web side of Web 3.0.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the Web does this example best represent?

A Trinidad blogger gets comments and shares on every post.
questions.explain: Two-way interaction through comments and shares is Web 2.0.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the Web does this example best represent?

An AI assistant personalises a news feed using linked data about the user's interests.
questions.explain: Intelligent, personalised and machine-readable services point to Web 3.0.

questions.stem: The Kingston studio Yaad Games releases a free online game in which thousands of players explore a shared Caribbean island at the same time. Every month the studio publishes a new story chapter, and players can build and share their own levels. Which statement BEST explains why this is an example of digital publishing?
options: Thousands of people play it, so it is a website.
Content is distributed online, published in ongoing updates and includes user-generated levels shared with other players.
It is free, so it must be a form of publishing.
It uses graphics, and anything with graphics is digital publishing.

questions.stem:
You are working with Zara at the Island Pulse Media. A retired teacher from Spanish Town has written an illustrated history of Emancipation Day in Jamaica and wants it read across the region and the diaspora. Make the best publishing decisions.

The book has about 80 pages of text and 20 photographs with captions. Most of her readers will use phones. Which format do you recommend first?
options: A scanned PDF of the printed pages.
A reflowable EPUB 3 with alt text for every photograph.

questions.stem: She wants the book in Apple Books, Kobo, Google Play Books and Barnes & Noble, but has little time. How should she distribute it?
options: Email the file to readers who ask for it.
Upload once through an aggregator such as Draft2Digital, and use KDP for Amazon.
Post the full book free on her Facebook page.

questions.stem: Before upload, she asks about ISBNs and metadata. What do you advise?
options: Use one ISBN for every format and leave the description blank so readers are curious.
Get separate ISBNs for the e-book and any print edition, and write a keyword-rich description with categories such as Caribbean history.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Jerome is quizzing interns at the Island Pulse Media before they start the Caribbean Roots podcast.

The word "podcast" blends which two words?
questions.explain: Podcast blends "iPod" and "broadcast", from the era when episodes were loaded onto iPods.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: What lets podcast episodes download automatically?
questions.explain: RSS (or Atom) feeds tell apps that a new episode exists so they can fetch it automatically.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: A video podcast is called a...
questions.explain: Video podcasts are also called vodcasts.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: What software checks feeds for new episodes and downloads them?
options: An aggregator (feed reader or podcast app)
questions.explain: Aggregators, today usually podcast apps, check subscribed feeds for new episodes.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: Weekly interviews with Grenadian cocoa farmers fit which use of a podcast?
questions.explain: In-depth conversations with guests and experts are the interview use.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: Where should a podcast preview the next episode?
options: In the first line of the introduction
questions.explain: The conclusion summarises key points, gives a call to action and previews upcoming episodes.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: What makes a podcast different from an ordinary audio file on a website?
options: It can be subscribed to and updates automatically
questions.explain: Automatic delivery through a subscription feed is the key distinction.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Keisha has a pile of production notes for two projects by Island Pulse Media: a filmed host video and an audio slideshow. Sort each note into the right project.

Which project does this note belong to?

Check the host's yellow top against the background at Fort James.
questions.explain: Dressing and background balance matter when viewers see the presenter.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which project does this note belong to?

Arrange the 15 photos on a storyboard before writing narration.
questions.explain: Visual sequencing of photos before writing is an audio slideshow technique.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which project does this note belong to?

Clip the mic to the shirt so it does not block the face.
questions.explain: Microphones must not block the speaker's face on camera.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which project does this note belong to?

Slow the narration so each photo has time to register.
questions.explain: Pacing control lets images and sound work together.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which project does this note belong to?

Keep cue cards in order and slide each one away discreetly.
questions.explain: Cue cards support an on-camera presenter.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which project does this note belong to?

Choose a calm voice tone for a hurricane remembrance story.
questions.explain: Voice tone selection matches narration to the emotional tone of the images.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which project does this note belong to?

Work on posture, eye contact and deportment.
questions.explain: Deportment is visible only when the presenter is on screen.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which project does this note belong to?

Record the voice first, then lay out the images in the editor.
questions.explain: Voice-first is a flexible workflow for audio slideshows.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Maya and Malik are planning several projects for the Island Pulse Media. Decide which tool each task needs.

Which planning tool fits this task best?

Sketching the eight shots of a 30-second ad for the Heineken Regatta, with camera angles.
questions.explain: Shot-by-shot visual planning with angles is a storyboard.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which planning tool fits this task best?

Writing the host's words and interview questions for a podcast episode.
questions.explain: The words to be spoken are planned in a script.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which planning tool fits this task best?

Grey boxes showing where the menu, hero image and booking button go on a hotel home page.
questions.explain: A low-fidelity layout of structure only is a wireframe.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which planning tool fits this task best?

A full-colour design of the app home screen with the real logo and photos, for client approval.
questions.explain: A high-fidelity static design that shows the final look is a mock-up.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which planning tool fits this task best?

Narration lines beside shot descriptions for a tourism video.
questions.explain: A two-column audio-visual script pairs narration with shots.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which planning tool fits this task best?

Frames showing the order of photos in an audio slideshow about Emancipation Day.
questions.explain: Sequencing images visually is storyboarding.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which planning tool fits this task best?

A quick black-and-white layout of a blog post page drawn in Balsamiq.
questions.explain: Balsamiq is designed for quick, low-fidelity wireframes.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which planning tool fits this task best?

Showing a client exactly how an Instagram post will look with brand colours and fonts.
questions.explain: Showing the final visual design is a mock-up.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Maya is helping several Trinidadian clients choose a web authoring tool. Sort each tool or description into its type.

Which type of web authoring tool is this?

Visual Studio Code: typing HTML and CSS for a San Fernando restaurant menu page.
questions.explain: VS Code is a text (code) editor: you write the HTML and CSS yourself.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which type of web authoring tool is this?

Notepad++: fixing a broken link tag by hand.
questions.explain: Notepad++ is a basic text editor for editing code directly.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which type of web authoring tool is this?

Sublime Text: editing a JavaScript file for a photo gallery.
questions.explain: Sublime Text is a text editor for writing code line by line.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which type of web authoring tool is this?

Adobe Dreamweaver design view: dragging an image into place and seeing the page update.
questions.explain: Dreamweaver offers a visual WYSIWYG view that writes the code for you.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which type of web authoring tool is this?

WordPress Gutenberg: adding a heading block and an image block to a blog post.
questions.explain: Gutenberg is a visual block editor: what you see is what you get.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which type of web authoring tool is this?

Joomla: a heritage foundation site with user accounts, menus and many articles.
questions.explain: Joomla is a CMS for managing a whole site's content.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which type of web authoring tool is this?

Drupal: a large, structured site for a Caribbean university with many editors.
questions.explain: Drupal is a powerful CMS suited to complex sites.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Which type of web authoring tool is this?

WordPress with a theme and plugins: a Bequia guesthouse posting weekly news.
questions.explain: WordPress as a whole is a CMS: themes, plugins and content management.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
Jerome is building an app for Antigua Sailing Club and keeps asking copyright questions. Help him.

Jerome writes original code for the app tonight. When is it protected by copyright?
options: Only after he adds the © symbol
Only after he registers it with an IP office
Automatically, as soon as it is written and saved
questions.explain: Copyright is automatic once an original work is fixed in a form, such as a saved file. Registration and © are optional.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: He wants to name the app "Sail Away". Can copyright protect the name?
options: No, titles and short names are not protected by copyright; a trademark may protect them
questions.explain: Copyright does not protect titles or short phrases. Brand names are protected by trademark registration.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: Which international agreement means his app is protected in Canada and the UK without registering there?
questions.explain: The Berne Convention gives automatic protection in all member countries.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: The Berne Convention minimum term of copyright for most works is...
options: until the author stops selling the work
life of the author plus 50 years
questions.explain: Berne sets a minimum of life plus 50 years. Many countries go further, such as life plus 70.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: He finds a 19th-century engraving of English Harbour whose artist died over 150 years ago. It is most likely...
questions.explain: With the creator long dead, copyright has expired and the work is in the public domain. A modern photograph of it could still carry its own copyright, so check the source.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: The club wants a soca track in the app trailer. Who can usually license it?
options: Any YouTube user who uploaded it
The rights holder or a collecting society such as COTT
questions.explain: Rights holders, often through collecting societies, license music. An uploader on YouTube rarely owns the rights.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: A CAPE student in Port of Spain is producing a promotional video for the Maracas Bay food truck. She uses a full three-minute hit soca song as the soundtrack, credits the artist in the description and says it is "fair use because I am a student". Which statement BEST evaluates her position?
options: It is likely infringement: Trinidad and Tobago applies fair dealing for listed purposes, and using a whole song in a commercial promotion fits none of them, even with credit.
It is fair use because she credited the artist.
It is legal because the song is on YouTube, so it is public.
It is legal because students are exempt from copyright law.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem:
You are a junior creator at Island Pulse Media. The Spicemas Youth Troupe in Grenada needs a 30-second promotional video and a blog post in three days. Make the right authoring decisions.

Zara asks how you will start. The client's brief says: "Show young people that Carnival is about culture and creativity, not just partying." What do you do first?
options: Start filming random party footage at a Spicemas fete tonight and decide later.
Brainstorm concepts against the brief, then storyboard the 30-second video and outline the blog post.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: Your concept shows troupe members designing costumes, practising steelpan and talking about their grandparents' Carnival memories. You need music. Malik suggests a famous international chart hit. What do you choose?
options: Ask the troupe's steelpan players to record an original piece, or license a local soca track from the rights holder.
Use the chart hit and credit the artist in the caption.

questions.topic: Authoring digital content in a Caribbean context
questions.stem: For the blog post you want to include a beautiful photograph of last year's parade that you found online. What do you do?
options: Check the licence. If it is CC BY, use it with full attribution; if not, contact the photographer for permission or use your own photo.
Use it because it is on Google Images, so it is free.
Copy it and write the caption as if you took it.

questions.stem:
The Island Pulse Media is designing a website for the Mango Lane Café on Fort Street. Sort each item from the project folder.

Is this a low-fidelity or a high-fidelity prototype?

A pencil sketch of the home page on printer paper, with boxes marked "photo" and "menu".
questions.explain: Paper, pencil and placeholder boxes are the signs of a low-fidelity prototype.

questions.stem:
Is this a low-fidelity or a high-fidelity prototype?

A Figma file where clicking "Order now" slides to a checkout screen with the café's real logo.
questions.explain: Real branding plus working interactions make this high-fidelity.

questions.stem:
Is this a low-fidelity or a high-fidelity prototype?

Sticky notes on a whiteboard, each one a page, moved around during a team meeting.
questions.explain: Sticky notes are quick, cheap and rough, which is low-fidelity.

questions.stem:
Is this a low-fidelity or a high-fidelity prototype?

A grey-box Balsamiq wireframe with hand-drawn style lines and no colour.
questions.explain: Balsamiq deliberately looks sketchy so people focus on structure, not style. That is low-fidelity.

questions.stem:
Is this a low-fidelity or a high-fidelity prototype?

A clickable mobile prototype using the café's brand colours, photos of johnny cakes and the final fonts.
questions.explain: Final colours, images and fonts with clickable links are high-fidelity.

questions.stem:
Is this a low-fidelity or a high-fidelity prototype?

Paper screens that Zara swaps by hand while a customer "taps" them with a finger.
questions.explain: This is paper prototyping. A person acts as the computer, which is still low-fidelity.

questions.stem:
Is this a low-fidelity or a high-fidelity prototype?

A prototype with smart-animate transitions that the developer will inspect for exact spacing values.
questions.explain: Detailed spacing, transitions and developer handover belong to high-fidelity work.

questions.stem:
Is this a low-fidelity or a high-fidelity prototype?

A black-marker layout drawn in a Paper 02 exam with labelled boxes.
questions.explain: Hand-drawn layouts with labels are low-fidelity, and they are exactly what Paper 02 often asks for.

questions.stem:
Zara at the Island Pulse Media has mixed up the files for the Holetown Market Online project. Sort each file using the definitions.

Is this a wireframe, a mockup or a prototype?

A greyscale layout labelled "Low-Fidelity Wireframe", with boxes for images and lines for text.
questions.explain: Greyscale, placeholders and the label all mark a wireframe: the skeleton of the design.

questions.stem:
Is this a wireframe, a mockup or a prototype?

A whiteboard sketch mapping where the search bar, product list and menu go.
questions.explain: It shows only layout and structure, so it is a wireframe.

questions.stem:
Is this a wireframe, a mockup or a prototype?

A full-colour home page with the market's logo, fonts and product photos, but nothing can be clicked.
questions.explain: High-fidelity but static: that is a mockup.

questions.stem:
Is this a wireframe, a mockup or a prototype?

Two versions of the home page, one in teal and one in coral, for the client to compare.
questions.explain: Multiple variations of a key screen to choose a visual direction is the mockup "strategic decision point".

questions.stem:
Is this a wireframe, a mockup or a prototype?

A Sketch file used to perfect button styles and spacing across every screen.
questions.explain: Refining visual consistency is a reason to use mockups.

questions.stem:
Is this a wireframe, a mockup or a prototype?

A Figma file where tapping "Sign up" moves through account creation to first login.
questions.explain: A clickable sign-up flow simulating real interactions is a prototype.

questions.stem:
Is this a wireframe, a mockup or a prototype?

A clickable demo tested with five vendors to find confusing steps before coding.
questions.explain: Validating user experience with real users is a purpose of prototypes.

questions.stem:
Is this a wireframe, a mockup or a prototype?

An Axure RP file where a form shows different screens depending on the answer chosen.
questions.explain: Conditional logic and dynamic content are advanced prototyping features.

questions.stem:
The Island Pulse Media is working on several projects across the islands. Sort each prototype into one of the four types.

Which of the four types of prototype is this?

Jerome writes a few lines of code to see whether a new route-finding algorithm for the ANU Bus Pass app is fast enough on older phones.
questions.explain: An engineer testing new technology and performance with just enough code is a feasibility prototype.

questions.stem:
Which of the four types of prototype is this?

A rough test checking whether a photo-recognition feature can identify Caribbean reef fish quickly enough to be useful for Belize Reef Divers.
questions.explain: It tests technical risk before any design work, which is feasibility.

questions.stem:
Which of the four types of prototype is this?

Linked grey boxes in Balsamiq that let testers tap from "Menu" to "Order" for a fish-fry stand at Oistins.
questions.explain: An interactive wireframe that does not look real, used to test the workflow, is a low-fidelity user prototype.

questions.stem:
Which of the four types of prototype is this?

Zara watches three students try to register for a Carnival event using clickable sketches, noting where they hesitate.
questions.explain: Finding usability issues early in the workflow with rough screens is the job of a low-fidelity user prototype.

questions.stem:
Which of the four types of prototype is this?

A polished Figma simulation in full brand colours that Keisha presents to the board of an Antigua hotel to win approval.
questions.explain: Realistic-looking and used to communicate a proposed product to stakeholders: high-fidelity user.

questions.stem:
Which of the four types of prototype is this?

A realistic, working simulation of a Curaçao art trail app, with real photos and smooth transitions, shown to investors.
questions.explain: It looks real and works as a simulation, but it does not use live data. That makes it high-fidelity user.

questions.stem:
Which of the four types of prototype is this?

Developers release a very limited version of a market-price app to 30 vendors in Castries, pulling real prices each morning.
questions.explain: A very limited implementation with real data and live traffic is a live-data prototype.

questions.stem:
Which of the four types of prototype is this?

A bare-bones booking page goes online for one weekend to see whether real customers actually book Montego Bay kayak tours through it.
questions.explain: Real traffic proving that it works in the world is the mark of a live-data prototype.

questions.stem:
Maya at the Island Pulse Media is finishing the website for the Seaglass & Silk boutique on Frederick Street. Sort each item.

Does this describe an HTML sitemap or an XML sitemap?

A simple bulleted outline of every page, with links that use page titles as the anchor text.
questions.explain: A bulleted outline of linked page titles is exactly what an HTML sitemap is.

questions.stem:
Does this describe an HTML sitemap or an XML sitemap?

A file at /sitemap.xml full of url and loc tags.
questions.explain: A list of URLs marked up with tags is an XML sitemap.

questions.stem:
Does this describe an HTML sitemap or an XML sitemap?

Built exclusively for search engine bots, to guide them to every page you want indexed.
questions.explain: XML sitemaps are for bots, not people.

questions.stem:
Does this describe an HTML sitemap or an XML sitemap?

A shopper who cannot find the Returns policy clicks "Sitemap" in the footer and finds it in the list.
questions.explain: Helping visitors navigate by following links is the job of an HTML sitemap.

questions.stem:
Does this describe an HTML sitemap or an XML sitemap?

Includes a lastmod tag so Googlebot knows the Sale page changed yesterday.
questions.explain: Last-updated information in tags makes the site more readable for Googlebot: XML.

questions.stem:
Does this describe an HTML sitemap or an XML sitemap?

Maya submits it in Google Search Console so the new Carnival Collection pages are crawled.
questions.explain: Submitting to a search engine so pages are crawled and indexed is what an XML sitemap is for.

questions.stem:
Does this describe an HTML sitemap or an XML sitemap?

Designed so users can find all the information they are looking for on the website.
questions.explain: Guiding visitors to everything on the site is the purpose of an HTML sitemap.

questions.stem:
Does this describe an HTML sitemap or an XML sitemap?

Like the sitemap page on Apple.com, styled to match the rest of the site.
questions.explain: The sitemap on Apple.com is a classic HTML sitemap: a readable page for visitors.

questions.stem:
Zara is reviewing student interns' layouts for the Portsmouth Seafood Festival. Identify the principle each comment is about.

"Your headline, photo and button are all stacked in the exact centre. Try putting the chef's face on one of the grid intersections."
questions.explain: Placing the focal point on a grid intersection, instead of the centre, is the rule of thirds.

questions.stem: "The left column has three big photos and the right is empty. The page feels as if it will tip over."
questions.explain: Uneven visual weight is a balance problem. Add weight to the right or redistribute the photos.

questions.stem: "Your captions start at slightly different points from the edges of the images."
questions.explain: Elements that do not share a common edge are misaligned. Snap them to a grid.

questions.stem: "Pale yellow text on a white background is almost impossible to read in the sun."
questions.explain: Readability depends on contrast between text and background, especially on phones outdoors.

questions.stem: "The ticket price is the same size as the small print. Make the most important information biggest."
questions.explain: Visual hierarchy uses size, weight and position to show what matters most.

questions.stem: "Everything is jammed together. Give each section some breathing room."
questions.explain: White space (spacing) separates groups and makes a page easier to scan.

questions.stem:
This activity asks you to list cloud-based tools for a concept map, a navigational chart, a site map and a hierarchy map. Help the Island Pulse Media team pick the best tool for each job.

Keisha wants to build a concept map for a Carnival website, with linking words on every arrow, starting from a ready-made concept map template.
questions.explain: Lucidchart has concept map templates and lets you type linking words on each line, as in the video in this unit.

questions.stem: Jerome needs a free flowchart of the checkout navigation for the Lagoon Grill in Frigate Bay, on a school computer where he cannot create an account.
questions.explain: draw.io is free, has flowchart shapes and arrows, and can be used without signing up.

questions.stem: Maya wants to lay out every page of the Seaglass & Silk boutique as a visual site map of page blocks before any design starts.
questions.explain: Octopus.do is a visual sitemap builder made for planning pages as blocks.

questions.stem: The boutique site is live and Maya now needs an XML sitemap to submit to Google Search Console.
questions.explain: The XML-Sitemaps.com generator crawls a live site and produces the XML file for search engines.

questions.stem: The team is already designing in Figma and wants a shared whiteboard to drag sticky notes into a hierarchy map, Home at the top.
questions.explain: FigJam is Figma's whiteboard, so the hierarchy map sits right beside the design files.

questions.stem: A CAPE group already makes its SBA posters in Canva and wants a free infinite board to brainstorm ideas with a purpose.
questions.explain: Canva whiteboards suit brainstorming and concept maps, and the group already knows Canva.

questions.stem: A group of three CAPE students at Seagrape Bay Secondary School must produce a clickable mobile app prototype for their SBA. They work from different homes, want to edit the same file at the same time, and need reusable buttons that update everywhere. Which tool BEST meets all of these needs?

The Island Pulse Media has several jobs this month. Choose the best artifact for each stage or need.

The Curaçao Art Trail team has just agreed the idea and needs to settle which pages exist and how they connect.
questions.explain: Early-stage concept validation and structural alignment is when to use wireframes.

questions.stem: A hotel client must approve the brand colours and fonts before the developer receives handoff specifications.
questions.explain: Visual design refinement, stakeholder approval and developer handoff specifications are mockup jobs.

questions.stem: An investor wants to tap through a ferry-booking app on a phone before funding it.
questions.explain: Investor demos and interactive testing are what prototypes are best for.

questions.stem: The team wants to explore five different layout ideas in one afternoon.
questions.explain: Exploring multiple concepts rapidly is a wireframe strength: they are quick and cheap.

questions.stem: A small restaurant only wants a fresh look for its existing website. Following "choose tools strategically", the team should mainly produce...
questions.explain: A simple refresh might only need mockups. A complex app benefits from full prototyping.

questions.stem: Which principle says you should add detail only after confirming you are solving the right problem?
questions.explain: Start simple with low-fidelity wireframes and iterate fast before adding detail.

questions.stem:
You are a junior designer at Island Pulse Media. Belize Reef Divers company wants a booking website. Make the best decisions.

The owner sends a long list of ideas: dive packages, a blog, photo galleries, safety rules, staff bios, prices and a booking form. Zara asks you where to begin.
options: Open Figma straight away and design a beautiful full-colour home page.
Make a concept map of the ideas, then group them into a site map with clear levels.

questions.stem: The site map is approved. Next you must show the owner the layout of the home and booking pages. What do you produce?
options: Quick low-fidelity wireframes on paper or in Balsamiq, then test them with two real customers.
Skip testing; the owner already likes the site map.
A final-colour mock-up of every page so the owner can pick colours first.

questions.stem: Testers could not find the booking button on the home page. You move to a high-fidelity Figma prototype. How do you fix the problem?
options: Give the "Book a dive" button strong contrast, place it where the Z-pattern ends, and add it to every package page as a component.
Make the button the same colour as the background so the design looks calm.

questions.stem:
Keisha is reviewing early notes for the Taste of Castries guide. Each note describes one quality of the content. Sort it into the test it helps the content pass.

Which quality does this feature mainly show?

Each vendor entry lists prices in US dollars and opening hours.
questions.explain: Prices and hours answer the real questions a visitor has, so this makes the content useful.

questions.stem:
Which quality does this feature mainly show?

The page loads in under three seconds on a phone with roaming data.
questions.explain: Speed is about how easy the content is to use, so this is usability.

questions.stem:
Which quality does this feature mainly show?

Every entry ends with a "Get directions" button.
questions.explain: A clear button moves the reader to act, so this is purposeful.

questions.stem:
Which quality does this feature mainly show?

Walking times from the cruise pier are given for every stop.
questions.explain: Visitors need to know they can get there and back in time. That is a real need answered.

questions.stem:
Which quality does this feature mainly show?

Descriptive headings let readers jump straight to the vendor they want.
questions.explain: Headings make content easy to scan and navigate, which is usability.

questions.stem:
Which quality does this feature mainly show?

A short line invites readers to share the trail with friends on the ship.
questions.explain: It prompts an action that spreads the content, so it is purposeful.

questions.stem:
Which quality does this feature mainly show?

The guide appears when someone searches "street food Castries".
questions.explain: Being easy to find is part of usability. Content that cannot be found cannot be used.

questions.stem:
Which quality does this feature mainly show?

A note explains which vendors take cards and which take cash only.
questions.explain: Payment is a real need for visitors, so this detail is useful.

questions.stem:
Keisha is checking sources before the Taste of Castries guide goes live. Sort each source.

Is this source credible enough to use, or questionable?

A recorded interview with a johnny cake vendor about her recipe and prices this season.
questions.explain: Primary research from the person who knows best is credible, as long as it is quoted accurately with permission.

questions.stem:
Is this source credible enough to use, or questionable?

An anonymous TikTok claiming accra was "first made in 2010".
questions.explain: No authority, no evidence and it cannot be confirmed. Questionable.

questions.stem:
Is this source credible enough to use, or questionable?

The official St. Lucia tourism website listing this year's cruise season events.
questions.explain: Official, current and relevant. Still double-check dates close to publishing.

questions.stem:
Is this source credible enough to use, or questionable?

A 2014 blog post giving vendor opening hours.
questions.explain: It fails currency. Opening hours change; confirm directly with the vendor.

questions.stem:
Is this source credible enough to use, or questionable?

A national newspaper report quoting named food vendors.
questions.explain: An established news outlet with named sources has authority and accountability.

questions.stem:
Is this source credible enough to use, or questionable?

A chatbot answer giving a precise number of food trucks on the island, with no source.
questions.explain: Such tools can invent figures. Without a verifiable source, do not publish it.

questions.stem:
Is this source credible enough to use, or questionable?

A vendor's own flyer saying it has "the best ribs on the island".
questions.explain: The purpose is to sell, so it is biased. You may quote it as their claim, not as fact.

questions.stem:
Is this source credible enough to use, or questionable?

A university research paper on Caribbean food heritage with references.
questions.explain: Academic, referenced work has strong authority and accuracy.

questions.stem:
Keisha is checking the Taste of Castries brief and some briefs for other clients. Choose the best answer each time.

Denise has five hours ashore and roaming data. Which feature matters MOST for her?
options: walking times from the pier and fast-loading pages
questions.explain: The persona tells you her real constraints: time and data. The content must serve those first.

questions.stem: Which line is "friendly, not childish"?
options: "Patrons are advised that johnny cakes are available."
"You'll love the crispy johnny cakes at this stall."
questions.explain: It is warm and addresses the reader, without childish slang or cold formality.

questions.stem: Which line is "confident, not boastful"?
options: "We think it might be quite nice."
"A Jeremie Street favourite with locals for over ten years."
questions.explain: Confidence comes from specific, believable evidence, not empty superlatives or weak hedging.

questions.stem: A brief for a storm shelter update in St. Lucia. The best tone is...
questions.explain: In emergencies people need calm, clear, trustworthy instructions.

questions.stem: "Real St. Lucian street food is a short walk from your ship" is the brief's...
questions.explain: The key message is the one sentence readers must remember.

questions.stem: "150 QR code scans from the pier flyers in December" is a...
questions.explain: It has a number and a time, so success can be measured.

questions.stem:
Maya is teaching an intern the four CC conditions. Each card describes a rule or a use. Sort it under the condition it describes.

Which CC condition does this describe?

You must credit the photographer by name.
questions.explain: BY means attribution: always credit the creator.

questions.stem:
Which CC condition does this describe?

You remix a CC song, so your remix must be shared under the same licence.
questions.explain: SA (share-alike) means new work must carry the same licence.

questions.stem:
Which CC condition does this describe?

You cannot use the photo on a page that promotes paying vendors.
questions.explain: NC (non-commercial) forbids money-making uses, including promoting businesses.

questions.stem:
Which CC condition does this describe?

You may share the image, but you cannot crop it or add text.
questions.explain: ND (no derivatives) means no changes at all.

questions.stem:
Which CC condition does this describe?

The credit line follows TASL: title, author, source, licence.
questions.explain: TASL is how you meet the BY (attribution) condition properly.

questions.stem:
Which CC condition does this describe?

A student uses the photo free in a school project, but a hotel cannot use it in an advert.
questions.explain: Non-commercial use is allowed; commercial use is not. That is NC.

questions.stem:
Which CC condition does this describe?

You translate a CC article into Papiamentu and must release it under the same CC licence.
questions.explain: A translation is a new work; SA requires the same licence.

questions.stem:
Which CC condition does this describe?

You must use the video clip exactly as it is, with no edits.
questions.explain: ND means you may not change the work.

questions.stem:
You are Maya, responsible for images on the Taste of Castries guide. The deadline is close and the brief says "no paid stock photos". Make the best decisions.

You find a stunning photo of Vigie Beach on Flickr. The licence label says CC BY-NC 2.0. What do you do first?
options: Use it with a credit line; credit is all CC asks for.
Read what each condition means for this project before deciding.

questions.stem: BY means credit the creator. NC means non-commercial. Is the Taste of Castries guide a commercial use?
options: No. It is a free blog post, so it is non-commercial.
Yes. The vendors paid for it and it promotes their businesses, so it is commercial.

questions.stem: So the CC BY-NC photo is ruled out, and paid stock is not allowed. What now?
options: Take a similar photo from a Google image search; it is online, so it is free.
Shoot your own photos of the vendors and their food.

questions.stem: Your photos show vendors and some customers whose faces are clear. The images will promote businesses. What do you do before publishing?
options: Publish them; the photos were taken in a public street.
Get signed releases from the vendors and anyone recognisable, and log them with the photos.

questions.stem: The Antigua Sailing Week Fan Club runs a commercial website that sells T-shirts. Keisha wants to use a photo from Wikimedia Commons on the shop page and crop it into a banner. Which licence on the photo would allow this use, as long as she credits the photographer?

Maya is preparing assets for the Taste of Castries page. Choose the best option each time.

A colour photo of a plate of saltfish and johnny cakes.
questions.explain: Photos with many colours compress best as WebP or JPEG.

questions.stem: The Taste of Castries logo, which must stay sharp at any size.
questions.explain: SVG is vector, so logos stay crisp at every size and the files are tiny.

questions.stem: A trail map graphic with text labels and flat colours.
questions.explain: PNG keeps text and sharp edges clean. Low-quality JPEG would blur the labels.

questions.stem: For most images on the page, aim to keep each file...
questions.explain: Under 200 KB keeps pages fast on mobile data. Ppi is a print setting.

questions.stem: The best file name for a photo of bakes at the Castries Market is...
questions.explain: Lower case, hyphens and descriptive words help both SEO and organisation.

questions.stem: A 6000 px wide camera photo will be shown in an 800 px column. You should...
options: resize it to display size first
questions.explain: Resize to display size. The extra pixels are invisible but cost data and time.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Malik and Keisha are planning shoots for clients across the region. Choose the best option each time.

A 40-minute Instagram Live interview with a Trinidad soca artist. Which set-up?
options: phone on a tripod with a lavalier mic
questions.explain: Long recordings need steady, hands-free framing and clear voice. A tripod and clip-on mic solve both.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: Close-up product photos of handmade jewellery for an online shop in St. John's, with a blurred background.
options: mirrorless camera with a wide-aperture lens
questions.explain: A wide aperture gives shallow depth of field, blurring the background so the product stands out.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: A smooth walking tour of Redcliffe Quay filmed while moving.
questions.explain: A gimbal stabilises movement so walking shots do not shake.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: The client wants a quick TikTok from a Dickenson Bay beach fete tonight.
questions.explain: Phones are fast, light and already set up for vertical short video and instant upload.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: Recording a podcast voice track at home. The biggest quality gain comes from...
options: a USB or lavalier microphone in a quiet room
questions.explain: For audio-only content, the microphone and the room matter most.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
You are assisting Malik from the Island Pulse Media at Antigua Sailing Week in English Harbour. The brief: three hero photos for a website gallery and Instagram. Make the best camera decisions.

Shot 1 is a portrait of a young local skipper on the dock. Behind her are crowds, ropes and parked cars. Which setting do you choose?
options: Shallow focus: about f/1.8, step closer and zoom in a little so the background turns to bokeh.
Deep focus at f/11 so every rope and car is sharp.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: Shot 2 is an establishing shot of the whole fleet crossing the bay from Shirley Heights above English Harbour. What do you choose?
options: f/1.8 so one boat is sharp and the rest are blurred.
Deep focus around f/11 so the boats and the coastline are all sharp.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: Shot 3 celebrates the winning crew. It is 12 noon with harsh, overhead sun. The prize-giving is at 5.30 p.m. What do you do?
options: Wait for the prize-giving in the golden hour and shoot from a low angle as they lift the trophy.
Shoot now from a high angle, looking down at the crew.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Jerome is listing the software on the Island Pulse Media intern laptops. Sort each tool.

Which category does this tool belong to?

GIMP
questions.explain: GIMP is free, open-source raster image software.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

Adobe Photoshop
questions.explain: Photoshop is the proprietary industry standard for photo editing, sold by subscription.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

Canva
questions.explain: Canva runs in the browser and stores designs online.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

Audacity
questions.explain: Audacity is a free, open-source audio editor.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

WeVideo
questions.explain: WeVideo is a browser-based video editor with cloud storage.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

Kdenlive
questions.explain: Kdenlive is a free, open-source non-linear video editor.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

DaVinci Resolve
questions.explain: DaVinci Resolve is a professional editing and colour grading suite used in film and TV studios.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

CapCut
questions.explain: CapCut is a cloud-connected editor popular for short vertical video.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

OBS
questions.explain: OBS Studio is free and open-source software for screen recording and livestreaming.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Which category does this tool belong to?

Final Cut Pro
questions.explain: Final Cut Pro is Apple's professional, paid video editor.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: Malik recorded an interview with a Dominica cocoa farmer for Caribbean Roots podcast. There is a steady air-conditioner hum throughout. Following good practice, he recorded ten seconds of room tone at the start. What should he do FIRST in Audacity?
options: Apply Noise Reduction at the maximum setting to the whole track.
Select the ten seconds of room tone and use Noise Reduction to Get Noise Profile.
Add intro music on a new track to cover the hum.
Normalize the track to make it louder.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
Keisha is publishing the Chez Corail promo and the Regatta highlights for the Island Pulse Media. Choose the correct setting each time.

Which video container is the web standard?
questions.explain: MP4 plays in almost every browser and app. XCF and AUP3 are project files, not videos.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: Which video codec should go inside it?
questions.explain: H.264 compresses the picture efficiently and is supported almost everywhere. AAC is for audio.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: Which audio codec pairs with H.264 in an MP4?
questions.explain: AAC is the standard compressed audio codec in web MP4 files.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: The Regatta promo is for Instagram Reels. Which size?
questions.explain: Reels are vertical 9:16, which is 1080 x 1920.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: The Chez Corail video is for the restaurant website banner. Which size?
questions.explain: A website banner is landscape 16:9, which is 1920 x 1080.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: The video has fast fireworks cuts. What is the safe limit?
options: Any number if there are captions
No more than three flashes per second
questions.explain: More than three flashes per second can trigger seizures; captions do not change that.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem:
You are working with Malik on a 30-second web promo for Curaçao Jazz Nights. Make the best decisions.

The edit is finished. The client wants it on their website and on Instagram Reels. How do you export?
options: One uncompressed master file of several gigabytes for both.
Two MP4 (H.264/AAC) versions: 1920 by 1080 for the website and 1080 by 1920 for Reels.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: The client says, "Most people watch Reels with the sound off." What do you add?
