options: Proofread captions: burned-in open captions for Reels and an SRT file for the website player.
Nothing. The music is the best part.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques for digital content development
questions.stem: The video will sit on the page Home > Events > Jazz Nights. Visitors arrive from Google straight onto that page. How do you help them find other events?
options: Add a breadcrumb trail at the top so they can click back to Events or Home.
Hope they use the browser back button.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Maya is planning a page for the Sea Breeze Guesthouse in Gros Islet. Using the house analogy, decide which language handles each job: the frame and walls, the paint and landscaping, or the electricity.

Which language does this job?

A main heading that says "Sea Breeze Guesthouse"
questions.explain: The heading itself is content and structure: part of the frame and walls.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which language does this job?

Making that heading purple and centred
questions.explain: Colour and alignment are presentation: the paint.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which language does this job?

Placing a photo of the beach on the page
questions.explain: The img element adds the image to the structure. CSS may size it later, but HTML puts it there.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which language does this job?

A thank-you message that pops up when a guest presses "Book"
questions.explain: Responding to a click is behaviour: the electricity.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which language does this job?

Using the same font on every page of the site
questions.explain: Fonts are presentation, best set once in an external style sheet.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which language does this job?

A list of three menu links: Home, Rooms, Contact
questions.explain: Lists and links are structure, built with ul, li and a.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which language does this job?

A slideshow that changes photo every five seconds
questions.explain: Changing the page over time is behaviour, handled by JavaScript.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which language does this job?

Stacking the room boxes in one column on a phone
questions.explain: Layout is presentation. CSS with a media query rearranges the same HTML.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which language does this job?

A form that warns "Check your phone number" as soon as a guest types one digit too few
questions.explain: Checking input and responding instantly is an action and response: JavaScript.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Maya is tidying the CSS for the Sea Breeze Guesthouse site before Zara reviews it. Decide where each piece of CSS lives, or which method each description fits.

Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> in the head
questions.explain: The link tag connects the page to a separate .css file: external CSS.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

A <style> element inside the head of one page
questions.explain: CSS written in a style element in the head is internal (embedded) CSS.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

<p style="color:purple;">
questions.explain: A style attribute on one element is inline CSS.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

One file called style.css shared by all five pages
questions.explain: A shared separate file is the whole point of external CSS.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

Best for consistent styling across the whole site
questions.explain: Change one file and every linked page updates.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

Useful for one unique page, such as a one-off Carnival countdown page
questions.explain: Internal CSS suits a single page that needs its own styles.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

Changes just that one element
questions.explain: Inline CSS affects only the element it is written on.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

<h1 style="text-align:center;">Sea Breeze</h1>
questions.explain: Another style attribute inside an opening tag: inline.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Is this external, internal or inline CSS?

<style> body { font-family: Arial; } </style>
questions.explain: Rules inside a style element are internal CSS.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: The Sea Breeze Guesthouse page links style.css, which contains p { color: blue; }. Further down the head, after the link, an internal style element contains p { color: green; }. One paragraph is written as <p style="color:red;">. No rule uses !important. What colours appear?
options: That paragraph is red; every other paragraph is blue, because external beats internal.
Every paragraph is blue, because the external style sheet always wins.
Every paragraph is green, because internal CSS beats inline CSS.
That paragraph is red; every other paragraph is green.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Maya is writing the style sheet for Pineapple Grove. Decide which kind of selector each rule uses.

Which type of selector is this?

p { line-height: 1.6; }
questions.explain: No dot or hash: it targets every p element.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which type of selector is this?

.room-card { border: 1px solid #ccc; }
questions.explain: The dot shows a class. Every room card can share it.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which type of selector is this?

#booking-form { background: #fff7e6; }
questions.explain: The hash shows an id. There is only one booking form on the page.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which type of selector is this?

footer { text-align: center; }
questions.explain: footer is an HTML element name, so this is an element selector.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which type of selector is this?

.btn { padding: 12px 24px; }
questions.explain: A reusable button style is a class: many buttons can use it.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which type of selector is this?

#hero { height: 60vh; }
questions.explain: The single large banner at the top of the home page is unique, so an id fits.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which type of selector is this?

h2 { color: #7a1f3d; }
questions.explain: All h2 headings are styled; this is an element selector.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Which type of selector is this?

.highlight { color: #b8860b; }
questions.explain: A class you can add to any text you want to highlight.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Keisha (marketing, Island Pulse Media) keeps asking Maya for small changes to the Cocoa Grove site. Choose the CSS that does each job.

Keisha wants more space between the text of a room card and its border, inside the card.
questions.explain: Padding is the space inside the border. Margin would push the whole card away from its neighbours.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: She wants the cards spaced further apart from each other.
questions.explain: Margin sits outside the border and separates one box from the next.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: The brand red is rgb(122, 31, 61). Which hex code is the same colour?
questions.explain: 122 is 7a, 31 is 1f and 61 is 3d in hexadecimal, in the order red, green, blue.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: Body text feels cramped. Which property adds space between lines?
questions.explain: line-height controls the vertical space between lines; 1.5 to 1.7 suits body text.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: Which declaration gives the booking button rounded corners?
questions.explain: border-radius rounds the corners of the box. The other two are not valid CSS.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: Which rule makes every link inside the nav white?
questions.explain: nav a is a descendant selector: links inside nav. Note that CSS uses the American spelling color.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: Maya needs the Guavaberry Grove photo gallery to show twelve photos in neat rows of four columns on a laptop, with equal gaps between rows and columns. Which CSS is the MOST suitable starting point?
options: <table> with four <td> cells in each row

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Pommecythere Grove needs both a printed brochure for the Piarco Airport tourism desk and a website. Sort each setting by where it belongs.

Does this belong to print production or screen (web) production?

Images set to 300 dpi
questions.explain: 300 dpi is the usual standard for sharp printed material.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this belong to print production or screen (web) production?

CMYK colour model
questions.explain: Printers mix cyan, magenta, yellow and black inks.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this belong to print production or screen (web) production?

Hero photo exported at 1920 px wide and compressed to under 300 KB
questions.explain: Web images are measured in pixels and kept small so pages load quickly on mobile data.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this belong to print production or screen (web) production?

Colours written as hex codes such as #7a1f3d
questions.explain: Hex codes describe RGB light colours used on screens and in CSS.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this belong to print production or screen (web) production?

Font sizes in rem so text scales when the user zooms
questions.explain: rem is a CSS unit that respects the user's browser text settings.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this belong to print production or screen (web) production?

A 3 mm bleed added around the page edge
questions.explain: Bleed stops white edges after a printed page is trimmed.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this belong to print production or screen (web) production?

Media queries for phones and tablets
questions.explain: Media queries adapt a web layout to different screen sizes.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this belong to print production or screen (web) production?

Saved as a high-quality PDF for the print shop
questions.explain: Print shops usually want a print-ready PDF.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Guavaberry Grove is a six-room guest house in Sea Cows Bay, Tortola, in the British Virgin Islands. The owner, Mrs. Richardson, wants a website that brings in direct bookings instead of relying only on travel sites. Help Maya make the right decisions.

Mrs. Richardson is eager and says: "Just start coding today. I want it to look like a luxury resort site I saw." What should Maya do first?
options: Agree a short brief (audience, purpose, pages), then draw a site map and wireframes for approval.
Start coding straight away and copy the luxury site's design and photos.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: The wireframes are approved. Maya now sets up the code. How should she handle the styling for five pages?
options: A data table to position the header, menu and content.
One external style sheet (css/style.css) linked from every page, with semantic header, nav, main and footer.
Inline style attributes on each element of each page.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: Testing shows that on a phone, the three room cards are squashed side by side and the 5 MB hero photo takes a long time to load on mobile data. What does Maya fix?
options: Add a mobile-first media query (one column on phones, three from 768 px), set img max-width: 100%, and export the hero at 1920 px compressed to about 250 KB.
Tell visitors in the footer to use a laptop for the best experience.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem: Keisha wants a pale yellow booking button with white text, a YouTube tour that opens in a new tab, and a Google Map. What does Maya do?
options: Use the deep sorrel red with white text for strong contrast, embed the YouTube tour and map with titled iframes, and give any new-tab external link rel="noopener".
Use the pale yellow button because it matches the brand, and leave out iframe titles to keep the code short.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Zara is reviewing Cocoa Grove and two other Caribbean sites against WCAG basics. Sort each feature.

Does this feature support accessibility and usability, or create a barrier?

Every photo has meaningful alt text
questions.explain: Alt text makes images perceivable for screen-reader users.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this feature support accessibility and usability, or create a barrier?

Light grey text on a white background
questions.explain: Low contrast fails WCAG and is hard to read in bright Caribbean sunlight.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this feature support accessibility and usability, or create a barrier?

The video tour has captions
questions.explain: Captions help deaf visitors and anyone watching with the sound off.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this feature support accessibility and usability, or create a barrier?

Links are shown only by a slightly different colour, with no underline or hover change
questions.explain: Users, especially those with colour blindness, may not see that the text is a link.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this feature support accessibility and usability, or create a barrier?

The booking form can be completed using only the keyboard
questions.explain: Keyboard access makes the form operable for people who cannot use a mouse.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this feature support accessibility and usability, or create a barrier?

Music autoplays loudly when the page opens
questions.explain: Autoplay audio interferes with screen readers and startles users.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this feature support accessibility and usability, or create a barrier?

Headings follow h1, h2, h3 in order
questions.explain: A logical heading structure lets screen-reader users navigate the page.

questions.topic: Website building with HTML and CSS
questions.stem:
Does this feature support accessibility and usability, or create a barrier?

Text is set in px and cannot grow when the user zooms
questions.explain: Users who need larger text are blocked. rem units and zoom-friendly layouts help.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
The Island Pulse Media has five clients across the Caribbean. Choose the most suitable hosting for each.

A CAPE student wants to publish her hand-coded HTML and CSS e-portfolio for free with HTTPS.
questions.explain: A static site needs no server-side code, and free static hosts provide HTTPS at no cost.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem: The Grenada Spice Tours needs a small WordPress site and a few email addresses on a tight budget.
questions.explain: Shared hosting is cheap, managed by the host and usually includes email and one-click WordPress. GitHub Pages cannot run WordPress.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem: The Port of Spain Carnival Tix site gets a huge traffic spike for two weeks each year.
questions.explain: Cloud hosting can scale up resources during the spike and scale down afterwards.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem: A growing online craft shop in Kingston needs custom software and more guaranteed resources, with a technician to manage it.
questions.explain: A VPS gives guaranteed resources and control to install software, at a moderate cost.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem: Which host type would NOT be able to process a booking form and save it to a database without extra services?
options: Shared hosting with PHP and MySQL
questions.explain: Static hosts serve files only. They need a third-party form service or other add-ons to collect data.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem: Guavaberry Grove wants guests to check room availability online, submit a booking request, and let the owner update prices herself each season without editing code. Which solution BEST meets all three needs?
options: The hand-coded HTML site on GitHub Pages with prices typed into a table
A CMS such as WordPress on shared hosting, with a booking plugin that stores requests in a database
Inline CSS on every page to highlight the prices
A PDF price list emailed to guests who ask

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
Maya has finished the Guavaberry Grove site. The owner, Mrs. Richardson, now wants it online with a booking enquiry form, and later a WordPress blog. Make the infrastructure and security decisions.

Mrs. Richardson asks which domain to register. Most guests come from the USA, the Netherlands and the wider Caribbean, and she wants a clear local identity. What does Maya recommend?
options: Let Maya register the domain in her own personal name to save time.
Register guavaberrygrove.vg (and guavaberrygrove.com if available) in the business's name, with auto-renew and WHOIS privacy turned on.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem: The site needs a booking enquiry form and a blog the owner can update herself. Which hosting does Maya choose?
options: Reputable shared hosting with free SSL, automatic backups and WordPress support.
A free static host only, with the form posting to nowhere.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem: Setting up WordPress, Maya must choose the admin login. The receptionist will also need access to read enquiries. What does Maya do?
options: A unique username (not "admin"), a long passphrase stored in a password manager, 2FA, and an Editor-level account for the receptionist.
Username "admin", password "guavaberry1", shared by everyone so nobody gets locked out.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem: Six months later, WordPress shows updates for three plugins, and one plugin has not been used since launch. A storm warning is issued for the island. What does Maya advise?
options: Back up the site, update WordPress and the plugins, delete the unused plugin, and confirm an off-site backup copy exists.
Ignore the updates because the site is working fine.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
After building Guavaberry Grove both ways, Maya lists what she noticed. Sort each observation by the approach it describes.

Is this an advantage of hand-coding, or an advantage of a website builder?

Every element can be designed exactly as the mock-up shows.
options: Advantage of hand-coded HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Hand-coding gives full creative control, without template limits.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage of hand-coding, or an advantage of a website builder?

The owner could add a new page herself in ten minutes with no training in code.
options: Advantage of hand-coded HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Drag-and-drop editors let non-coders update content.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage of hand-coding, or an advantage of a website builder?

The site files can be moved to any host at any time.
options: Advantage of hand-coded HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Hand-coded files are portable; builders often lock you in.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage of hand-coding, or an advantage of a website builder?

Hosting, SSL and security updates are handled by the platform.
options: Advantage of hand-coded HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Hosted builders manage the infrastructure for you.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage of hand-coding, or an advantage of a website builder?

Pages are lean and load quickly on mobile data.
options: Advantage of hand-coded HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Hand-written code avoids extra platform scripts.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage of hand-coding, or an advantage of a website builder?

A professional-looking template was ready in under an hour.
options: Advantage of hand-coded HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Templates make builders very fast.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage of hand-coding, or an advantage of a website builder?

Building it proves coding skill for a portfolio or the SBA.
options: Advantage of hand-coded HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Hand-coding demonstrates technical skill that examiners and employers value.

questions.topic: Website infrastructure, data handling and security
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage of hand-coding, or an advantage of a website builder?

A map, a video and a contact form were added with a few clicks.
options: Advantage of hand-coded HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Builders have ready-made widgets for common features.

questions.stem:
Keisha at the Island Pulse Media is fielding calls from clients across the region. Choose the form of digital publishing each client is describing.

A Curaçao dive shop wants a regular email that lands in customers' inboxes every Monday with dive conditions and offers.
questions.explain: A regular opt-in email pushed to subscribers is a newsletter. A blog waits for readers to visit.

questions.stem: A Trinidad author wants readers to change the font size on their phones and have the text reflow.
questions.explain: EPUB is reflowable, so text adjusts to screen and font size. PDF keeps a fixed layout.

questions.stem: A Belize tourism body wants a quarterly, beautifully laid-out edition with photo spreads and embedded video.
questions.explain: Issue-based, designed layout and a regular schedule are the marks of a digital magazine.

questions.stem: A St. Kitts historian wants listeners to subscribe and receive each new 30-minute audio episode automatically.
questions.explain: Episodes delivered through an RSS feed that listeners subscribe to make a podcast.

questions.stem: A Speightstown bakery wants customers to order and pay from their phones, with push notifications when the bread is ready.
questions.explain: Ordering, payment and push notifications are app features. A blog or magazine cannot do this.

questions.stem: A Roseau artist wants to share short clips, build followers and reply to comments every day.
questions.explain: Profiles, followers, sharing and comments define social networking platforms.

questions.stem:
Maya at the Island Pulse Media is grouping a client's publications in different ways. For each grouping, decide which basis she is using.

Which basis of classification is being used?

Putting an electricity outage alert and a national news site together because both inform people.
questions.explain: Grouping by why something was published (to inform) is classification by purpose.

questions.stem:
Which basis of classification is being used?

Separating content for cruise visitors at the Willemstad cruise terminal from content for local residents.
questions.explain: Grouping by who the content is for is classification by audience.

questions.stem:
Which basis of classification is being used?

Grouping a podcast and an audio walking tour together because both are audio.
questions.explain: Grouping by the media used (audio) is classification by content type.

questions.stem:
Which basis of classification is being used?

Placing a PDF brochure in "read only" and a quiz game in "user choices change the outcome".
questions.explain: Grouping by how much the user can do is classification by level of interactivity.

questions.stem:
Which basis of classification is being used?

Grouping a brand Instagram account and an online store because both aim to sell.
questions.explain: Persuading and selling is a purpose.

questions.stem:
Which basis of classification is being used?

Making a separate children's version of a history e-book for primary schools.
questions.explain: Children are a target audience, so this is classification by audience.

questions.stem:
Which basis of classification is being used?

Listing a blog, an e-book and a newsletter together as text-based publications.
questions.explain: Text-based is a content type.

questions.stem:
Which basis of classification is being used?

Placing blog posts with comments in the "medium" group, between e-books and apps.
questions.explain: Comments and shares give medium interactivity, which is the interactivity basis.

questions.stem: The Antigua Sailing Week Live page on a social networking platform has 40,000 followers and thousands of comments on every post. However, a survey shows many sailors could not find the race start times, and several said the comments were full of arguments. Which conclusion is the BEST evaluation?
options: The page has low accuracy because there are many comments.
The page has a privacy problem because sailors cannot find start times.
The page is excellent because 40,000 followers proves it is high quality.
High audience engagement but low user satisfaction and usability, so the page needs a clear schedule and better comment moderation.

questions.stem:
You are advising the Bonaire Heritage Youth Club, which wants to teach 13 to 18 year olds about the island's salt-pan history. Make the best decisions.

The club president says: "Let's make a 200-page e-book. Everything in one place." Most of the audience use phones and spend their free time on TikTok and games. What do you advise first?
options: Analyse the purpose and audience first: what must they learn, and how do they already consume content?
Agree to the 200-page e-book; it is the most complete option.

questions.stem: Your research shows the teens prefer short video and interactive content, and many have limited mobile data. Which main form do you recommend?
options: A 4K two-hour documentary to stream on YouTube.
A short-form video series (60 to 90 seconds each) with captions, plus a lightweight quiz game on a mobile web page.
A custom native app with 3D graphics that must be installed.

questions.stem: The game will ask players for a nickname. A parent asks about safety. What do you add?
options: Ask for full name, school and phone number so prizes can be sent.
Collect only a nickname (no email or location), state this in a simple privacy notice, use HTTPS and moderate any leaderboard names.

questions.stem:
Maya at the Island Pulse Media is sorting client notes. Decide which type of platform each note describes.

Which type of platform is described?

A student blog at grenadaspice.blogspot.com with no fees at all.
questions.explain: Blogger is hosted by Google, free, and uses a blogspot subdomain.

questions.stem:
Which type of platform is described?

A Willemstad boutique pays a monthly Squarespace plan for templates and online sales.
questions.explain: Squarespace is a hosted service that charges a subscription.

questions.stem:
Which type of platform is described?

The client installs WordPress.org software on rented hosting and must update plugins.
questions.explain: Installing the software yourself on your own hosting is self-hosting, with full responsibility for updates.

questions.stem:
Which type of platform is described?

A Jamaican essayist publishes on Medium to reach its readers, paying nothing.
questions.explain: Medium hosts the content; writing and publishing are free.

questions.stem:
Which type of platform is described?

A Wix premium plan removes Wix ads and connects a custom domain.
questions.explain: Premium Wix plans are paid hosted services.

questions.stem:
Which type of platform is described?

The owner must arrange their own backups and security plugin after the server is hacked.
questions.explain: On a self-hosted site, security and backups are the owner's responsibility.

questions.stem:
Which type of platform is described?

A free WordPress.com site that shows the platform's ads and a wordpress.com address.
questions.explain: The free WordPress.com plan is hosted, free, and limited.

questions.stem:
Which type of platform is described?

Full freedom to edit the theme's PHP code and add any plugin.
questions.explain: Full code and plugin control is the main benefit of self-hosting.

questions.stem:
Malik at the Island Pulse Media is uploading a client's video about the Spice Island Emporium on Frederick Street in Port of Spain. Choose the best setting each time.

The client must approve the video before anyone else sees it, but needs to watch it without logging into Malik's account.
questions.explain: Unlisted lets anyone with the link watch it, but it does not appear in search or on the channel.

questions.stem: Which thumbnail size matches YouTube's recommended 16:9 format?
questions.explain: 1280 by 720 is 16:9 landscape, YouTube's recommended thumbnail size. 1080 by 1920 is vertical 9:16.

questions.stem: Viewers want to jump straight to the tasting section. What should Malik add?
questions.explain: Timestamps in the description create chapters, so viewers can jump to sections.

questions.stem: Auto-captions wrote "shadow benny" instead of "chadon beni". What should he do?
options: leave them; auto-captions are always fine
questions.explain: Edited captions improve accuracy, accessibility and searchability. Turning them off excludes deaf viewers.

questions.stem: The title, description, tags and thumbnail together are called the video's...
questions.explain: Metadata is data about the video, used by search and recommendations.

questions.stem: The client is paid by a rum brand to feature its product. What must they do?
questions.explain: Platform rules and advertising standards require paid promotions to be disclosed.

questions.stem:
Keisha is preparing a report for the Grande Riviere Turtle Watch in Trinidad on using social media platforms. Sort each point.

Is this a benefit or a limitation of using an online platform?

Free analytics show which turtle videos are watched longest.
questions.explain: Built-in analytics are a key benefit of platforms.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of using an online platform?

A feed algorithm change halves the reach of the group's posts overnight.
questions.explain: Algorithm changes are outside your control: a limitation.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of using an online platform?

A video is muted because it used a popular song without a licence.
questions.explain: Copyright rules and claims limit what you can publish.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of using an online platform?

Volunteers can post from their phones in seconds.
questions.explain: Ease of use is a benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of using an online platform?

The group cannot download a list of its followers' contact details.
questions.explain: You do not own the audience on a rented platform.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of using an online platform?

A nesting-season post is shared by visitors in Canada and the Netherlands.
questions.explain: Global audience reach is a major benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of using an online platform?

The account is hacked because two-factor authentication was not turned on.
questions.explain: Security risks are a limitation that must be managed.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of using an online platform?

Live comments let residents ask questions during a beach clean-up stream.
questions.explain: Community features are a benefit.

questions.stem: Speightstown Kitchen sells fish cakes and bakes and takes all its orders through one social media account. The account is suspended by mistake for a week. Which action would MOST reduce this risk in future?
options: Turn off comments on all posts.
Post more often on the same account.
Build an owned channel, such as a simple website with an order form and an email or WhatsApp list, and link to it from social media.
Buy followers to increase the account's size.

questions.stem:
You are advising Georgetown Youth Media Collective, a group of four students who want to publish Caribbean news explainers, short videos and occasional live Q&As. They have a small budget and plan to grow. Make the best decisions.

One member says: "Let's just post everything on TikTok. It's free and everyone is there." What do you advise?
options: Agree: one free platform is enough.
Use TikTok and YouTube for reach, but also create an owned home such as a website or newsletter.

questions.stem: For the written explainers, which platform do you recommend to start with?
options: A hosted WordPress.com plan with a custom domain, upgrading to self-hosted WordPress when they need custom features.
Self-hosted WordPress with ten premium plugins straight away, though no one knows how to maintain it.

questions.stem: They plan a live Q&A with a local politician on Facebook Live. What do you add to the plan?
options: Just go live from a phone in the hallway and see what happens.
A test stream, an external microphone, a chat moderator, clear comment rules and no copyrighted background music.

questions.stem: Six months later, how should they keep the platforms useful?
options: Set a maintenance schedule: update facts and plugins, check analytics, back up, and archive outdated explainers.
Stop updating old posts; only new content matters.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Clients are asking the Island Pulse Media for advice. Choose the type of content management that best fits each need.

A Barbados law firm needs versioning, auditing and regulatory compliance for thousands of contracts.
questions.explain: Controlling the document lifecycle and compliance is the main purpose of a DMS, the "e-cabinet".

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A Bridgetown restaurant wants to update its menu pages and blog through a browser.
questions.explain: Content destined for the web is the job of WCM, such as WordPress.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A regional telecom company must capture, manage, store, preserve and deliver all its information across departments and islands.
questions.explain: Those are the five ECM stages covering all of an organisation's information.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A Carnival committee wants one set of event listings to feed its website, app, airport screens and a smart speaker.
questions.explain: Content delivered as data over an API to many heads is a headless CMS.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A cruise line's sales staff need secure access to price sheets on their tablets, with remote wipe if one is lost.
questions.explain: Secure access to corporate data on mobile devices, with identity management, is MCM.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A media house needs to tag 40,000 photos with photographer, location and licence expiry.
questions.explain: Managing rich media files with rights metadata is Digital Asset Management.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: The St. Lucia Jazz and Arts Festival publishes its programme on a WordPress website. It now wants the same programme to appear in a new mobile app, on digital screens at the venue and in a smart speaker skill, without staff retyping it. Which solution BEST meets this need?
options: Document Management Software with versioning for the programme PDF.
Three separate websites, one for each channel.
A headless CMS that stores the programme once and delivers it through an API to each head.
A new WordPress theme with bigger fonts.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Malik is preparing a comparison for Windward Islands Weekly. Sort each statement using the comparison table.

Does this describe a traditional (coupled) CMS or a headless CMS?

Themes and templates are built in.
questions.explain: A coupled CMS includes its own front end (the head) through themes.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Does this describe a traditional (coupled) CMS or a headless CMS?

Developers build each front end separately.
questions.explain: A headless CMS has no built-in front end, so each head is built by developers.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Does this describe a traditional (coupled) CMS or a headless CMS?

Output is mainly one website.
questions.explain: The body and one head are joined, so content is locked to one output.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Does this describe a traditional (coupled) CMS or a headless CMS?

Content can go to any channel that can call the API.
questions.explain: Delivering content as data over an API is what makes headless multi-channel.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Does this describe a traditional (coupled) CMS or a headless CMS?

Low skills needed; ideal for non-technical users.
questions.explain: A traditional CMS lets non-technical users manage a site without developers.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Does this describe a traditional (coupled) CMS or a headless CMS?

Very high flexibility: any design or framework.
questions.explain: Because the front end is separate, developers can use any technology.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Does this describe a traditional (coupled) CMS or a headless CMS?

Wix, Squarespace and Joomla.
questions.explain: These are coupled systems with built-in themes.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Does this describe a traditional (coupled) CMS or a headless CMS?

Contentful, Sanity and Strapi.
questions.explain: These are headless CMS products that deliver content via API.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Jerome is preparing notes for a client in Antigua. Sort each statement into the three CMS classifications.

Which classification does this describe?

Drupal, which a developer can download and customise without special permission.
questions.explain: Open source CMS can be used and customised by anyone without a licence.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which classification does this describe?

Microsoft SharePoint, used under a paid licence.
questions.explain: SharePoint is owned by Microsoft and used under licence: proprietary.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which classification does this describe?

Wix: a monthly subscription that includes hosting and support.
questions.explain: Software, hosting and support bundled in a cloud subscription is SaaS.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which classification does this describe?

Thousands of free plugins and themes written by a worldwide community.
questions.explain: Because anyone can develop for open source CMS, the ecosystem is huge.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which classification does this describe?

Even licence holders cannot change the code without a developer's licence.
questions.explain: The owner controls a proprietary application.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which classification does this describe?

Squarespace: the supplier handles maintenance and upgrades in real time.
questions.explain: With SaaS, the supplier handles maintenance, upgrades and technical issues.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which classification does this describe?

Joomla, which runs on PHP.
questions.explain: The most popular open source CMS (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla) run on PHP.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which classification does this describe?

Sitecore, with professional vendor support for large enterprises.
questions.explain: Vendor support and enterprise features are advantages of proprietary CMS.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which classification does this describe?

Webflow: priced per site, hosted in the cloud.
questions.explain: Subscription priced per site or user, hosted in the cloud, is SaaS.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: The Frigate Bay Yacht Services wants a cloud CMS installed on its own cloud web server so that its developer can alter the source code and add a custom berth-booking module. Which type of cloud CMS is this?

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Zara is preparing a talk on why web publishing in the Caribbean has changed. Sort each example by the main factor it shows.

Which factor is MAINLY shown?

A Grenada spice farmer builds a professional site from a cheap template in an afternoon.
questions.explain: Templates and site builders have become cheap standard products: commoditisation and affordability.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which factor is MAINLY shown?

Almost every customer at a Gros Islet café browses on a phone with 4G.
questions.explain: Always-on mobile technology everywhere is pervasiveness.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which factor is MAINLY shown?

A news site adds captions and screen-reader-friendly headings for visually impaired readers.
questions.explain: Making content usable by people with disabilities is accessibility.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which factor is MAINLY shown?

A new data protection law requires sites to explain how they use visitors' data.
questions.explain: Laws and regulation are the politics factor.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which factor is MAINLY shown?

A Jamaican teenager builds a large YouTube audience with no TV station behind her.
questions.explain: Individuals publishing without gatekeepers is empowerment.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which factor is MAINLY shown?

Local businesses move their promotions to WhatsApp Channels after customers start using them daily.
questions.explain: Following where users have moved is adoption.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which factor is MAINLY shown?

Stock photos and fonts that once cost a lot are now free on Canva.
questions.explain: Specialist resources becoming cheap and standard is commoditisation.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Which factor is MAINLY shown?

A government portal offers a low-data text version for users with weak connections.
questions.explain: Making content reachable for people with weak connections is accessibility.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
Clients of the Island Pulse Media describe what they have noticed. Name the trend each time.

A hotel's website can be added to a guest's home screen and still shows the map without Wi-Fi.
questions.explain: Home-screen install and offline use through a service worker define a PWA.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: Customers ask their phones, "Where can I eat doubles near Maracas?"
questions.explain: Spoken, question-style searches are voice search.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A news site lets readers see three free articles a month, then asks them to subscribe.
questions.explain: A few free articles before payment is metered access.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A writer moves her readers from social media to a paid email publication on Substack.
questions.explain: Direct-to-subscriber email, sometimes paid, is the newsletter and subscription trend.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A newsroom uses a tool to transcribe interviews and draft alt text, then an editor checks everything.
questions.explain: AI assisting the workflow, with human checking, is the responsible approach.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A Trinidad podcast also publishes each episode as an audio article and a captioned vertical clip.
questions.explain: Publishing in audio, video and visual formats alongside text is this trend.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: Portsmouth Gazette notices that many readers now get answers such as "Canefield market days" straight from AI search summaries and never visit its website. Which response is MOST likely to protect its income?
options: Publish more short generic articles to appear in more search results.
Switch from WordPress to a proprietary CMS.
Build a direct relationship with readers through a newsletter and membership, and focus on local reporting AI cannot easily replace.
Remove the website and post only on one social platform.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem:
You are working with Zara's team at the Island Pulse Media on a case study: Windward Islands Weekly in Kingstown, St. Vincent. One developer pastes every story by hand, photos are on three laptops, and the app shows different headlines from the website. Make the best decisions.

Reporters email stories to the developer, and last week a story with a wrong date went live. What do you set up first?
options: Make every reporter an Administrator so they can fix mistakes faster.
A CMS with user roles and a workflow: reporters draft as Authors, an Editor checks, the editor-in-chief approves before scheduling.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: The paper wants the same stories on its website, app, morning newsletter and a lobby screen, without retyping. What do you recommend?
options: Ask staff to copy and paste each story into the app, newsletter and screen software.
A headless set-up: the body stores each story once and the API sends it to all four heads.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: Jerome must sort 40,000 photos from three laptops. What does he use?
options: A DAM, tagging each photo with location, event, photographer and licence expiry.
An MCM system so staff can open photos on tablets.
One big shared folder named "Photos" with no tags.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: Search traffic is falling as AI summaries answer questions directly. How do you respond?
options: Copy whatever a large US site is doing this week.
Check analytics and Google Trends, then grow the newsletter and memberships and focus on local reporting.

questions.topic: Content management and trends in web publishing
questions.stem: A manager suggests publishing 50 AI-written stories a day with no checks. What do you say?
options: Use AI only to assist with transcripts, alt text and drafts; a human checks every fact and AI use is disclosed under a clear AI policy.
Agree; more content always means more readers.

questions.stem:
Jerome, the mobile developer at the Island Pulse Media, is mapping the ecosystem for a new beach-safety app. Sort each item into the correct component.

Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

A live wave-height map inside the app.
questions.explain: It is what people view and use on the screen, so it is content.

questions.stem:
Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

A cell tower on Crocus Hill carrying 4G signals.
questions.explain: Towers are part of the physical network that delivers data: infrastructure.

questions.stem:
Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

A tourist from Toronto checking conditions at Shoal Bay, Anguilla.
questions.explain: A person using the service is a user.

questions.stem:
Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

A mid-range Samsung phone running Android.
questions.explain: The handset and its operating system make up the device component.

questions.stem:
Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

The cloud server that stores the beach data.
questions.explain: Servers and data centres are back-end infrastructure, even if users never see them.

questions.stem:
Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

A short safety video about rip currents.
questions.explain: Video shown to people is content.

questions.stem:
Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

A lifeguard team updating flag colours each morning.
questions.explain: The lifeguards use the app to post updates, so they are users (and content contributors).

questions.stem:
Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

An Apple Watch that buzzes with a storm alert.
questions.explain: Wearables are devices in the ecosystem.

questions.stem:
Which ecosystem component does this belong to?

The Google Play and Apple App Store distribution systems.
questions.explain: App stores are part of the distribution infrastructure that gets apps onto devices.

questions.stem:
The Island Pulse Media is planning an app for the Oranjestad Night Market. Answer each question about mobile consumers.

Most target users are on prepaid data. Which design choice fits BEST?
options: Autoplay HD video on the home screen
Compressed images and an offline menu
questions.explain: Data-conscious prepaid users expect apps that use little data. Compression and offline content respect that.

questions.stem: Vendors already take orders through WhatsApp. What does this tell Jerome?
options: Users expect messaging-style ordering, so the app should link to or copy that flow
questions.explain: Existing behaviour shows what users find natural. Good apps build on familiar patterns.

questions.stem: Traffic to the app will peak on Friday nights when cruise ships are in port. This is an example of...
questions.explain: When and how often people use a service is a usage pattern.

questions.stem: A user deletes the app because it takes eight seconds to load. Which expectation was not met?
questions.explain: Mobile users expect near-instant loading. Slow performance is a top reason for uninstalling.

questions.stem: Visitors want to pay vendors by phone. Which consumer expectation is MOST important for payments?
questions.explain: Users will not enter payment details unless they trust the app is secure.

questions.stem: A mobile customer in Philipsburg has complained for months that her carrier keeps charging her for a data bundle she cancelled. The carrier has not resolved it. Which organisation is MOST appropriate for her to contact next?
options: Bureau Telecommunications and Post (BTP), Sint Maarten

questions.stem:
You are advising the Island Connect Nassau app, used by visitors to find restaurants, tours and taxis. One morning, a fault on an international link slows Internet across the island. Make the best decisions.

Users complain the app is not loading. The app's data is hosted on servers in the United States. What do you do first?
options: Find out which part of the ecosystem failed by checking with the carriers and the hosting provider.
Rewrite the app immediately; it must be badly coded.

questions.stem: The carriers confirm reduced international capacity. Local traffic still works. How can the app keep serving visitors?
options: Add an offline mode with cached listings and keep a copy of key data on a local or regional server.
Tell visitors to wait until the cable is fixed.
Switch to sending HD promotional videos instead.

questions.stem: After the outage, the government asks how to reduce the risk in future. What do you recommend?
options: Support more cable routes and backup links, local data hosting, and clear rules from the regulator on outage reporting.
Nothing. Outages are just bad luck.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
Jerome at the Island Pulse Media is briefing new interns. Sort each statement to the operating system it describes.

Which operating system does this describe?

Built on the open-source AOSP and used by Samsung, Motorola and TCL.
questions.explain: Many manufacturers use Android's open-source core.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
Which operating system does this describe?

Runs only on iPhone, with Apple controlling hardware and software.
questions.explain: This closed, single-maker ecosystem is iOS.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
Which operating system does this describe?

Developed by Huawei after it lost access to Google services.
questions.explain: HarmonyOS was Huawei's response to trade restrictions from 2019.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
Which operating system does this describe?

Developers struggle to test on thousands of different models and OS versions.
questions.explain: That is fragmentation, the classic Android challenge.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
Which operating system does this describe?

Apps must follow the Human Interface Guidelines and pass a strict review.
questions.explain: The HIG and App Review express Apple's design and security philosophy.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
Which operating system does this describe?

Designed to share tasks across phones, watches, TVs and cars, with apps from AppGallery.
questions.explain: Distributed, multi-device design and AppGallery belong to HarmonyOS.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
Which operating system does this describe?

Apps are distributed mainly through Google Play.
questions.explain: Google Play is Android's main store, though others exist.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
Which operating system does this describe?

Most devices receive updates at the same time, so fragmentation is low.
questions.explain: Apple pushes updates to most iPhones quickly.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
The Island Pulse Media has five client briefs. Choose the most suitable device for each.

A Carnival road-march timer that shows only the next band and a countdown on the wrist.
questions.explain: Glanceable, wrist-based information suits a smartwatch.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem: A hands-free recipe guide for pommecythere liqueur while the user's hands are busy.
questions.explain: Voice control lets the cook follow steps without touching a screen.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem: A digital menu customers browse at the table in a San Fernando restaurant.
questions.explain: A tablet's larger screen shows photos and prices clearly.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem: A step-count challenge for a school health campaign.
questions.explain: Wearables with motion sensors count steps automatically.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem: A tour app with maps and GPS for visitors walking around Port of Spain.
questions.explain: Smartphones are portable, have GPS and are what visitors already carry.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem: St. Lucia Jazz Pass startup has one developer who knows JavaScript, a small budget and only eight weeks before the festival. About half its audience uses iPhones and half uses Android. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Build two separate native apps in Kotlin and Swift.
Build one app with React Native and publish to both stores.
Build an iOS-only app in Xcode.
Build an Android-only app in Android Studio.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem:
You are advising Bay Hopper Ferries, which runs boats from Chaguanas and Port of Spain to Grenada and Venezuela. It wants an app for timetables, tickets and delay alerts. Make the best decisions.

The owner says, "Everyone has an iPhone, so just build for iOS." What do you do first?
options: Agree and start an iOS-only app in Xcode.
Check the audience: survey passengers and look at web analytics and StatCounter data for the island.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem: Data shows a mix: many visitors use iPhones, while most local commuters use Android. The budget is modest and the app must be ready before the tourist season in eight weeks. Which build approach?
options: Two native apps built by two separate teams.
A cross-platform app (for example Flutter) for both stores, plus a simple web timetable.

questions.topic: Mobile operating systems, platforms and devices
questions.stem: Passengers want delay alerts even when their phone has weak signal at sea. What feature do you prioritise?
options: A live HD camera stream from the boat.
Push notifications plus an offline timetable and saved tickets with QR codes.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Keisha at the Island Pulse Media is preparing an infographic comparing Caribbean and global mobile use. Help her interpret the data correctly.

Antigua and Barbuda shows more than 100 mobile subscriptions per 100 people. The BEST explanation is...
options: every resident owns exactly one phone
many people use two SIMs and visitors buy local SIMs
questions.explain: Subscriptions count SIM cards, not people. Dual SIMs and tourists push the figure above 100.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Which organisation is the UN agency that publishes global ICT statistics?
questions.explain: The ITU is the United Nations agency for information and communication technologies.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Keisha wants remittances as a share of GDP for Jamaica. Which source fits BEST?
questions.explain: The World Bank publishes remittance data by country and year.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Many people live within mobile broadband coverage but do not use the Internet. GSMA calls this...
questions.explain: The usage gap is people who are covered but not connected, often because of cost, skills or lack of relevant content.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Which statement is written in the BEST exam style?
options: According to ITU (2025), roughly three quarters of people worldwide use the Internet.
Loads of people use phones now.
questions.explain: It names the source and year and uses an approximate, defensible figure.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Malik is filming a short documentary for the Island Pulse Media about mobile technology across the Caribbean. Sort each clip into the sector it shows.

Which sector does this mobile application serve?

A Dominica farmer receives an SMS warning of heavy rain before harvesting.
questions.explain: Weather alerts to protect crops support agriculture.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Which sector does this mobile application serve?

A Breadfruit Valley Secondary student watches a CXC revision video on her phone on the bus.
questions.explain: Mobile learning supports education.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Which sector does this mobile application serve?

A cruise passenger books a catamaran tour to the Tobago Cays by app.
questions.explain: Booking visitor experiences is tourism.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Which sector does this mobile application serve?

Residents of the Turks and Caicos Islands check a hurricane tracker and shelter list.
questions.explain: Preparing for storms is disaster management.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Which sector does this mobile application serve?

A Jamaican yam farmer posts produce in a WhatsApp group to find buyers.
questions.explain: Selling produce by mobile supports agriculture.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Which sector does this mobile application serve?

A teacher posts homework in Google Classroom for students without laptops.
questions.explain: Using mobile platforms for coursework is education.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Which sector does this mobile application serve?

A restaurant in Soufrière, St. Lucia, uses a QR-code menu in English and French.
questions.explain: Serving visitors in their language supports tourism.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Which sector does this mobile application serve?

After a storm, a family abroad uses a social media group to locate relatives.
questions.explain: Finding people after a hurricane is part of disaster response and recovery.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: A report states that most of the apps used daily in Guyana are produced outside the Caribbean. Which statement BEST explains an ECONOMIC effect of this imbalance?
options: Young people may hear fewer local accents and stories.
Phones in Guyana have smaller screens.
Spending on subscriptions, in-app purchases and advertising flows mainly to foreign companies rather than local businesses.
The ITU publishes statistics every year.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
You are advising the Antigua and Barbuda Ready app, which will send hurricane alerts and help residents check in as safe. Make the best decisions.

The developer wants to collect every user's contacts, live location at all times and photos of their ID. What do you advise?
options: Collect everything; it might be useful later.
Collect only what is needed, ask for clear consent and follow Antigua and Barbuda's data protection law.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Testing shows that after a storm, networks may be down for hours or days. How should the app handle this?
options: Rely only on a live online map that needs constant data.
Store shelter lists, emergency numbers and checklists offline, and send short SMS alerts as well as push notifications.

questions.topic: Caribbean context vs the international mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: During a storm, a fake message spreads on WhatsApp claiming a shelter has closed. What should the app do?
options: Ignore it; rumours are not the app's problem.
Post verified updates from official sources, clearly marked, and include a "check before you share" message.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Jerome, the mobile developer at the Island Pulse Media, has a whiteboard full of app ideas from clients. Sort each idea by the main local need it addresses.

Which local need does this app idea mainly address?

Live minibus locations between Castries and Gros Islet.
questions.explain: Helping people move around the island is a transport need.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Which local need does this app idea mainly address?

A walking tour of Basseterre's Circus and Independence Square for cruise passengers with a map of shops.
questions.explain: Guiding visitors around attractions meets a tourism need.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Which local need does this app idea mainly address?

Push alerts when a hurricane watch is issued, with a list of shelters.
questions.explain: Warning people and guiding them to safety is a safety and disaster preparedness need.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Which local need does this app idea mainly address?

Reminders for a child's vaccinations at the local clinic.
questions.explain: Vaccination reminders support community health.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Which local need does this app idea mainly address?

A Dominica farmer checks banana prices and pest alerts before harvest.
questions.explain: Market prices and pest alerts help farmers earn more: an agriculture need.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Which local need does this app idea mainly address?

A WhatsApp-style ordering page for a nutmeg-products shop in Grenada.
questions.explain: Helping a small business take orders online meets a small business need.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Which local need does this app idea mainly address?

Recorded stories from elders about Emancipation Day traditions.
questions.explain: Recording oral history preserves heritage and culture for future generations.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Which local need does this app idea mainly address?

A game that teaches Papiamentu words to children in Curaçao.
questions.explain: A language learning game supports education and cultural identity.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
Keisha, the marketing lead at Island Pulse Media, is preparing a pitch for a heritage app. Help her choose the best answers.

An app records elders in Sauteurs telling stories about traditional life. The main benefit is...
questions.explain: Recording stories protects heritage and passes it on: cultural preservation.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem: A Grenadian living in New York uses a local app to follow island news and order a gift from a St. George's shop. This shows...
questions.explain: Mobile apps keep the diaspora linked to home, socially and economically.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem: A local news app sends an alert about a power outage in Grenville. This is mainly a...
questions.explain: Timely local news keeps the community informed, a social benefit.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem: Which is a SOCIAL benefit rather than an economic benefit?
options: The app is sold to clients in Belize
Young people feel pride seeing their culture in an app
questions.explain: Pride and identity are social benefits. Jobs and sales are economic benefits.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem: Before publishing recordings of a Carnival band's music, the developer must...
options: compress the files to MP3 only
get permission and credit the band
publish them first and ask later
questions.explain: Cultural content still belongs to its creators. Permission and credit are ethical and legal duties.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem: An audio tour plays the history of Fort George when the user arrives there. This links users to...
questions.explain: Location-based stories connect users to local history at the place it happened.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem: St. Kitts start-up NevisCode builds a hurricane-preparedness app for its own island. Two years later it licenses the same app, rebranded, to disaster offices in Dominica and Grenada. Which economic benefit does this BEST illustrate?

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem:
The Turks and Caicos charity Rebuild Together has asked Island Pulse Media to plan a disaster preparedness app. You are advising Jerome. Make the best decisions.

The charity wants the app to load all its content live from the Internet so information is always fresh. What do you advise first?
options: Agree: live content is always best, and everyone has Internet.
Store the essential content (checklists, shelters, emergency numbers) on the phone so it works offline, and update it when there is a connection.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem: Good. Next, who should the content be written for?
options: Residents and visitors in English, Spanish, Dutch and French, in plain language, with official information from the Office of Disaster Management.
English only, using technical meteorological terms to sound professional.

questions.topic: Benefits of developing local mobile applications
questions.stem: The charity asks how to keep the app running for years, since it has only one grant. What do you suggest?
options: Spend the whole grant on launch and worry about updates later.
Plan sustainability: partner with the government and telecoms providers, seek sponsorship and add a donation feature for the diaspora.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
Jerome, the mobile developer at Island Pulse Media, is reviewing the first screen of the LoloGo food-ordering app. Choose the best decision each time.

The "Add to order" button is 28 by 28 dp. Jerome should...
options: leave it; users can zoom in
make the text inside it smaller
increase it to at least 48 by 48 dp
questions.explain: Material Design recommends touch targets of at least 48 by 48 dp so fingers can tap accurately.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem: Two buttons, "Cancel" and "Pay", are touching each other. The risk is...
options: accidental taps on the wrong action
questions.explain: Targets need spacing so users do not hit the wrong one, especially for costly actions like paying.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem: The logo looks blurry on a new high-density phone. The best fix is to...
options: use a vector (SVG) logo or higher-resolution versions
questions.explain: Vector graphics, or images supplied at @2x and @3x, stay sharp on high-density screens.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem: Where should the main "Checkout" button go for comfortable one-handed use?
options: bottom of the screen, in the thumb zone
questions.explain: The lower half of the screen is easiest for the thumb to reach.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem: Users must swipe left on a dish to delete it, but some do not discover it. Jerome should...
options: also provide a visible delete button
questions.explain: Hidden gestures need a visible alternative so every user can complete the task.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
A Grenada nutmeg cooperative wants an app for farmers in the hills around Grenville, where the signal is weak. Sort each design choice.

Is this choice good or poor for users with weak connections and limited data?

Market prices are cached so farmers can see the last update offline.
questions.explain: Caching lets users see useful data even without a signal.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
Is this choice good or poor for users with weak connections and limited data?

Every screen autoplays a high-definition video introduction.
questions.explain: Autoplay HD video wastes data and loads slowly on weak signals.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
Is this choice good or poor for users with weak connections and limited data?

Photos are compressed and resized to the size they display at.
questions.explain: Optimised images load faster and use less data.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
Is this choice good or poor for users with weak connections and limited data?

Forms are saved on the phone and sent when a signal returns.
questions.explain: This is offline-first: no work is lost when the connection drops.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
Is this choice good or poor for users with weak connections and limited data?

The app shows a blank white screen when offline.
questions.explain: Users need clear feedback, not a blank screen, when there is no connection.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
Is this choice good or poor for users with weak connections and limited data?

A "Wi-Fi only" setting for downloading training videos.
questions.explain: Letting users control data use protects their prepaid data.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
Is this choice good or poor for users with weak connections and limited data?

The app downloads all 300 images at once when it opens.
questions.explain: Lazy loading would load only what the user needs right now.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
Is this choice good or poor for users with weak connections and limited data?

The app is 400 MB because of unused graphics.
questions.explain: Large app size is costly to download and fills limited storage.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem: The Bajan bus app RouteMate asks users to fill in a five-step form to buy a ticket. Testers on real buses in Bridgetown often lose everything they typed when a call comes in or they reach their stop. Which design strategy BEST addresses this portability problem?
options: Require users to stay on the screen until the form is complete.
Increase the resolution of the images on the form.
Save the user's progress automatically so they can resume where they left off, and shorten the form.
Add a long tutorial video before the form.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem:
The Seven Mile Beach Vendors Association wants an app so visitors can order drinks and snacks from their sunbeds. Jerome asks you to make the key UX decisions.

Zara's draft uses a stylish light grey text on a white background. The app will be used outdoors in strong sun. What do you recommend?
options: Switch to high-contrast colours and bold, larger text so the screen is readable in sunlight.
Keep the design; users can turn up their brightness.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem: Visitors include cruise passengers on roaming plans who avoid using mobile data. What do you do?
options: Keep the app very light, with a QR code at each sunbed that opens a small menu page, compressed images and the beach bar's free Wi-Fi.
Require a 250 MB app download with video menus.

questions.topic: Factors that impact the mobile user experience
questions.stem: Testing shows older visitors and some Spanish-speaking guests struggle with the icons. What is your final change?
options: Add text labels to icons, larger touch targets, a language switch (English, Spanish, French, Italian) and labels for screen readers.
Remove all text so the design looks cleaner.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Jerome, the mobile developer at the Island Pulse Media, has a long wish list for the LoloGo app. He has six weeks to launch. Sort each feature.

Is this feature a Must have for the MVP, or can it wait for version 2?

Browse each lolo's menu with prices.
questions.explain: Without a menu, customers cannot order. This is core to the purpose.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Is this feature a Must have for the MVP, or can it wait for version 2?

Place an order for pickup.
questions.explain: Ordering is the main purpose of the app, so it must be in the MVP.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Is this feature a Must have for the MVP, or can it wait for version 2?

A notification when the order is ready.
questions.explain: This delivers the key benefit: no queuing.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Is this feature a Must have for the MVP, or can it wait for version 2?

Loyalty points and badges.
questions.explain: Nice to have, but the app works without it. Add it once the MVP is proven.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Is this feature a Must have for the MVP, or can it wait for version 2?

Augmented reality view of each dish.
questions.explain: Impressive but costly, and not needed to order food.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Is this feature a Must have for the MVP, or can it wait for version 2?

Recipe videos from the cooks.
questions.explain: Adds cultural value but uses data and time. It can come later.
