questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Is this feature a Must have for the MVP, or can it wait for version 2?

Live map tracking of delivery riders.
questions.explain: The MVP is pickup only. Delivery tracking is a later feature.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Is this feature a Must have for the MVP, or can it wait for version 2?

Choose which lolo to order from.
questions.explain: Customers need to pick the vendor before they can order.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Jerome is answering questions from students on a work-experience visit to Island Pulse Media. Choose the best answer.

Which IDE is the official tool for building native Android apps?
questions.explain: Android Studio is Google's official IDE for Android, with the Android SDK and emulator built in.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem: Google's preferred language for new Android apps is...
questions.explain: Kotlin is preferred; Java is still supported. Swift is for Apple platforms.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem: A student has only a Windows laptop. Which tool can she NOT run directly?
questions.explain: Xcode runs only on macOS. Android Studio runs on Windows; App Inventor runs in a browser.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem: A set of tools, libraries, documentation and emulators for building apps for a platform is called...
questions.explain: SDK stands for software development kit.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem: A small team wants ONE codebase for both Android and iOS. They should consider...
options: a cross-platform tool such as Flutter or React Native
questions.explain: Cross-platform tools share most code across both platforms, saving time and cost.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem: Which language is used with SwiftUI in Xcode?
questions.explain: SwiftUI is Apple's interface framework, written in Swift. Dart is used by Flutter.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem: Grenada Spice Farmers Cooperative keeps a Google Sheet listing 60 farms, their spices, contact numbers and opening days. The manager has no coding skills and a very small budget, and wants a simple app that buyers can search within a week. Which tool is MOST suitable?
options: Android Studio with Kotlin, because Kotlin is Google's preferred language.
Xcode with Swift, because native apps perform best.
Glide, because it builds an app directly from a spreadsheet with no coding.
Balsamiq, because it is quick and easy.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
The LoloGo prototype is built. Jerome must decide how to test it before Carnival, the busiest season for the lolos. Advise him.

Jerome has tested LoloGo only on his own new phone over office Wi-Fi. Everything works. What should he do next?
options: Test on several phones, including an older budget Android, on mobile data and in sunlight, and log every bug.
Publish it to Google Play immediately; it works on his phone.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem: The device tests are fixed. Now, how should he check that LoloGo meets the lolo owners' needs?
options: Run user acceptance testing: the owners use the app against their agreed requirements and sign off, with usability sessions with a few customers.
Ask a fellow developer to read the code instead.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem: The owners approve. There are three weeks to Carnival. What is the best final step?
options: Add five new features, such as loyalty points and AR dishes, without further testing.
Run a beta through Google Play internal or closed testing (and TestFlight for iPhone users) with about 30 regular customers, collect feedback, fix the top issues, then launch.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
The Dominica Trails app team kept a diary of their work. Sort each entry by the stage of development it belongs to.

Which stage does this diary entry describe?

We wrote a persona: Andre, 35, hiker from Roseau, uses an older Android phone.
questions.explain: Personas describe target users, part of conceptualisation.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Which stage does this diary entry describe?

We agreed the MVP: trail list, offline maps, emergency contacts.
questions.explain: Defining core features and the MVP is conceptualisation.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Which stage does this diary entry describe?

We sketched five screens on paper with annotations.
questions.explain: Paper sketches are low-fidelity wireframes.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Which stage does this diary entry describe?

We linked the Figma frames so testers could tap through.
questions.explain: Linking frames creates a clickable prototype.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Which stage does this diary entry describe?

We dragged a ListView and a Map component into the App Inventor Designer.
questions.explain: Adding components in App Inventor is building the app.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Which stage does this diary entry describe?

We wrote Kotlin code in Android Studio for the trail list.
questions.explain: Writing code in an IDE is building.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Which stage does this diary entry describe?

The tourism office checked the app against the brief and signed off.
questions.explain: The client confirming requirements is user acceptance testing.

questions.topic: Tools and techniques to create a mobile application
questions.stem:
Which stage does this diary entry describe?

Thirty hikers tried a beta and we fixed the top three issues.
questions.explain: Beta testing followed by fixes is testing and refinement.

questions.stem:
Jerome at the Island Pulse Media is advising four clients across the region. Sort each situation into the distribution model it describes.

Which distribution model is being used?

A Grenada spice tour app is approved by Apple and appears in App Store search results.
questions.explain: Apple reviewed and listed it, so it is distributed through an official app store.

questions.stem:
Which distribution model is being used?

A Barbados hotel emails its housekeeping staff a private app that only company phones can install.
questions.explain: A private app for internal staff, managed by the organisation, is enterprise distribution.

questions.stem:
Which distribution model is being used?

A festival in Trinidad tells visitors to scan a QR code and tap "Add to Home Screen".
questions.explain: Adding a site to the home screen from the browser is how a progressive web app is installed.

questions.stem:
Which distribution model is being used?

A developer posts an APK file on a website and tells users to allow "install unknown apps".
questions.explain: Installing an APK from outside the store is direct download, also called sideloading.

questions.stem:
Which distribution model is being used?

A Barbados food delivery app updates itself automatically every week through Google Play.
questions.explain: Automatic updates handled by Google Play are a feature of store distribution.

questions.stem:
Which distribution model is being used?

Electricity-company field technicians use a meter-reading app pushed to their tablets by the IT department.
questions.explain: An app pushed by IT to staff devices through device management is enterprise distribution.

questions.stem:
Which distribution model is being used?

A Dominica news service works in any phone browser and saves articles for offline reading.
questions.explain: Browser-based access with offline saving describes a web app or PWA.

questions.stem:
Which distribution model is being used?

A beta version of a game is shared as an installation file in a WhatsApp group.
questions.explain: Sharing the installation file directly, outside a store, is direct download.

questions.stem: Grand Anse Taxi Co-op wants its new booking app on members' Android phones quickly. A volunteer suggests posting the APK on a Facebook page so passengers can install it straight away. Which is the STRONGEST reason to distribute through Google Play instead?
options: APK files cannot be installed on Android phones.
Google Play apps are always free, so passengers save money.
Passengers would have to allow "install unknown apps", the file would not be reviewed for malware, and security updates would not arrive automatically.
Facebook does not allow links to be posted.

questions.stem:
Jerome and Keisha at the Island Pulse Media are launching the Hairouna Trails app: a guide to hiking trails, heritage sites and food stops across St. Vincent for residents and cruise visitors. You are the launch manager. Make the best decisions.

The app works, but nobody outside the team has used it. The client wants it in the stores tomorrow. What do you do first?
options: Launch tomorrow; bugs can be fixed after the reviews come in.
Run a two-week closed beta with 30 local hikers and tour guides, and fix what they report.

questions.stem: The beta went well. Now you prepare the store listing. Which listing do you choose?
options: Title "GT App", a long paragraph of history, and the login screen as the first screenshot.
Title "Hairouna Trails: St. Vincent Hikes", keywords such as St. Vincent, hiking, beaches, heritage, and captioned screenshots of the trail map first.
Copy the description of a popular international hiking app word for word.

questions.stem: You have a small budget. The audience is residents plus cruise visitors arriving at the Kingstown cruise berth. How do you promote the launch?
options: Spend the whole budget on one international TV advert.
QR posters at the cruise terminal and tourist office, a press release to local newspapers and radio, two local hiking influencers, and an email to beta sign-ups.

questions.stem: One month later, downloads are good but many users stop opening the app after their first hike. What next?
options: Add new trails monthly, send a friendly weekend notification, prompt for a rating after a completed hike and reply to reviews.
Send five promotional notifications every day.

questions.stem:
Maya and Jerome at the Island Pulse Media face these decisions for clients in Belize and Curaçao. Choose the best answer.

A Belize client wants one product that works on any phone, needs no store approval and updates instantly. Best choice?
questions.explain: A PWA runs in the browser on any device, avoids store review and updates as soon as the site changes.

questions.stem: Many people see the store listing but few install it. Which metric shows this problem?
questions.explain: Conversion rate compares listing visitors with installs. Low conversion points to weak screenshots, icon or description.

questions.stem: Improving an app's title, keywords and screenshots to rank higher in the store is called...
questions.explain: App Store Optimisation works inside the app stores; SEO is for web search engines.

questions.stem: A Curaçao bank wants an app only its staff can install. Which model?
questions.explain: Enterprise distribution keeps a private app within one organisation.

questions.stem: Users can sign up on Google Play so the app installs automatically on launch day. This is...
questions.explain: Pre-registration builds a launch-day audience before the app is released.

questions.stem: Which is an example of "earned" rather than paid media?
options: a newspaper article written after a press release
questions.explain: Earned media is coverage you did not pay for directly, such as news stories and independent reviews.

questions.stem:
Jerome at the Island Pulse Media is reviewing how different apps charge users. Sort each description.

Which commercial model does this describe?

Users pay US$4.99 before they can download a Carnival costume design app.
questions.explain: Payment before download, with everything unlocked, is a paid (premium) app.

questions.stem:
Which commercial model does this describe?

A Caribbean language app is free, but offline lessons and no ads need "Plus".
questions.explain: A free core with a paid upgrade tier is the freemium model.

questions.stem:
Which commercial model does this describe?

A domino game sells packs of 500 coins that can be bought again and again.
questions.explain: Coins are consumable virtual goods bought inside the app: in-app purchases.

questions.stem:
Which commercial model does this describe?

A recipe app sells a one-off "Christmas in Jamaica" content pack.
questions.explain: A content pack bought inside the app is a non-consumable in-app purchase.

questions.stem:
Which commercial model does this describe?

A photo editor is free with basic filters; professional tools are in a paid version.
questions.explain: Basic features free, advanced features paid: freemium.

questions.stem:
Which commercial model does this describe?

A sailing navigation app costs US$9.99 in the store and has no ads or upgrades.
questions.explain: One upfront price with no further charges is a paid app.

questions.stem:
Which commercial model does this describe?

A cricket game lets players unlock a new stadium for US$1.99.
questions.explain: Unlocking a feature inside the app with a single payment is an in-app purchase.

questions.stem: The Caribbean Taxi Tech company built one booking app. It now sells the same app to taxi associations in St. Lucia, Antigua and Dominica, each with its own name, logo and colours, for a setup fee plus a monthly charge. Which model BEST describes this?

Identify the community-supported funding model in each situation.

A Guyanese team raises US$8,000 from 400 backers on a crowdfunding platform before they start coding a farming app.
questions.explain: Many small pledges for a specific future project is crowdfunding.

questions.stem: A foundation gives a Jamaican health-app team money to build a clinic finder, with progress reports required.
questions.explain: Institutional funding for a defined purpose, with conditions and reports, is a grant.

questions.stem: Readers of Wikipedia see a banner asking them to give whatever they can.
questions.explain: Voluntary gifts from users are donations; this is Wikipedia's main funding source.

questions.stem: A telecoms company funds a free hurricane-alert app and its logo appears on the start screen.
questions.explain: Funding in return for recognition is sponsorship.

questions.stem: Signal can avoid collecting users' data for ads mainly because...
options: it charges a high download price
it is funded by donations and grants through a non-profit
questions.explain: Signal's non-profit, donation-and-grant model removes the commercial incentive to track users.

questions.stem:
Zara at the Island Pulse Media is advising Bim Moves, a new app listing events, beach parties, live music and Crop Over activities across Barbados. The audience is local young people aged 16 to 30 and visitors. Help choose a revenue model.

The founders want to charge US$6.99 to download the app so they make money from day one. What do you advise?
options: Agree: a high price shows quality.
Make the core listings free so many people download it; a price would stop most young locals from trying it.

questions.stem: The app will be free. How should it earn money?
options: Collect and sell users' location history to marketing companies.
Charge event organisers and bars a fee for featured listings, plus a small banner slot sold to local businesses.
Show a full-screen interstitial ad every time a user opens an event.

questions.stem: Some regular users ask for extra features: early ticket alerts and no ads. What do you add?
options: Remove all free features and force everyone onto a subscription.
An optional "Bim Moves Plus" at a low monthly price, with clear terms and easy cancellation.

questions.stem: Many young users do not have credit cards. How do you handle payments for Plus?
options: Support store gift cards and check carrier billing with local operators, and price it for the local market.
Accept international credit cards only; that is the users' problem.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Jerome at the Island Pulse Media is reviewing client requests from around the region. Identify the trend behind each one.

A St. Kitts hotel wants guests' phones to unlock room doors and control the air conditioning.
questions.explain: Connected locks and air-conditioning units controlled by phone are IoT devices.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: A traffic camera at the Demerara Harbour Bridge processes video locally and sends only alerts, not full footage.
questions.explain: Processing data near its source and sending only results is edge computing.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: A bank app adds a chatbot that answers customer questions in plain language at any hour.
questions.explain: A conversational assistant is AI built into the app.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: A network upgrade gives near-instant response for cloud gaming and supports thousands of sensors.
questions.explain: Very low latency and capacity for many devices are the key features of 5G.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Customers at a Georgetown café pay by tapping their phone on the card reader.
questions.explain: Tap-to-pay with a phone wallet is a mobile payment.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Some trends are about new hardware; others change how apps are built or delivered; others are about experiences. Sort each example.

What kind of trend is this?

A phone that unfolds into a small tablet.
options: How apps are built or delivered
questions.explain: Foldables are a hardware trend that forces apps to adapt their layouts.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
What kind of trend is this?

A smartwatch that tracks heart rate during a Carnival road march.
options: How apps are built or delivered
questions.explain: Wearables are new devices with their own app requirements.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
What kind of trend is this?

A youth group in Curaçao builds its event app in Thunkable with no code.
options: How apps are built or delivered
questions.explain: Low-code/no-code changes how apps are built and who can build them.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
What kind of trend is this?

A Dominica news site can be added to the home screen and read offline.
options: How apps are built or delivered
questions.explain: A PWA is a delivery method: web technology that behaves like an app.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
What kind of trend is this?

A camera view shows labels floating over each shop on Frederick Street in Port of Spain.
options: How apps are built or delivered
questions.explain: Digital labels laid over the live camera view are augmented reality.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
What kind of trend is this?

A headset lets a buyer in Toronto walk through a villa in Ocho Rios.
options: How apps are built or delivered
questions.explain: A fully virtual environment through a headset is virtual reality.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
What kind of trend is this?

Smart earbuds translate a conversation in real time.
options: How apps are built or delivered
questions.explain: Wearable devices increasingly carry AI features, but the trend here is the new hardware.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
What kind of trend is this?

A Bahamas agency uses FlutterFlow to build an app for both Android and iOS from one design.
options: How apps are built or delivered
questions.explain: Visual cross-platform builders are part of the low-code trend.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Which description BEST fits the definition of a super app?
options: An app that runs extremely fast on 5G networks.
One app in which users chat, pay bills, order food, book rides and use mini-programs from other businesses.
A very popular app with millions of downloads, such as a hit game.
A single-purpose app built with a no-code tool.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem:
Zara and Maya at the Island Pulse Media are advising a government working group in Sint Maarten that wants a mobile app for public services: bill payments, permit applications and appointment booking. Make the best decisions.

A minister wants the app to require the newest phones so it can use the latest AR and AI features. What do you advise?
options: Agree: the newest technology will make the island look modern.
First research residents' devices, data costs and digital skills; the app must serve everyone, including older residents.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Research shows most residents use mid-range Android phones and prepaid data. How should the service be delivered?
options: A large app that streams high-definition video guides and only works on 5G.
A light store app plus a PWA version, both working on 4G and saving forms offline until a connection returns.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: The app will handle ID numbers and payments, and some users live on the French side or are EU citizens. What do you build in?
options: Collect as much data as possible now; security can be added later.
Privacy by design: encryption, 2FA, data minimisation, a clear privacy policy and compliance with local law and GDPR.

questions.topic: Factors influencing trends in the mobile ecosystem
questions.stem: Before launch, how do you check you are building on real trends, not hype?
options: Copy whatever the most-downloaded app in the US store is doing.
Use GSMA Intelligence and ITU data for regional mobile use, Google Trends for local search interest, and survey residents.
